google_compute_autoscaler.autoscaling_policy.custom_metric_utiliza: Filter string to identify a specific time series for the custom metric. Used to select which resource's metric data to scale on, often with conditions like resource.type or metric labels.
The identifier (name) of the Cloud Monitoring metric to use for autoscaling. For example, compute.googleapis.com/instance/network/received_bytes_count.
The target value of the custom metric that a single instance should handle. This is used as a per-instance scaling target to determine the number of instances needed.
The target value of the custom metric that the autoscaler maintains. The autoscaler adjusts the number of instances to keep the metric value close to this target.
Specifies whether the utilization target is a gauge, delta per second, or delta per minute. Allowed values are DELTA_PER_MINUTE, DELTA_PER_SECOND, and GAUGE.
google_compute_autoscaler.autoscaling_policy.scaling_schedules.dis: Whether the scaling schedule is disabled. When set to true, the schedule is inactive and its scaling actions are not applied, even if the scheduled time occurs.
google_compute_autoscaler.autoscaling_policy.scaling_schedules.dur: The duration of the scaling schedule in seconds. Must be between 1 and 86400 seconds inclusive.
google_compute_autoscaler.autoscaling_policy.scaling_schedules.min: The minimum number of replicas that must be running for the autoscaler to apply this scaling schedule. If the current number of replicas is below this value, the autoscaler first scales to it.
google_compute_autoscaler.autoscaling_policy.scaling_schedules.sch: The cron-style schedule expression that determines when the scaling schedule is active. It uses standard cron syntax (e.g., '0 9 * * *' for daily at 9 AM).
google_compute_autoscaler.autoscaling_policy.scaling_schedules.tim: The time zone to use when interpreting the schedule. Must be a time zone name from the IANA time zone database (e.g., 'America/New_York').
google_compute_autoscaler.scaling_schedule_status.last_start_time: The timestamp of the most recent start of this scaling schedule.
google_compute_autoscaler.scaling_schedule_status.state: The state of the scaling schedule, which can be ACTIVE, OBSOLETE, or DELETED.
google_compute_autoscaler.status_details.message: The human-readable status message that provides additional details about the autoscaler's current state.
google_compute_autoscaler.status_details.type: The type of the autoscaler status detail, indicating a specific scaling condition or issue. Valid values include: ALL_INSTANCES_UNHEALTHY, BACKEND_SERVICE_DOES_NOT_EXIST, CAPPED_AT_MAX_NUM_REPLICAS, CUSTOM_METRIC_DATA_POINTS_TOO_SPARSE, CUSTOM_METRIC_INVALID, MIN_EQUALS_MAX, MISSING_CUSTOM_METRIC_DATA_POINTS, MISSING_LOAD_BALANCING_DATA_POINTS, MODE_OFF, MODE_ONLY_SCALE_OUT, MODE_ONLY_UP, MORE_THAN_ONE_BACKEND_SERVICE, NOT_ENOUGH_QUOTA_AVAILABLE, REGION_RESOURCE_STOCKOUT, SCALING_TARGET_DOES_NOT_EXIST, SCHEDULED_INSTANCES_GREATER_THAN_AUTOSCALER_MAX, SCHEDULED_INSTANCES_LESS_THAN_AUTOSCALER_MIN, UNKNOWN, UNSUPPORTED_MAX_RATE_LOAD_BALANCING_CONFIGURATION, ZONE_RESOURCE_STOCKOUT.

google_compute_backend_bucket.cdn_policy.bypass_cache_on_request_heade: The name of the request header to bypass the cache for.
google_compute_backend_bucket.cdn_policy.negative_caching_policy.code: The HTTP status code that this negative caching policy applies to.
google_compute_backend_bucket.cdn_policy.negative_caching_policy.ttl: Time-to-live in seconds for the cached response for the specified HTTP status code. This defines how long the negative cache entry persists.
google_compute_backend_bucket.used_by.reference: The reference URL of the resource that uses this backend bucket, such as a URL map.

google_compute_backend_service.backends.balancing_mode: Specifies the balancing mode for this backend, which determines how traffic is distributed among instances. Valid values are CONNECTION (based on connection count), UTILIZATION (based on CPU utilization), RATE (based on requests per second), IN_FLIGHT (based on in-flight requests), and CUSTOM_METRICS (based on custom metrics).
google_compute_backend_service.backends.capacity_scaler: The capacity scaler for this backend, a floating-point value between 0 and 1. It determines the fraction of traffic that this backend will receive, with 1 (default) meaning full capacity.
google_compute_backend_service.backends.custom_metrics.max_utilization: The maximum ratio of the custom metric's actual value to its target value. If a backend's metric exceeds this ratio, the load balancer considers it over-utilized and stops sending it new requests.
google_compute_backend_service.backends.custom_metrics.name: The name of the custom metric used for load balancing this backend.
google_compute_backend_service.backends.failover: If true, this backend is used only as a failover backend, meaning it receives traffic only when all other backends in the service are unhealthy.
google_compute_backend_service.backends.group: The fully-qualified URL of a zonal or regional instance group, network endpoint group (NEG), or other backend resource that serves traffic for this backend service. This is required for each backend.
google_compute_backend_service.backends.max_connections: Maximum number of connections to the backend. This applies when the balancing mode is CONNECTION and is used to determine backend capacity.
google_compute_backend_service.backends.max_connections_per_endpoint: The maximum number of simultaneous connections allowed per backend endpoint (e.g., per instance in an instance group). This field is used when the backend's balancing mode is 'CONNECTION' and the protocol is TCP or UDP; a value of 0 indicates no limit.
google_compute_backend_service.backends.max_in_flight_requests: The maximum number of simultaneous in-flight requests allowed for this backend. If not set, the default is 1024.
google_compute_backend_service.backends.max_in_flight_requests_per_endp: The maximum number of simultaneous (in-flight) requests allowed per backend endpoint. This setting can be used to protect endpoints from being overwhelmed by concurrent requests.
google_compute_backend_service.backends.max_in_flight_requests_per_inst: The maximum number of outstanding (in-flight) requests that a single backend instance can receive. This setting limits the number of simultaneous requests to an instance, helping to prevent overload in the backend service.
google_compute_backend_service.backends.max_rate: The maximum requests per second (RPS) that the backend can handle. Used only when the backend's balancing mode is RATE.
google_compute_backend_service.backends.max_rate_per_endpoint: The maximum number of requests per second (RPS) that each endpoint (instance) in this backend is allowed to handle. This setting is used for capacity-based load balancing and applies only when the backend service's load balancing protocol supports rate-based distribution.
google_compute_backend_service.backends.max_rate_per_instance: The maximum rate (in requests per second) that each instance in the backend instance group is allowed to receive. This setting is used when the balancing mode is RATE.
google_compute_backend_service.backends.max_utilization: The maximum utilization threshold for the backend, expressed as a fraction. This is used when the backend's balancing mode is set to UTILIZATION, and the backend is considered at capacity when its utilization reaches this value.
google_compute_backend_service.backends.orchestration_info.resource_uri: The URI of the resource being orchestrated by this backend, such as an Instance Group Manager.
google_compute_backend_service.backends.preference: Specifies the preference of this backend within the backend service. This field is used by load balancing policies that differentiate between preferred and default backends. Allowed values are DEFAULT, PREFERENCE_UNSPECIFIED, and PREFERRED.
google_compute_backend_service.backends.traffic_duration: Specifies whether the backend is expected to handle long-lived or short-lived traffic. Allowed values are LONG, SHORT, and TRAFFIC_DURATION_UNSPECIFIED.
google_compute_backend_service.cdn_policy.bypass_cache_on_request_heade: The name of the request header that, when present in the request, triggers bypassing the cache. The header name must be a valid HTTP header name.
google_compute_backend_service.cdn_policy.negative_caching_policy.code: HTTP status code for which negative caching is applied (e.g., 404, 405, 500).
google_compute_backend_service.cdn_policy.negative_caching_policy.ttl: The TTL (in seconds) for which to cache responses with the corresponding status code in the negative caching policy.
google_compute_backend_service.ha_policy: The high availability (HA) policy for the backend service, which can include an HA mode (e.g., ACTIVE or INACTIVE) controlling cross-region failover behavior.
google_compute_backend_service.ha_policy.leader.network_endpoint: The network endpoint to be designated as the leader in the high-availability policy. This object identifies the specific endpoint that holds the leader role.
google_compute_backend_service.locality_lb_policies.custom_policy: Configuration for a custom load balancing policy applied to a specific locality. This object defines a user-defined policy where a built-in policy is not used.
google_compute_backend_service.locality_lb_policies.custom_policy.data: The data to be passed to the custom policy, as a string.
google_compute_backend_service.locality_lb_policies.policy: Configuration for the locality load balancing policy. This object defines the standard load balancing algorithm and its optional settings within a locality LB policy.
google_compute_backend_service.locality_lb_policies.policy.name: The name of the load balancing policy. Must be one of: INVALID_LB_POLICY, LEAST_REQUEST, MAGLEV, ORIGINAL_DESTINATION, RANDOM, RING_HASH, ROUND_ROBIN, WEIGHTED_GCP_RENDEZVOUS, WEIGHTED_MAGLEV, WEIGHTED_ROUND_ROBIN.
The name of the HTTP request header to include in the backend service logs.
google_compute_backend_service.log_config.logging_http_response_headers: The name of an HTTP response header to include in the logs for the backend service.
google_compute_backend_service.network_pass_through_lb_traffic_policy: The network pass-through load balancer traffic policy for this backend service. This field is output-only and populated by the API with the effective traffic handling configuration for pass-through load balancers.
google_compute_backend_service.network_pass_through_lb_traffic_policy.z: Configures zonal affinity for the load balancer, which influences whether traffic is steered to backends in the same zone as the client.
google_compute_backend_service.subsetting.policy: The subsetting policy for this backend service. Allowed values are `CONSISTENT_HASH_SUBSETTING` and `NONE`.
google_compute_backend_service.tls_settings: Settings for authenticating the backend service with a client certificate.
google_compute_backend_service.tls_settings.subject_alt_names.dns_name: The DNS name to be included in the subject alternative names for TLS validation. This is used when the backend service’s TLS settings specify a DNS SAN.
google_compute_backend_service.tls_settings.subject_alt_names.uniform_r: A uniform resource identifier (URI) to be used as a subject alternative name for the backend service's TLS certificate.
google_compute_backend_service.used_by.reference: The URL of the resource that references (uses) this backend service.

google_compute_disk.async_primary_disk: The primary disk in an asynchronous replication pairing. When this disk is configured as a secondary disk, this computed attribute contains the disk name and zone of the primary disk.
google_compute_disk.async_secondary_disks.async_replication_: The disk to be used as the secondary disk for asynchronous replication. This nested object defines the target disk that receives replicated data from the primary disk.
The resource policy that defines the consistency group for this disk's asynchronous replication. Provide the self-link or full URL of the policy.
The ID of the consistency group policy used for this disk's asynchronous replication. A consistency group policy ensures that multiple disks in a group are replicated to the same point in time.
The URL of the secondary disk used for asynchronous replication.
The ID of the disk that acts as the secondary disk for asynchronous replication.
google_compute_disk.disk_encryption_key: Encryption key configuration for the disk. This block can be used to specify a customer-supplied raw key or a customer-managed Cloud KMS key at creation time, and it is also populated with computed metadata (such as a fingerprint) for the key that was actually used.
google_compute_disk.guest_os_features.type: The type of guest OS feature to enable on the disk. Valid values are: BARE_METAL_LINUX_COMPATIBLE, CCA_CAPABLE, FEATURE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED, GVNIC, IDPF, MULTI_IP_SUBNET, SECURE_BOOT, SEV_CAPABLE, SEV_LIVE_MIGRATABLE, SEV_LIVE_MIGRATABLE_V2, SEV_SNP_CAPABLE, SNP_SVSM_CAPABLE, TDX_CAPABLE, UEFI_COMPATIBLE, VIRTIO_SCSI_MULTIQUEUE, and WINDOWS.
google_compute_disk.resource_status: An output-only object that reports the physical storage zones of the disk, including the primary zone and, for regional disks, the replica zone.
google_compute_disk.resource_status.async_primary_disk: The primary disk that is part of the async replication relationship. This field is present on secondary disks and provides the URL and state of the primary disk.
google_compute_disk.resource_status.async_primary_disk.state: The lifecycle state of the asynchronous primary disk replication, such as CREATED, STARTING, ACTIVE, STOPPING, STOPPED, or STATE_UNSPECIFIED.
google_compute_disk.source_image_encryption_key: Customer-supplied encryption key used to decrypt the source image when creating the disk. This field is output-only and is populated by the API with the key details used for the source image.
google_compute_disk.source_snapshot_encryption_key: The customer-supplied encryption key of the source snapshot used to create this disk. This output-only field exposes details about the key (e.g., raw key or KMS key reference) that was used to decrypt the source snapshot.

google_compute_external_vpn_gateway.interfaces.id: The numeric identifier for this interface, unique within the external VPN gateway, used to associate it with VPN tunnels.
google_compute_external_vpn_gateway.interfaces.ip_address: The public IPv4 address for this interface of the external VPN gateway.
google_compute_external_vpn_gateway.interfaces.ipv6_address: The IPv6 address of the external VPN gateway interface. This is the peer address used for establishing VPN tunnels over IPv6.

google_compute_firewall.allowed.ipprotocol: The IP protocol to which this rule applies. Valid values are 'tcp', 'udp', 'icmp', 'esp', 'ah', 'sctp', or 'all'.
google_compute_firewall.allowed.ports: An optional list of ports or port ranges (e.g., '80' or '8000-9000') to which this rule applies. Only valid for TCP and UDP protocols; if omitted, the rule applies to all ports.
google_compute_firewall.denied.ipprotocol: The IP protocol to which this firewall rule applies. Can be one of 'tcp', 'udp', 'icmp', 'esp', 'ah', 'sctp', or 'all'.
google_compute_firewall.denied.ports: A list of destination ports to deny for the specified protocol. Ports can be individual numbers or ranges (e.g., '80' or '1000-2000'). If not specified, all ports for the protocol are denied.

google_compute_firewall_policie.associations.attachment_target: The full resource name of the folder or organization that this firewall policy is associated with.
google_compute_firewall_policie.associations.firewall_policy_id: The unique ID of the firewall policy to associate with the target.
google_compute_firewall_policie.associations.short_name: A short, unique identifier for the association within the firewall policy, used for display and management purposes.
google_compute_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.description: An optional user-defined description for this packet mirroring rule within the firewall policy.
google_compute_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.direction: Specifies the direction of traffic to which this packet mirroring rule applies. Valid values are 'INGRESS' and 'EGRESS'.
google_compute_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.disabled: Whether this packet mirroring rule is disabled. When set to true, the rule is not enforced.
google_compute_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.match: The match criteria that specify which network traffic is subject to this packet mirroring rule.
google_compute_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.match.dest_addres: List of destination address groups that define the destination IP addresses to match in the packet mirroring rule.
google_compute_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.match.dest_fqdns: A list of destination fully qualified domain names (FQDNs) used by the match criteria for packet mirroring rules. Traffic mirrored by the rule must be destined to one of the specified FQDNs.
google_compute_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.match.dest_ip_ran: A list of destination IP address ranges in CIDR format. Traffic whose destination IP falls within any of these ranges matches this packet mirroring rule.
google_compute_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.match.dest_networ: Specifies the network context of the destination traffic that this rule matches. Valid values are INTERNET, INTRA_VPC, NON_INTERNET, UNSPECIFIED, and VPC_NETWORKS.
The destination network type to match for packet mirroring. The allowed values are: INTERNET, INTRA_VPC, NON_INTERNET, UNSPECIFIED, and VPC_NETWORKS.
google_compute_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.match.dest_region: A list of destination region codes (for example, 'us-central1') that the packet mirroring rule matches on. The rule applies only to packets with a destination in one of the specified regions.
google_compute_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.match.dest_threat: A list of threat intelligence feeds to match against the destination IP address of the traffic.
google_compute_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.match.layer4_conf: A list of layer 4 configurations used to match packets based on protocol and port. Each configuration specifies the IP protocol (such as TCP, UDP, ICMP) and an optional list of destination ports, allowing the firewall policy rule to apply to specific traffic types.
The IP protocol to match. Accepts protocol names such as tcp, udp, icmp, esp, ah, ipip, sctp, a numeric IP protocol number, or 'all' to match any protocol.
Specifies the list of destination port numbers or ranges to match for this layer4 configuration. Each entry is a string, e.g., '80' or '8000-9000'. If omitted, the rule matches all ports.
google_compute_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.match.src_address: A list of full resource URLs to network address groups used as the source address match. Packets from sources that belong to these groups are mirrored.
google_compute_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.match.src_fqdns: The list of fully qualified domain names (FQDNs) that the rule uses as the source match condition. Traffic originating from these FQDNs matches the rule.
google_compute_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.match.src_ip_rang: A list of source IP address ranges in CIDR notation that the packet mirroring rule matches on. If specified, the rule only applies to traffic originating from these ranges.
google_compute_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.match.src_network: Specifies the source network context for matching traffic. Allowed values are: INTERNET, INTRA_VPC, NON_INTERNET, UNSPECIFIED, and VPC_NETWORKS.
The type of source network that the rule matches. Valid values are INTERNET, INTRA_VPC, NON_INTERNET, UNSPECIFIED, and VPC_NETWORKS.
List of source CIDR networks to match. Traffic from any of these source IP ranges will match the rule and be mirrored. Each entry must be a valid CIDR block, for example: '10.0.0.0/8'.
google_compute_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.match.src_region_: Specifies the list of source region codes (e.g., 'us-central1', 'europe-west1') from which traffic must originate for the rule to apply.
google_compute_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.match.src_secure_: List of secure tags used to match source resources for this packet mirroring rule. Traffic originating from any resource carrying one of these tags will be mirrored.
The name of the Secure Tag value to match in the source of the packet. This is the full resource name, such as `tagValues/123456789`.
The state of the secure tag, indicating whether it is currently effective or ineffective. Allowed values are 'EFFECTIVE' and 'INEFFECTIVE'.
google_compute_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.match.src_threat_: A list of threat intelligence sources used to match the source IP address of traffic. If specified, the rule applies only to traffic whose source IP is identified by one of the listed threat intelligence feeds.
google_compute_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.priority: The priority of this packet mirroring rule. Lower values are evaluated first. Must be an integer between 0 and 65535.
google_compute_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.rule_name: The name of the packet mirroring rule. This is a user-provided name used to identify the rule in the firewall policy.
google_compute_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.target_forwarding: List of forwarding rule URLs that are the target of the packet mirroring rule. Traffic sent to these forwarding rules is mirrored to the collector.
google_compute_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.target_secure_tag: A list of secure tags that identify the target instances whose traffic will be mirrored by this packet mirroring rule.
The name of the secure tag. Secure tags are used to identify which instances or resources this packet mirroring rule applies to.
The state of the secure tag, indicating whether the tag is currently effective or ineffective. Valid values are EFFECTIVE and INEFFECTIVE.
google_compute_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.target_service_ac: A list of service accounts that the rule targets. Instances with any of these service accounts will have their traffic affected by this packet mirroring rule. If not specified, the rule applies to all instances.
google_compute_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.target_type: The type of target to which the packet mirroring rule applies. Valid values are INSTANCES and INTERNAL_MANAGED_LB.
google_compute_firewall_policie.rules.direction: The direction in which the rule applies. Possible values are EGRESS for outbound traffic and INGRESS for inbound traffic.
google_compute_firewall_policie.rules.disabled: Whether this rule is disabled. When set to true, the rule is not enforced. Defaults to false.
google_compute_firewall_policie.rules.enable_logging: Whether to enable logging for this firewall policy rule. When set to true, traffic matching the rule is logged to Cloud Logging.
google_compute_firewall_policie.rules.match: The match block specifies the criteria that determine which traffic the firewall policy rule applies to, including source and destination IP ranges, protocols, and ports.
google_compute_firewall_policie.rules.match.dest_address_groups: The list of destination address groups that the rule matches. Address groups are named collections of IP addresses, and this field specifies which groups the rule’s destination addresses must belong to.
google_compute_firewall_policie.rules.match.dest_fqdns: A list of destination fully qualified domain names (FQDNs) to match for this firewall policy rule. Traffic destined to any of these FQDNs is evaluated against the rule's action. This field is available only for hierarchical firewall policy rules (e.g., organization or folder firewall policies), not for standard VPC firewall rules.
google_compute_firewall_policie.rules.match.dest_ip_ranges: A list of destination IP ranges (in CIDR format) to which this firewall policy rule applies.
google_compute_firewall_policie.rules.match.dest_network_context: Specifies the destination network context for the firewall rule match. Valid values are INTERNET, INTRA_VPC, NON_INTERNET, UNSPECIFIED, and VPC_NETWORKS.
google_compute_firewall_policie.rules.match.dest_network_type: The type of destination network for the firewall policy rule. Allowed values are: INTERNET, INTRA_VPC, NON_INTERNET, UNSPECIFIED, and VPC_NETWORKS. This field is used in the match condition to specify the network type of the destination.
google_compute_firewall_policie.rules.match.dest_region_codes: The list of destination region codes (e.g., 'us-central1') that the rule matches. If set, the rule applies only to traffic destined for the specified GCP regions.
google_compute_firewall_policie.rules.match.dest_threat_intelligences: A list of threat intelligence types used to match traffic based on the destination IP's known threat category.
google_compute_firewall_policie.rules.match.layer4_configs: List of layer 4 configurations used to match traffic by IP protocol and port(s). Each object specifies an IP protocol and an optional list of ports.
google_compute_firewall_policie.rules.match.layer4_configs.ip_protocol: The IP protocol to match for this layer-4 config. Supported values include tcp, udp, icmp, esp, ah, ipip, or a custom protocol number.
google_compute_firewall_policie.rules.match.layer4_configs.ports: An optional list of destination ports or port ranges (e.g., '80' or '8000-8080') to which this layer4 config applies. This field is only applicable when the protocol is TCP or UDP; if not specified, the rule applies to all ports.
google_compute_firewall_policie.rules.match.src_address_groups: A list of source address groups (as URLs or names) that the source IP of the packet must belong to for the rule to match.
google_compute_firewall_policie.rules.match.src_fqdns: A list of source fully qualified domain names (FQDNs) that this firewall policy rule matches.
google_compute_firewall_policie.rules.match.src_ip_ranges: A list of source IP address ranges in CIDR notation. The firewall rule matches traffic originating from any of the specified IP ranges.
google_compute_firewall_policie.rules.match.src_network_context: Specifies the network context of the source of traffic to match. Allowed values are INTERNET (traffic from the internet), INTRA_VPC (traffic within the same VPC), NON_INTERNET (traffic not from the internet), UNSPECIFIED (no context specified), and VPC_NETWORKS (traffic from other VPC networks).
google_compute_firewall_policie.rules.match.src_network_type: The source network type used for the firewall policy rule's match condition. Valid values are: INTERNET, INTRA_VPC, NON_INTERNET, UNSPECIFIED, and VPC_NETWORKS.
google_compute_firewall_policie.rules.match.src_networks: A list of source networks (by name or URL) that the rule matches. Traffic originating from any of these networks is considered a match.
google_compute_firewall_policie.rules.match.src_region_codes: A list of source region codes (e.g., 'us-central1') for the firewall policy rule to match. Traffic originating from any of the specified source regions will match the rule; if left empty, the rule matches all source regions.
google_compute_firewall_policie.rules.match.src_secure_tags: List of secure tags that the source of the traffic must match for the rule to apply. Each object requires a `name` (the secure tag name) and optionally a `scope` (the scope of the tag, e.g., 'global' or a folder ID).
google_compute_firewall_policie.rules.match.src_secure_tags.name: The name of the secure tag to match for the source of the traffic.
google_compute_firewall_policie.rules.match.src_secure_tags.state: State of the secure tag, indicating whether it is effective (EFFECTIVE) or ineffective (INEFFECTIVE) for the firewall rule's source tag matching.
google_compute_firewall_policie.rules.match.src_threat_intelligences: Threat intelligence sources to match against the source IP address. This can include lists such as known malicious IPs, public cloud ranges, scanners, or proxies.
google_compute_firewall_policie.rules.priority: Priority for this firewall policy rule, determining evaluation order; lower numbers have higher precedence and are evaluated first.
google_compute_firewall_policie.rules.rule_name: An optional name for the rule. This field is not a unique identifier.
google_compute_firewall_policie.rules.rule_tuple_count: The number of tuples in the firewall policy rule, representing the combinations of source ranges, destination ranges, and port ranges. This is a computed value returned by the API.
google_compute_firewall_policie.rules.target_forwarding_rules: A list of target forwarding rule URLs that this firewall policy rule applies to. If unspecified, the rule applies to all forwarding rules in the policy's network.
google_compute_firewall_policie.rules.target_resources: A list of network resource URLs to which this firewall policy rule applies.
google_compute_firewall_policie.rules.target_secure_tags: A list of secure tags that determine which resources the firewall policy rule applies to. The rule targets resources that have any of the specified secure tags.
google_compute_firewall_policie.rules.target_secure_tags.state: The state of the secure tag, indicating whether it is currently in effect (EFFECTIVE) or not (INEFFECTIVE) for the firewall policy rule's target.
google_compute_firewall_policie.rules.target_service_accounts: A list of service account email addresses that the firewall rule applies to. If specified, the rule applies only to instances whose service account matches one of these accounts.
google_compute_firewall_policie.rules.target_type: Specifies the type of target that the firewall policy rule applies to. Allowed values are `INSTANCES` and `INTERNAL_MANAGED_LB`.
google_compute_firewall_policie.rules.tls_inspect: If true, this rule is used for TLS inspection. When enabled, the rule's action must be either 'apply' or 'deny'.

google_compute_forwarding_rule.attached_extensions.reference: The self-link or complete URL of the extension resource attached to this forwarding rule.
google_compute_forwarding_rule.metadata_filters.filter_labels: The list of label-value pairs to match against for the forwarding rule's metadata filter.
google_compute_forwarding_rule.metadata_filters.filter_labels.name: The name of the metadata filter label. This is the key of the label.
google_compute_forwarding_rule.metadata_filters.filter_labels.value: The value of the metadata filter label. This is the value part of a key-value pair used to match incoming metadata traffic for the forwarding rule.
google_compute_forwarding_rule.metadata_filters.filter_match_criteria: Specifies how the metadata filter labels are matched against traffic. Valid values are MATCH_ALL (require all labels to match), MATCH_ANY (allow any one label to match), and NOT_SET (no specific matching criteria).
google_compute_forwarding_rule.psc_connection_status: The status of the Private Service Connect (PSC) connection associated with this forwarding rule. Possible values are: ACCEPTED, CLOSED, NEEDS_ATTENTION, PENDING, REJECTED, and STATUS_UNSPECIFIED.
google_compute_forwarding_rule.service_directory_registrations.namespac: The Service Directory namespace where the forwarding rule will be registered as a service.
google_compute_forwarding_rule.service_directory_registrations.service: The name of the Service Directory service to register the forwarding rule with. If not specified, a service name of the form `forwarding_rule_<forwarding_rule_name>` is automatically generated.
google_compute_forwarding_rule.service_directory_registrations.service_: The region of the Service Directory service to register. If not specified, it defaults to the region of the forwarding rule.

google_compute_future_reservation.aggregate_reservation.in_use_resources.a: The accelerator-specific configuration for a resource in the aggregate reservation's in-use resources list. It defines the accelerator type and count to be reserved.
The number of accelerators of the specified type that are currently in use by this aggregate reservation.
The type of accelerator (e.g., GPU) associated with the in-use resources in the aggregate future reservation.
google_compute_future_reservation.aggregate_reservation.reserved_resources: The number of accelerators of the specified type to reserve in the future reservation.
The type of accelerator (e.g., `nvidia-tesla-t4`) to reserve for the future reservation.
google_compute_future_reservation.commitment_info: Information about the commitment that this future reservation is associated with. This field is output-only and may be absent if the reservation is not tied to a commitment.
google_compute_future_reservation.confidential_compute_type: The confidential compute type for the future reservation. Possible values are `CONFIDENTIAL_COMPUTE_TYPE_TDX` (Intel Trust Domain Extensions) and `CONFIDENTIAL_COMPUTE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED`.
google_compute_future_reservation.share_settings.project_map.project_id: The ID of the Google Cloud project to share the future reservation with.
google_compute_future_reservation.specific_sku_properties: Output-only object containing the properties of the specific SKU (e.g., machine type, minimum CPU platform) reserved by this future reservation.
google_compute_future_reservation.specific_sku_properties.instance_propert: The number of guest accelerators of the specified type to attach to the instance.

The full or partial URL of the accelerator type resource to attach (e.g., 'projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-t4'). Identifies the GPU model to use for the guest accelerator.
The size of the local SSD in GB. Each local SSD is 375 GB by default.
The interface to use for attaching the local SSD. Valid values are `NVME` and `SCSI`.
google_compute_future_reservation.status.last_known_good_state.future_rese: The ID of a project that is granted access to the future reservation. It appears in the project_map share settings, identifying a specific project that can use the reservation.
Specifies the configuration for a specific SKU future reservation, including details like machine type and the total number of resources to reserve.
The number of accelerator cards of the specified type to attach to the instance.
The type of accelerator (GPU) to attach to the instance, specified as the accelerator type resource name (e.g., nvidia-tesla-t4).
The size of the local SSD disk in gigabytes (GB), expressed as a string.
The interface type for the local SSD. Accepts 'NVME' or 'SCSI'.
The time window for the future reservation, specifying the start and end times during which the reservation is active.
The end time of the time window during which the future reservation is active, in RFC3339 UTC format.
google_compute_future_reservation.time_window: The time window during which the future reservation is active, defining the start and end times for the reserved capacity.
google_compute_future_reservation.time_window.end_time: The end time of the future reservation's time window, in RFC3339 format (e.g., '2024-12-31T23:59:59Z'). The reservation is active from start_time until this end time.

google_compute_global_forwarding_rule.attached_extensions.reference: The URL or full resource name of the attached service attachment (e.g., a Private Service Connect service attachment) to associate with this forwarding rule.
google_compute_global_forwarding_rule.metadata_filters.filter_labels: The list of label name/value pairs used to match incoming requests for the forwarding rule. Each label defines a metadata filter condition that must be satisfied for the rule to apply.
google_compute_global_forwarding_rule.metadata_filters.filter_labels.name: The name (key) of the metadata filter label. This is the label that must match the incoming request metadata.
google_compute_global_forwarding_rule.metadata_filters.filter_labels.value: The value of the metadata filter label. This is used with the associated label name to match incoming request metadata and determine whether the forwarding rule applies.
google_compute_global_forwarding_rule.metadata_filters.filter_match_criteria: Specifies the match criteria for the metadata filter. Allowed values are MATCH_ALL (must match all labels), MATCH_ANY (must match at least one label), and NOT_SET (no filtering applied).
google_compute_global_forwarding_rule.psc_connection_status: The status of the Private Service Connect (PSC) connection for this global forwarding rule. Possible values are: ACCEPTED, CLOSED, NEEDS_ATTENTION, PENDING, REJECTED, and STATUS_UNSPECIFIED.
google_compute_global_forwarding_rule.service_directory_registrations.namespac: The name of the Service Directory namespace in which the forwarding rule's service is registered. This is required for Service Directory integration and must match an existing namespace.
google_compute_global_forwarding_rule.service_directory_registrations.service: The Service Directory service to register with the forwarding rule. Provide the fully qualified service name (e.g., projects/my-project/locations/us-central1/namespaces/my-ns/services/my-service).
google_compute_global_forwarding_rule.service_directory_registrations.service_: The region for the Service Directory registration associated with this global forwarding rule.

google_compute_global_public_delegated_p.public_delegated_sub_prefixs.allocatable: The prefix length (in bits) of the sub-prefixes that can be allocated from this public delegated sub-prefix. This value is an integer representing the CIDR mask length.
google_compute_global_public_delegated_p.public_delegated_sub_prefixs.delegatee_p: The project ID to which this sub-prefix is delegated. The specified project is allowed to use this prefix range.
google_compute_global_public_delegated_p.public_delegated_sub_prefixs.enable_enha: Enables enhanced IPv4 allocation for this public delegated sub-prefix. This feature allows the sub-prefix to be used with Cloud NAT and internal load balancing.
google_compute_global_public_delegated_p.public_delegated_sub_prefixs.ip_cidr_ran: The IP address range of this sub-prefix, in CIDR notation (e.g., '192.0.2.0/24').
google_compute_global_public_delegated_p.public_delegated_sub_prefixs.ipv6_access: The access type for this IPv6 sub-prefix, indicating whether it is used for external (public) traffic or internal (private) traffic. Allowed values: EXTERNAL or INTERNAL.
google_compute_global_public_delegated_p.public_delegated_sub_prefixs.is_address: Whether this sub-prefix is a single IP address (true) or a CIDR prefix (false).
google_compute_global_public_delegated_p.public_delegated_sub_prefixs.mode: The mode of the sub-prefix, specifying the type of resources that can be created from it. Possible values are DELEGATION, EXTERNAL_IPV6_FORWARDING_RULE_CREATION, EXTERNAL_IPV6_SUBNETWORK_CREATION, and INTERNAL_IPV6_SUBNETWORK_CREATION.
google_compute_global_public_delegated_p.public_delegated_sub_prefixs.region: The region where this public delegated sub-prefix is located. The sub-prefix can only be used within this region.
google_compute_global_public_delegated_p.public_delegated_sub_prefixs.status: The status of the public delegated sub-prefix, indicating whether it is currently active or inactive. Valid values are ACTIVE and INACTIVE.

google_compute_global_vm_extension_polic.extension_policies.pinned_version: The specific version of the extension to pin the policy to. When set, the policy always uses this exact version. If unset, the latest available version is used.
google_compute_global_vm_extension_polic.instance_selectors.label_selector: A label selector object used to match instances based on their labels, determining which instances the policy applies to.
google_compute_global_vm_extension_polic.instance_selectors.label_selector.inclus: A map of key-value pairs that an instance's labels must match for the instance to be included in the selection. Instances with all of these labels are selected.
google_compute_global_vm_extension_polic.rollout_operation.rollout_status.current: A map of location names to the current rollout status for each location, indicating the progress of the rollout operation in each geographic region.
The current state of the rollout operation, with possible values STATE_CANCELLED, STATE_COMPLETED, STATE_FAILED, STATE_PAUSED, STATE_PROCESSING, STATE_UNKNOWN, and STATE_UNSPECIFIED.
google_compute_global_vm_extension_polic.rollout_operation.rollout_status.previou: The status details of the previous rollout operation, if one exists. This object is present only when a prior rollout has been performed and contains information about that prior rollout's state.

google_compute_health_check.grpc_health_check: A configuration block for a gRPC health check. It contains the parameters specific to the gRPC health check type within a Google Compute Engine health check.
google_compute_health_check.grpc_tls_health_check: A nested block that configures gRPC health checking over TLS. This is one of the health check types for a Compute Engine health check, used when the gRPC service requires TLS encryption.
google_compute_health_check.http2_health_check: The http2_health_check object contains settings for an HTTP/2 health check, one of the possible health check types in this resource. This field is computed and represents the active configuration when an HTTP/2 health check is used.
google_compute_health_check.http_health_check: The HTTP health check configuration. This field is computed and output-only, so it cannot be set by the user and is populated by the API.
google_compute_health_check.ssl_health_check: The SSL health check configuration for the health check resource. This is an output-only field that provides the settings used for SSL-based health checks.
google_compute_health_check.tcp_health_check: An output-only object that represents the TCP health check configuration applied to the resource, as returned by the Google Compute API.

google_compute_image.guest_os_features.type: Specifies the guest OS feature type for the image. Allowed values are: BARE_METAL_LINUX_COMPATIBLE, CCA_CAPABLE, FEATURE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED, GVNIC, IDPF, MULTI_IP_SUBNET, SECURE_BOOT, SEV_CAPABLE, SEV_LIVE_MIGRATABLE, SEV_LIVE_MIGRATABLE_V2, SEV_SNP_CAPABLE, SNP_SVSM_CAPABLE, TDX_CAPABLE, UEFI_COMPATIBLE, VIRTIO_SCSI_MULTIQUEUE, WINDOWS.
google_compute_image.image_encryption_key: The customer-supplied encryption key that protects the image. This is optional when creating an image and becomes computed (populated by the provider) when the image is sourced from an encrypted disk or image.
google_compute_image.shielded_instance_initial_state.dbs.cont: The base64-encoded content of the database file (e.g., a UEFI secure boot database) to be stored in the shielded instance initial state.
google_compute_image.shielded_instance_initial_state.dbs.file: The file type of the database entry. Must be one of BIN, UNDEFINED, or X509.
google_compute_image.shielded_instance_initial_state.dbxs.con: The base64-encoded content of the DBX (revoked signature database) file used as part of the Shielded VM initial state for integrity monitoring.
google_compute_image.shielded_instance_initial_state.dbxs.fil: The type of the file. Valid values are: BIN (binary), X509 (X.509 certificate), and UNDEFINED (unspecified).
google_compute_image.shielded_instance_initial_state.keks.con: The raw content of the Key Encryption Key (KEK), as specified in the shielded instance initial state.
google_compute_image.shielded_instance_initial_state.keks.fil: The format of the KEK file. Valid values are 'BIN' (binary file) and 'X509' (X.509 certificate). 'UNDEFINED' indicates an unspecified format.
google_compute_image.shielded_instance_initial_state.pk: The Platform Key (PK) for the shielded instance's secure boot, represented as an object containing the base64-encoded key content and its file type.
google_compute_image.source_disk_encryption_key: The customer-supplied encryption key used to encrypt the source disk when the image was created. This field is computed and output-only, providing the key's metadata after the image is created.
google_compute_image.source_image_encryption_key: The customer-supplied encryption key of the source image, used when creating an image from an encrypted source image. This field is output only and is populated when the source image uses a customer-supplied encryption key.
google_compute_image.source_snapshot_encryption_key: The encryption key used to decrypt the source snapshot when creating the image. This is an output-only field computed by the API.

google_compute_instance.disks.architecture: The CPU architecture of the disk. Must be one of: ARCHITECTURE_UNSPECIFIED, ARM64, or X86_64. This specifies whether the disk is compatible with ARM64 or x86_64 instances.
google_compute_instance.disks.auto_delete: If true, the disk will be automatically deleted when the instance is deleted.
google_compute_instance.disks.boot: A boolean flag indicating whether this disk is the boot disk for the instance. Only one disk can be the boot disk.
google_compute_instance.disks.device_name: The device name exposed to the instance for this disk. If not specified, Google Cloud assigns a default device name. This name is used to reference the disk inside the guest OS (e.g., as /dev/sdb).
google_compute_instance.disks.disk_encryption_key: Configuration for a customer-supplied encryption key (CSEK) to encrypt this disk.
google_compute_instance.disks.disk_encryption_key.kms_key_name: The full resource name of the Cloud KMS key used to encrypt the disk, in the format projects/{project}/locations/{location}/keyRings/{keyRing}/cryptoKeys/{key}. This key is a customer-managed encryption key (CMEK) used for disk encryption.
google_compute_instance.disks.disk_encryption_key.kms_key_servic: The service account being used for the encryption request for the given KMS key. If not specified, the instance's default service account is used.
google_compute_instance.disks.disk_encryption_key.raw_key: The customer-supplied encryption key for the disk, provided as a base64-encoded 256-bit key. This is used to encrypt the disk when using customer-supplied encryption keys.
google_compute_instance.disks.disk_encryption_key.rsa_encrypted_: The base64-encoded RSA-encrypted version of the customer-supplied encryption key, encrypted using Google's public RSA key. This is provided as an alternative to the unencrypted raw_key for protecting the key during transmission.
google_compute_instance.disks.disk_encryption_key.sha256: The SHA256 hash of the customer-supplied encryption key (raw_key). This field is computed by Google and used to verify the key.
google_compute_instance.disks.disk_size_gb: The size of the persistent disk in gigabytes (GB). If not set, the disk size is determined by the source image or the disk type's default.
google_compute_instance.disks.force_attach: If true, the disk is attached to this instance even if it is already attached to another instance. Defaults to false.
google_compute_instance.disks.guest_os_features: A list of guest OS features to enable for the disk. Each feature is an object with a `type` field, such as `UEFI_COMPATIBLE`, `SECURE_BOOT`, or `VIRTIO_SCSI_MULTIQUEUE`.
google_compute_instance.disks.guest_os_features.type: Specifies the type of guest OS feature to enable. Valid values include BARE_METAL_LINUX_COMPATIBLE, CCA_CAPABLE, FEATURE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED, GVNIC, IDPF, MULTI_IP_SUBNET, SECURE_BOOT, SEV_CAPABLE, SEV_LIVE_MIGRATABLE, SEV_LIVE_MIGRATABLE_V2, SEV_SNP_CAPABLE, SNP_SVSM_CAPABLE, TDX_CAPABLE, UEFI_COMPATIBLE, VIRTIO_SCSI_MULTIQUEUE, and WINDOWS.
google_compute_instance.disks.index: The zero-based index of the disk in the instance, where index 0 corresponds to the boot disk. This uniquely identifies the disk among all disks attached to the instance.
google_compute_instance.disks.initialize_params: This block is used to initialize a new disk from a source image or snapshot, specifying parameters such as the image, disk size, and disk type.
google_compute_instance.disks.initialize_params.architecture: The CPU architecture for the disk image. Valid values are ARCHITECTURE_UNSPECIFIED, ARM64, and X86_64.
google_compute_instance.disks.initialize_params.description: An optional description for the disk being initialized.
google_compute_instance.disks.initialize_params.disk_size_gb: Specifies the size of the disk in gigabytes. If not set, the default size of the underlying image is used.
google_compute_instance.disks.initialize_params.enable_confident: Enables Confidential Compute for this disk, which encrypts data in use and allows the disk to be used with confidential VM instances.
google_compute_instance.disks.initialize_params.labels: Labels to apply to the boot disk created from this initialize_params block.
google_compute_instance.disks.initialize_params.licenses: A list of license URIs to apply to this disk. This may be used to apply licenses that are not already present on the image.
google_compute_instance.disks.initialize_params.on_update_action: The update action to perform when the disk configuration changes. Supported values: RECREATE_DISK (recreate the disk on any update), RECREATE_DISK_IF_SOURCE_CHANGED (recreate only if the source image/snapshot changes), USE_EXISTING_DISK (keep the existing disk).
google_compute_instance.disks.initialize_params.provisioned_iops: The provisioned IOPS for the disk. This is applicable to disk types that support configurable IOPS, such as Hyperdisk or Extreme persistent disks.
google_compute_instance.disks.initialize_params.provisioned_thro: The provisioned throughput, in MB/s, for the disk. Only applicable to disk types that support provisioned throughput, such as Hyperdisk.
google_compute_instance.disks.initialize_params.replica_zones: The zones for a regional persistent disk. Provide exactly two zones to create a regional disk; if omitted, a zonal disk is created.
google_compute_instance.disks.initialize_params.resource_manager: A map of resource manager tags to apply to the disk. Keys must be in the format tagKeys/{tag_key_id} and values in the format tagValues/{tag_value_id}.
google_compute_instance.disks.initialize_params.resource_policie: A list of self-links to resource policies (such as snapshot schedules) to apply to the disk when it is created.
google_compute_instance.disks.initialize_params.source_image: The source image to use for creating this disk. Can be a fully-qualified image URL, a project/image reference, or an image family name.
google_compute_instance.disks.initialize_params.source_image_enc: Provides the customer-supplied encryption key used to decrypt the source image when creating a disk from an encrypted image. This block is only used if the source image is encrypted with a customer-supplied key.
The customer-managed encryption key (CMEK) name used to encrypt the source image. Required if the source image is encrypted with a CMEK.
The service account being used for the encryption request for the source image. If not specified, the default Compute Engine service account is used.
The raw key material, base64-encoded, used to decrypt the source image. Required if the source image is encrypted with a customer-supplied encryption key.

The base64-encoded RSA-encrypted key used to decrypt the source image. This key must be encrypted with the public key from the image's KMS key or the service account specified in the same encryption key block.
The SHA256 hash of the customer-supplied encryption key used to encrypt the source image.
google_compute_instance.disks.initialize_params.source_snapshot: The source snapshot used to create this disk. The disk will be initialized from the specified snapshot.
google_compute_instance.disks.initialize_params.source_snapshot_: The customer-supplied encryption key used to decrypt the source snapshot, if it was created with a customer-managed encryption key.

The name of the customer-managed encryption key (CMEK) used to encrypt the source snapshot. Must be a full resource name in the format projects/{project}/locations/{location}/keyRings/{keyRing}/cryptoKeys/{key}.
The service account being used for the encryption request for the given KMS key. If absent, the Compute Engine default service account is used.
The raw 256-bit customer-supplied encryption key, base64-encoded, used to decrypt the source snapshot. This key must match the encryption key used to encrypt the snapshot.

The RSA-encrypted (wrapped) customer-supplied encryption key used to decrypt the source snapshot. Provide either `raw_key` or `rsa_encrypted_key`; when using `rsa_encrypted_key`, also supply `kms_key_self_link`.
The SHA256 hash of the customer-supplied encryption key used to decrypt the source snapshot. This is required when the source snapshot is encrypted with a customer-supplied key.
google_compute_instance.disks.initialize_params.storage_pool: The URL of the storage pool in which to create the disk. If not specified, the default storage pool is used.
google_compute_instance.disks.interface: The disk interface type to use for attaching this disk. Must be one of 'SCSI' or 'NVME'.
google_compute_instance.disks.kind: The kind of the disk resource, which is always 'compute#attachedDisk' for disks attached to an instance.
google_compute_instance.disks.licenses: List of license self-links (URLs) to apply to the disk. This is typically used when creating a boot disk from a custom image to specify the operating system licenses that apply, such as 'https://www.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/debian-cloud/global/licenses/debian-10-buster'.
google_compute_instance.disks.mode: The mode in which the disk is attached to the instance, either READ_ONLY or READ_WRITE.
google_compute_instance.disks.saved_state: Specifies whether the disk's data is preserved when the instance is stopped. Use PRESERVED to keep the data, or DISK_SAVED_STATE_UNSPECIFIED for the default behavior.
google_compute_instance.disks.shielded_instance_initial_state: The shielded instance initial state for the disk, specifying the platform key (pk), key exchange key (kek), and database (db) that define the integrity policy for a Shielded VM instance booted from this disk.
google_compute_instance.disks.shielded_instance_initial_state.db: The list of database certificates for the shielded instance initial state. Each object in the list represents a certificate with fields for content and file type.
The base64-encoded contents of the UEFI db (database) file for the shielded instance's initial state.
The file type of the database file. Valid values are BIN, UNDEFINED, and X509.
A list of DBX (forbidden signature database) entries for the shielded VM initial state. These entries specify the forbidden signatures that Secure Boot will deny during boot.
The base64-encoded content of the DBX file (a forbidden signature database) used as part of the shielded VM initial state.
The file type of the DBXS, indicating whether the content is binary (BIN), an X.509 certificate (X509), or undefined (UNDEFINED).
google_compute_instance.disks.shielded_instance_initial_state.ke: List of key exchange key (KEK) certificates used by the shielded instance's initial state. Each entry includes the certificate content and file type.
The base64-encoded content of the key exchange key (KEK). This is used to provide the raw key data for shielded instance initial state.
The format of the key file. Allowed values are BIN, X509, and UNDEFINED.
google_compute_instance.disks.shielded_instance_initial_state.pk: The platform key (PK) entry, containing the base64-encoded content and file type of the platform key certificate used for verified boot.
Base64-encoded content of the platform key (PK) certificate.
The file type of the public key (pk) used in the shielded instance initial state. Valid values are BIN (binary), X509 (PEM certificate), or UNDEFINED.
google_compute_instance.disks.source: A reference (URL or name) to the source disk, image, or snapshot used to create or attach this disk.
google_compute_instance.disks.type: The type of the disk, either PERSISTENT (persistent disk) or SCRATCH (local SSD).
google_compute_instance.guest_accelerators.accelerator_count: The number of the guest accelerator cards of the specified type to attach to the instance.
google_compute_instance.guest_accelerators.accelerator_type: The type of accelerator (GPU) to attach to the instance, specified by its name or a full/partial URL to the accelerator type resource. For example, 'nvidia-tesla-k80' or 'zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-p100'.
google_compute_instance.instance_encryption_key: The customer-supplied encryption key used to encrypt the instance's boot disk. This field is computed and output-only.
google_compute_instance.metadata.items.key: The metadata key for the instance metadata entry. This key, combined with the value, defines a key-value pair for custom instance metadata.
google_compute_instance.metadata.items.value: The value for this metadata entry. This is the data associated with the metadata key on the instance.
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.access_configs: Configures external IP addresses for this network interface. You can specify a static IP with `nat_ip`, or leave it unset to receive an ephemeral IP.
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.access_configs.extern: The prefix length, in bits, of the external IPv6 address range assigned to this access configuration. It defines the network portion of the external IPv6 address.
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.access_configs.kind: The kind of the access config, always set to 'compute#accessConfig'.
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.access_configs.name: The name of this access configuration.
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.access_configs.nat_ip: The external IPv4 address assigned to the instance. Specify a static external IP (reserved) to assign it, or leave unset to have an ephemeral IP automatically assigned.
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.access_configs.networ: The network tier assigned to the access config's external IP. Allowed values are FIXED_STANDARD, PREMIUM, STANDARD, and STANDARD_OVERRIDES_FIXED_STANDARD, which control the pricing and performance tier for the external IP.
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.access_configs.public: Specifies a custom DNS PTR record for the public IP address of this access config. If not set, the default PTR record for the external IP is used.
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.access_configs.securi: The name of the Cloud Armor security policy to apply to this access config. This field is only applicable if the access_config type is EXTERNAL_MANAGED.
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.access_configs.set_pu: Indicates whether a public DNS PTR record should be set for the external IP address associated with this access config. Set to true to enable public PTR record creation.
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.access_configs.type: The type of access configuration. Valid values are DIRECT_IPV6 for direct IPv6 access and ONE_TO_ONE_NAT for standard one-to-one NAT (external IP).
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.alias_ip_ranges: A list of alias IP ranges to assign to this network interface. Each alias IP range allows the instance to use additional internal IP addresses. Typically includes an IP CIDR range and optionally a subnetwork range name.
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.alias_ip_ranges.ip_ci: The IP CIDR range for this alias IP, specified in CIDR notation (e.g., '10.0.0.0/24').
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.alias_ip_ranges.subne: The name of the subnetwork secondary range to use for this alias IP range. This range must have an internal IP address type. If not specified, the primary range of the subnetwork is used.
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.alias_ipv6_ranges: A list of IPv6 alias IP ranges to assign to this network interface. Each object defines an IPv6 CIDR range that the interface can use as an additional address.
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.alias_ipv6_ranges.ip_: The IPv6 CIDR range for this alias IP range, specified in CIDR notation (e.g., /64).
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.alias_ipv6_ranges.sub: The name of the subnetwork range from which the IPv6 alias range is allocated.
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.enable_vpc_scoped_dns: Enable VPC-scoped DNS for the network interface. When true, DNS queries from the instance are resolved using the VPC network's DNS configuration.
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.fingerprint: The fingerprint of the network interface, used for optimistic locking.
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.igmp_query: Configures the IGMP query mode for this network interface. Possible values are IGMP_QUERY_DISABLED and IGMP_QUERY_V2.
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.ipv6_access_configs: List of IPv6 access configurations for the network interface. Each configuration sets the external IPv6 address options, such as the network tier (e.g., PREMIUM or STANDARD) and optional public DNS domain name.
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.ipv6_access_configs.e: The external IPv6 address assigned to the instance's network interface in this IPv6 access configuration. This is a public IPv6 address used for internet-facing communication.
The prefix length of the external IPv6 address assigned to the instance's access config. Typically set to 32 for a /32 IPv6 address.
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.ipv6_access_configs.n: The external IPv6 address assigned to the instance. If not specified, an ephemeral IPv6 address is automatically assigned.
The network tier for this IPv6 access config. Valid values are FIXED_STANDARD, PREMIUM, STANDARD, and STANDARD_OVERRIDES_FIXED_STANDARD.
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.ipv6_access_configs.p: The domain name for the reverse DNS (PTR) record of the instance's public IPv6 address. When set, this custom domain is used for PTR lookups; otherwise, a Google Cloud default PTR record is used.
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.ipv6_access_configs.s: The name of the security policy (Cloud Armor policy) to apply to this IPv6 access config. This policy can be used to filter and protect traffic to the instance's public IPv6 address.
Whether to set the public PTR record for the IPv6 address. If set to true, a PTR record is created for the external IPv6 address to enable reverse DNS lookup. Defaults to false.
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.ipv6_access_configs.t: The type of IPv6 access configuration. Allowed values are DIRECT_IPV6 and ONE_TO_ONE_NAT.
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.ipv6_access_type: The type of IPv6 access. Valid values are EXTERNAL and INTERNAL. EXTERNAL means the IPv6 address is publicly accessible, while INTERNAL means it is private to the VPC network.
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.ipv6_address: The external IPv6 address assigned to this network interface.
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.kind: The kind of the network interface resource. It is always set to 'compute#networkInterface'.
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.name: The name assigned to this network interface, such as 'nic0'.
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.network: The name or self_link of the VPC network to attach this interface to. If subnetwork is not set, this field is required; otherwise, the network is inferred from the subnetwork.
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.network_attachment: The URL of the network attachment that this network interface should use. This can be specified instead of network or subnetwork when the interface is attached to a Network Attachment.
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.network_ip: The internal IPv4 address to assign to this network interface. If left unspecified, Compute Engine automatically assigns an ephemeral internal IP address.
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.nic_type: The type of network interface controller (NIC) to use for this network interface. Allowed values: GVNIC, IDPF, IRDMA, MRDMA, UNSPECIFIED_NIC_TYPE, VIRTIO_NET.
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.parent_nic_name: The name of the parent network interface that this interface is attached to or derived from, used in virtual NIC configurations (e.g., gVNIC).
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.queue_count: The number of queues to create for this network interface. This field is supported only for gVNIC NICs and is used to configure the number of queue pairs for the interface.
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.stack_type: The IP stack type for the network interface. Valid values are IPV4_IPV6 (dual-stack), IPV4_ONLY, or IPV6_ONLY.
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.subnetwork: The name or self_link of the subnetwork to attach to this network interface. If not specified, the default subnetwork for the network is used.
google_compute_instance.network_interfaces.vlan: The VLAN ID used for this network interface, applicable when the interface is attached to a VLAN attachment.
google_compute_instance.network_performance_config.total_egress_: The tier of total egress bandwidth for the instance. Valid values are DEFAULT (standard) and TIER_1 (higher bandwidth).
google_compute_instance.resource_status.scheduling: The scheduling configuration of the instance as reported by the API in the resource_status block. This includes computed values such as host error timeout seconds and node affinities.
google_compute_instance.resource_status.upcoming_maintenance.mai: The status of upcoming maintenance for the instance, indicating whether maintenance is ongoing, pending, or unknown. Possible values are ONGOING, PENDING, and UNKNOWN.
google_compute_instance.scheduling.node_affinities.key: The key for the node affinity, which corresponds to a node label key in the Compute Engine environment.
google_compute_instance.scheduling.node_affinities.operator: The operator for the node affinity condition. Valid values are IN (matches when the node is in the specified values), NOT_IN (matches when the node is not in the specified values), and OPERATOR_UNSPECIFIED (unspecified).
google_compute_instance.scheduling.node_affinities.values: The list of values for the node affinity key. This field is required when the operator is IN or NOT_IN.
google_compute_instance.service_accounts.email: The email address of the service account to associate with the instance.
google_compute_instance.service_accounts.scopes: List of OAuth 2.0 scopes that should be granted to the service account for accessing Google Cloud APIs. For example, 'https://www.googleapis.com/auth/compute.readonly' or 'https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform'.
google_compute_instance.source_machine_image_encryption_key: The customer-supplied encryption key for the source machine image used to create the instance. This field is output-only and reflects the encryption key details of the source image.
google_compute_instance.workload_identity_config: An output-only object containing the workload identity configuration for the instance, automatically computed and not user-settable.
google_compute_instance.workload_identity_config.identity: The email address of the service account to attach to the instance for workload identity. This enables the instance to use workload identity federation.

google_compute_instance_group.named_ports.name: The name of the named port, which must be unique within the instance group.
google_compute_instance_group.named_ports.port: The port number for the named port. This is the TCP/UDP port that the name maps to, used by load balancers or other services.

google_compute_instance_group_manager.all_instances_config: The all_instances_config block defines metadata and labels that are applied to every instance in the managed instance group. This computed value reflects the group's all-instances configuration.
google_compute_instance_group_manager.auto_healing_policies.health_check: The URL of the health check resource used to determine when to automatically recreate instances in the managed instance group. Must reference a health check of type HTTP, HTTPS, TCP, or SSL.
google_compute_instance_group_manager.auto_healing_policies.initial_delay_sec: The number of seconds to wait before the managed instance group applies autohealing policies to new instances. Must be between 0 and 3600 seconds.
google_compute_instance_group_manager.current_actions: The current actions being performed on the instances in this instance group manager. This computed field, which is output only, provides visibility into the operations currently being executed on the group's instances.
google_compute_instance_group_manager.distribution_policy: The distribution policy for the managed instance group, specifying how instances are distributed across zones and the target shape. This is a computed attribute reflecting the effective policy.
google_compute_instance_group_manager.distribution_policy.zones.zone: The name of a zone where instances are distributed. Must be in the same region as the instance group manager.
google_compute_instance_group_manager.instance_flexibility_policy: The instance flexibility policy for the managed instance group, which defines the set of machine types the group may use when creating instances. This computed field reflects the policy currently applied to the group.
google_compute_instance_group_manager.instance_flexibility_policy.instance_sel: The list of machine types to include in the instance selection. At least one machine type must be specified, and all machine types must be available in the same region as the instance group manager.
The rank of this instance selection, an integer from 0 to 100. Higher ranks indicate higher priority; Compute Engine uses the instance selection with the highest available rank.
google_compute_instance_group_manager.instance_lifecycle_policy: The lifecycle policy for instances in the managed instance group. This policy controls how the group handles instance updates and repairs.
google_compute_instance_group_manager.named_ports.name: The name of the named port. This name must be unique within the instance group.
google_compute_instance_group_manager.named_ports.port: The TCP/UDP port number that this named port maps to.
google_compute_instance_group_manager.resource_policies: An object that lists the resource policies (such as instance schedule policies) currently attached to the instance group manager. This field is computed and output-only, so it reflects the live state of the group.
google_compute_instance_group_manager.standby_policy: The standby policy for the managed instance group, which controls how instances are held in standby mode. This field is read-only (computed) and represents the effective standby configuration for the group.
google_compute_instance_group_manager.stateful_policy: The stateful policy for the managed instance group, which defines the preserved state (such as disks) for instances in the group. This field is computed by the provider and is output only, reflecting the actual applied stateful configuration.
google_compute_instance_group_manager.stateful_policy.preserved_state.disks.au: Specifies whether the disk is automatically deleted when the instance is deleted. In a stateful policy, set this to 'false' to preserve the disk; set to 'true' to delete it with the instance.
google_compute_instance_group_manager.stateful_policy.preserved_state.external: When true, the stateful external IP address is deleted when the instance is deleted. When false, the external IP address is preserved.
google_compute_instance_group_manager.stateful_policy.preserved_state.internal: The auto_delete setting for the internal IP address. A string containing 'true' or 'false' that controls whether the internal IP is automatically deleted when the instance is deleted, or if it is preserved for the next instance.
google_compute_instance_group_manager.status.all_instances_config: The effective all-instances configuration for the managed instance group, showing the properties (such as metadata) that are applied to all instances in the group.
google_compute_instance_group_manager.status.applied_accelerator_topologies.st: The lifecycle state of the applied accelerator topology. Possible values are ACTIVATING, ACTIVE, DEACTIVATING, FAILED, INCOMPLETE, and REACTIVATING.
Details about an error encountered when applying an accelerator topology to the instance group manager, within the state details of that applied topology.
List of error details that occurred while applying the accelerator topology to the instance group manager.

google_compute_instance_group_manager.status.bulk_instance_operation.last_prog: The machine-readable error code for this error entry.

google_compute_instance_group_manager.status.stateful: The stateful configuration status of the instance group manager, including whether a stateful configuration is present and the state of per-instance configurations.
google_compute_instance_group_manager.status.stateful.per_instance_configs: A map of instance names to their stateful configuration status, reflecting the per-instance stateful configuration state.
google_compute_instance_group_manager.status.version_target: The version that this instance group manager is targeting. It exposes the instance template and version name that the group is currently aiming to match, used for versioned canary updates.
google_compute_instance_group_manager.update_policy: The update policy for the instance group manager, providing details about how rolling updates are applied to instances. This field is output-only and contains the effective update settings.
google_compute_instance_group_manager.versions.instance_template: The instance template to use for this version. Specify the self-link or name of the instance template.
google_compute_instance_group_manager.versions.name: A unique name for this version within the instance group manager. It must be unique among all versions of the group.
google_compute_instance_group_manager.versions.target_size: The target number of instances for this version. Configure the fixed subfield for a static count or percent subfield for a percentage of the group's total size.
google_compute_instance_group_manager.versions.target_size.fixed: The fixed number of instances that should be running for this version. Must be a non-negative integer.
google_compute_instance_group_manager.versions.target_size.percent: The percentage of the instance group's current size that this version should target. For example, if the group has 100 instances and percent is 25, the version targets 25 instances. Must be an integer between 0 and 100.

google_compute_instance_group_manager_re.instances.preserved_state: Configuration for the state to preserve for the instance in the resize request. This block is used to set stateful disks and metadata that should be preserved when the instance is created or deleted. See the preserved_state sub-block for the full structure.
google_compute_instance_group_manager_re.instances.preserved_state.disks: Map of disk device names to their preservation state. The key is the device name of the disk, and the value configures preservation settings such as whether the disk is automatically deleted when the instance is deleted.
google_compute_instance_group_manager_re.instances.preserved_state.disks.auto_del: Specifies whether the preserved state disk is automatically deleted when the instance is deleted. Accepts string values 'true' or 'false' (defaults to 'false').
google_compute_instance_group_manager_re.instances.preserved_state.disks.mode: The access mode for the preserved disk. Valid values are READ_ONLY and READ_WRITE.
google_compute_instance_group_manager_re.instances.preserved_state.disks.source: The source disk associated with the preserved state. This is the device name or URL of the disk attached to the instance.
google_compute_instance_group_manager_re.instances.preserved_state.external_ips: Map of instance names to preserved external IP configurations for the resize operation. The keys are instance names, and the values are objects representing the external IP assignment for each instance.
google_compute_instance_group_manager_re.instances.preserved_state.external_ips.a: Whether the preserved external IP address should be automatically deleted when the associated instance is deleted, controlling the lifecycle of the IP in the instance's preserved state.
google_compute_instance_group_manager_re.instances.preserved_state.external_ips.i: The external IP address to preserve for the instance in the resize request.
The literal IP address value to preserve for the external IP.
google_compute_instance_group_manager_re.instances.preserved_state.internal_ips: Preserved internal IPs for the instance. The map keys are the network interface names, and the values define the IP address and auto-delete settings for each interface.
google_compute_instance_group_manager_re.instances.preserved_state.internal_ips.a: Indicates whether the preserved internal IP should be automatically deleted when the instance is deleted. Accepts 'true' or 'false'.
google_compute_instance_group_manager_re.instances.preserved_state.internal_ips.i: The static internal IP address to preserve for the instance's network interface when a resize operation recreates the instance. This is part of the preserved state defined for internal IPs.
The IPv4 address to preserve for this internal IP interface.
The literal IP address value for this internal IP interface.
google_compute_instance_group_manager_re.instances.preserved_state.metadata: Preserved metadata key-value pairs to be applied to the instances created by the resize request. This overrides metadata from the instance template for these instances.
google_compute_instance_group_manager_re.instances.status: The status of the instance in relation to the resize request. Possible values are APPLYING, DELETING, EFFECTIVE, NONE, UNAPPLIED, and UNAPPLIED_DELETION, indicating whether the instance is being applied, deleted, effective, not applicable, unapplied, or scheduled for deletion but not yet applied.
google_compute_instance_group_manager_re.status: The status of the resize request, containing the current state of the operation (such as pending, succeeded, or failed) and any error details if the request was not successful.
google_compute_instance_group_manager_re.status.error.errors.code: The error code for this error entry, typically a machine-readable identifier for the specific error type.

google_compute_instance_group_manager_re.status.error.errors.error_details.help: Help information for the error, containing links to documentation that can assist in resolving the issue.
google_compute_instance_group_manager_re.status.error.errors.error_details.help.l: A list of links to documentation or resources that provide additional information about the error. Each link includes a description and a URL.
The URL pointing to additional documentation or resources for troubleshooting the error.
google_compute_instance_group_manager_re.status.error.errors.error_details.locali: An object containing a localized error message and its locale. Provides a user-readable error description in the user's preferred language.
The locale code for the localized error message (e.g., en-US).
The localized text of the error message, intended for display to users.
