google_compute_instance_group_manager_re.status.error.errors.location: The location of the error in the request, such as the path to a specific field or parameter that caused the error.
google_compute_instance_group_manager_re.status.error.errors.message: A human-readable error message describing the failure.
google_compute_instance_group_manager_re.status.last_attempt: The result of the most recent resize attempt, including any error that occurred if the attempt failed.
google_compute_instance_group_manager_re.status.last_attempt.error.errors.code: The machine-readable error code associated with the error, such as a Compute Engine-specific error code.

google_compute_instance_template.properties: The instance properties defined by the template, containing configuration such as machine type, disks, network interfaces, and metadata. This field is computed and output-only.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.disks.architecture: Specifies the CPU architecture of the disk, used for the boot image. Allowed values are ARCHITECTURE_UNSPECIFIED (default), ARM64, and X86_64.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.disks.auto_delete: Indicates whether the disk should be automatically deleted when the instance is deleted. Defaults to false if not specified.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.disks.boot: Whether this disk is the boot disk for the instance. Only one disk can be marked as boot.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.disks.device_name: The name of the disk device as exposed to the guest operating system. This can be used to reference the disk inside the instance.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.disks.disk_encryption_key: The customer-supplied encryption key for the disk. This object configures how the disk is encrypted, typically using a raw key or a Cloud KMS key.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.disks.disk_encryption_key.kms: The fully qualified Cloud KMS key name used to encrypt the disk, such as projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/keyRings/{{key_ring}}/cryptoKeys/{{key}}.
The service account used to access the Cloud KMS key for disk encryption. If not specified, the Compute Engine Service Agent is used.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.disks.disk_encryption_key.raw: The raw customer-supplied encryption key, a base64-encoded 256-bit key, used to encrypt the disk. This key must be kept secret and is not retrievable after creation.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.disks.disk_encryption_key.rsa: The RSA-encrypted customer-supplied encryption key, base64-encoded. This key is used to encrypt the disk and must be a 256-bit key encrypted with Google's public RSA key.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.disks.disk_encryption_key.sha: The SHA256 hash of the raw disk encryption key. This is used to verify the key integrity and is often computed by Google Cloud when a raw_key is provided, but it can also be supplied to match a specific key.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.disks.disk_size_gb: The size of the disk in gigabytes, specified as a string (e.g., "10"). If omitted, the size is taken from the source image or snapshot.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.disks.force_attach: If set to true, the disk will be attached even if it is currently in use by another instance.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.disks.guest_os_features: List of features to enable for the guest operating system on this disk. Each object in the list specifies a feature via its `type` field, such as `UEFI_COMPATIBLE` or `VIRTIO_SCSI_MULTIQUEUE`, which allows the disk to support advanced guest OS capabilities.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.disks.guest_os_features.type: The type of guest OS feature to enable. Allowed values: BARE_METAL_LINUX_COMPATIBLE, CCA_CAPABLE, FEATURE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED, GVNIC, IDPF, MULTI_IP_SUBNET, SECURE_BOOT, SEV_CAPABLE, SEV_LIVE_MIGRATABLE, SEV_LIVE_MIGRATABLE_V2, SEV_SNP_CAPABLE, SNP_SVSM_CAPABLE, TDX_CAPABLE, UEFI_COMPATIBLE, VIRTIO_SCSI_MULTIQUEUE, WINDOWS.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.disks.index: The zero-based index of this disk. The boot disk must have index 0.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.disks.initialize_params: Specifies the parameters for initializing the disk, such as the source image, disk size, and disk type.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.disks.initialize_params.archi: The architecture of the disk image to use for the boot volume. Valid values are ARM64 and X86_64; ARCHITECTURE_UNSPECIFIED indicates that the architecture is not set.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.disks.initialize_params.descr: The description of the disk that will be created from these initialization parameters.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.disks.initialize_params.disk_: Specifies the name of the disk to create. If not provided, a name is automatically generated based on the instance name.
The size of the disk in gigabytes. If not specified, the default size is the size of the source image or snapshot.
The type of disk to provision, such as 'pd-standard' or 'pd-ssd'. Can be specified as a full or partial URL to a disk type resource.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.disks.initialize_params.enabl: Enable Confidential Compute mode for this disk. When enabled, the disk uses a hardware-based secure environment and supports confidential VM features. Defaults to false.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.disks.initialize_params.label: A set of key-value pairs to label the disk created from this initialization configuration. Labels can be used for organizing and identifying the disk.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.disks.initialize_params.on_up: Specifies the update action to take when the disk configuration changes. Allowed values are 'RECREATE_DISK', 'RECREATE_DISK_IF_SOURCE_CHANGED', and 'USE_EXISTING_DISK', controlling whether to recreate the disk, recreate only if the source changed, or keep the existing disk.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.disks.initialize_params.provi: Indicates how many IOPS to provision for the disk. This sets the number of I/O operations per second that the disk can handle, relevant for performance optimization of persistent disks.
The provisioned throughput for the disk, in MB/s, used to configure performance for supported disk types (e.g., Hyperdisk Throughput). Value is provided as a string.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.disks.initialize_params.repli: Specifies the zones for a regional persistent disk. The disk is replicated to these zones. Only applicable when creating a regional persistent disk.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.disks.initialize_params.resou: A map of resource manager tags to apply to the disk. Keys are resource manager tag key IDs (format: tagKeys/1234) and values are resource manager tag value IDs (format: tagValues/5678).
List of resource policies (e.g., snapshot schedule policies) to attach to the disk. These policies define automated operations such as scheduled snapshots.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.disks.initialize_params.sourc: The image to use for this disk, specified as a fully-qualified URL, self-link, or name.
The customer-supplied encryption key used to decrypt the source image when creating the disk. This is required if the source image is encrypted with a customer-supplied encryption key.
The fully qualified Cloud KMS key name (e.g., projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/keyRings/RING_NAME/cryptoKeys/KEY_NAME) used to encrypt the source image.
The email address of the service account used to authenticate to the KMS key for encrypting the source image. If omitted, the Compute Engine default service account is used.
The RFC 4648 base64-encoded 256-bit raw key used to decrypt the source image. Required if the source image is protected by a customer-supplied encryption key.
The RSA-encrypted 256-bit AES key, base64 encoded, used to decrypt the source image. Either this or `raw_key` must be specified.
The SHA256 hash of the customer-supplied encryption key. This is used to verify the integrity of the key when decrypting the source image.

The service account used to access the Cloud KMS key that encrypts the source snapshot.
The base64-encoded 256-bit customer-supplied encryption key used to encrypt the source snapshot.
The base64-encoded RSA-encrypted copy of the customer-supplied encryption key used to decrypt the source snapshot. Either this field or raw_key must be set.

google_compute_instance_template.properties.disks.initialize_params.stora: The URL of the storage pool in which the disk is created. When set, the disk is provisioned from the named storage pool, which must exist in the same project and zone as the instance template.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.disks.interface: Specifies the disk interface type. Allowed values are 'SCSI' and 'NVME'.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.disks.kind: The type of resource. For an attached disk in an instance template, this is always 'compute#attachedDisk'.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.disks.licenses: List of license URIs that apply to the disk, typically derived from the source image or snapshot.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.disks.mode: Specifies the access mode of the disk. Valid values are READ_ONLY (attaches the disk as read-only) and READ_WRITE (attaches the disk with read-write access).
google_compute_instance_template.properties.disks.saved_state: The saved state of the disk when the instance is stopped. Allowed values are DISK_SAVED_STATE_UNSPECIFIED (default) and PRESERVED.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.disks.shielded_instance_initi: Sets the initial state for shielded VM features on the boot disk, such as secure boot, vTPM, and integrity monitoring. This object configures which Shielded VM settings are enabled when the disk is used to boot a shielded instance.
The base64-encoded content of the DB file (e.g., a certificate or key) used in the shielded instance initial state for this disk.
The file type of the database entry in the shielded instance initial state. Allowed values are BIN, X509, and UNDEFINED.

The list of DBX (database exchange) entries for the shielded instance's UEFI secure boot. These entries define the forbidden database used to revoke untrusted certificates or manifests during integrity verification.
The base64-encoded content of the dbxs file for the shielded instance initial state.
The file type of the DBXS database entry. Valid values are BIN, X509, and UNDEFINED, indicating the encoding format of the file content.
The Key Exchange Key (KEK) for the shielded instance's initial state. This is a list of objects, each specifying a KEK file's content and file type.
The base64-encoded content of the Key Exchange Key (KEK) to set for the shielded instance's initial state. This is the actual key data.
The file type of the key content. Valid values are BIN (binary format), X509 (X.509 certificate format), and UNDEFINED.
The Platform Key (PK) of the shielded VM's initial state, which serves as the root of trust for the UEFI secure boot process.
The content of the platform key (PK) certificate for the shielded instance initial state, typically base64-encoded.
The format of the public key file. Allowed values are `BIN` (binary DER), `X509` (PEM encoded X.509 certificate), and `UNDEFINED` (unspecified).
google_compute_instance_template.properties.disks.source: The name or fully qualified URL of the source disk, image, or snapshot used to create the disk.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.disks.type: The type of disk to attach. Valid values are PERSISTENT for a standard persistent disk and SCRATCH for a local SSD.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.guest_accelerators.accelerato: The number of accelerators of the specified type to attach to the instance.
The name of the accelerator type to attach, such as 'nvidia-tesla-k80' or 'nvidia-tesla-p100'. Example: 'nvidia-tesla-k80'.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.metadata.items.key: The key of the metadata item, used to set custom metadata on the instance template.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.metadata.items.value: The value of the metadata item, corresponding to the metadata key in the instance template's metadata.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.network_interfaces.access_con: A list of access configurations for the network interface. Each access config assigns a public IP address to the instance, enabling external connectivity, and can include settings such as the NAT IP and network tier.
The external IPv6 address assigned to the instance's network interface access config. If omitted, an ephemeral IPv6 address is automatically assigned.
The prefix length of the external IPv6 address assigned to the instance. In Google Cloud, the only supported value is 96.
The type of resource. For an access config, this is always 'compute#accessConfig'.
The name of the access configuration. Defaults to 'external-nat' if not specified.
The external IP address to assign to the instance. If not specified, an ephemeral IP address is automatically assigned.
The network service tier for the access config. Accepted values are FIXED_STANDARD, PREMIUM, STANDARD, and STANDARD_OVERRIDES_FIXED_STANDARD.
The public DNS domain name to be used for the reverse DNS (PTR) record of the external IP address associated with this access config. Must be a valid DNS name.
The URL of a Cloud Armor security policy to apply to this access config. This policy filters traffic to the external IP address of the instance.
If true, a public DNS PTR record is set for the external IP address of this access config, enabling reverse DNS lookup. Defaults to false.
The type of access configuration. Valid values are DIRECT_IPV6 for direct IPv6 access and ONE_TO_ONE_NAT for static external IP address (NAT).
google_compute_instance_template.properties.network_interfaces.alias_ip_r: Alias IP ranges for this network interface. Each object in the list specifies a CIDR range (ip_cidr_range) and optionally a subnetwork range name (subnetwork_range_name) to assign as an alias IP range.
The IP CIDR range for this alias IP range, in CIDR notation (e.g., '10.0.0.0/24').
The name of a secondary IP range in the subnetwork to allocate IP addresses from for this alias IP range. If not specified, the primary IP range of the subnetwork is used.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.network_interfaces.alias_ipv6: The IPv6 CIDR range for the alias IP range on the network interface, specified in CIDR notation. This range must lie within the subnetwork's IPv6 address space and should not overlap with other alias ranges.
The name of the subnetwork's secondary IPv6 range to which the alias IPv6 IP address belongs. This must match an existing IPv6 range defined in the subnetwork's secondary IP ranges.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.network_interfaces.enable_vpc: Enables VPC-scoped DNS for this network interface, allowing DNS queries to use the VPC's DNS configuration and policies.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.network_interfaces.fingerprin: The fingerprint of the network interface configuration, generated by the API and used for optimistic locking. It changes whenever the interface settings are modified.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.network_interfaces.igmp_query: Whether IGMP query is enabled on this network interface. Valid values are `IGMP_QUERY_DISABLED` (no IGMP queries) and `IGMP_QUERY_V2` (enable IGMP v2 queries).
google_compute_instance_template.properties.network_interfaces.internal_i: The prefix length of the internal IPv6 address assigned to the network interface, such as 64 for a /64 subnetwork.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.network_interfaces.ipv6_acces: The IPv6 access configurations for this network interface. Each configuration assigns an external IPv6 address to the interface, enabling IPv6 internet access, with only one access config supported per interface.
The external IPv6 address for this access configuration. If not specified, an automatically allocated address is used.

The prefix length of the external IPv6 address assigned to the instance, expressed as an integer (e.g., 96). It defines the IPv6 network prefix and is used together with the external IPv6 address to specify the IPv6 configuration.
The kind of the IPv6 access config. This field is always set to 'compute#accessConfig'.
The name of this IPv6 access configuration. If omitted, the default value 'external-ipv6' is used.
The network tier for this IPv6 access config. Valid values are FIXED_STANDARD, PREMIUM, STANDARD, and STANDARD_OVERRIDES_FIXED_STANDARD.
The public PTR domain name for the IPv6 address, used for reverse DNS lookup.
The security policy to associate with this IPv6 access configuration.
Whether to set a public DNS PTR record for the IPv6 address. Set to true to enable.
The type of IPv6 access configuration. Possible values are DIRECT_IPV6 (direct external IPv6 connectivity) and ONE_TO_ONE_NAT (IPv6 connectivity through one-to-one NAT).
Specifies the access type for IPv6 addresses on this network interface. Set to EXTERNAL for an external IPv6 address, or INTERNAL for an internal IPv6 address.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.network_interfaces.ipv6_addre: The IPv6 address to assign to the network interface. This is used to specify a static IPv6 address for the interface.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.network_interfaces.kind: The type of the resource. Always 'compute#networkInterface'.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.network_interfaces.network: The name or self_link of the VPC network to attach this interface to. Either `network` or `subnetwork` is required; if you specify `subnetwork`, `network` is inferred.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.network_interfaces.network_at: URL of the network attachment resource to which this network interface attaches. If specified, it overrides the network and subnetwork fields, and is used for the network attachment type of network interface.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.network_interfaces.network_ip: The private IPv4 address to assign to this network interface. If not set, an ephemeral address is automatically assigned.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.network_interfaces.nic_type: Specifies the type of network interface card (NIC) to use for the interface. Allowed values are GVNIC, IDPF, IRDMA, MRDMA, UNSPECIFIED_NIC_TYPE, and VIRTIO_NET.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.network_interfaces.queue_coun: The number of queues to use for this network interface. A value of 0 indicates the default number of queues (one per vCPU). The value must be a power of 2 and cannot exceed the instance's vCPU count.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.network_interfaces.stack_type: The IP stack type for this network interface. Valid values are IPV4_IPV6 (dual-stack), IPV4_ONLY, and IPV6_ONLY.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.network_interfaces.subnetwork: The name or self-link of the subnetwork to which the network interface is attached. If not specified, the default subnetwork of the specified network is used.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.network_performance_config: Configuration block for network performance settings, including the total egress bandwidth tier which can be set to 'DEFAULT' or 'TIER_1'.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.network_performance_config.to: The egress bandwidth tier to enable for the instance's network performance configuration. Allowed values are DEFAULT and TIER_1.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.scheduling.node_affinities.ke: The label key for the node affinity requirement. This is the key of a node label used to match nodes.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.scheduling.node_affinities.op: Specifies the operator for the node affinity expression. Valid values are IN, NOT_IN, and OPERATOR_UNSPECIFIED.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.scheduling.node_affinities.va: The list of node affinity values. These values are matched against the key and operator to determine the scheduling constraint, e.g., the node group names when key is 'node-group-name'.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.service_accounts.email: The email address of the service account to associate with the instance. If not provided, the default Compute Engine service account is used.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.service_accounts.scopes: A list of OAuth scopes to associate with the service account for the instance. For example, 'cloud-platform' gives full access, while 'storage-ro' grants read-only access to Cloud Storage.
google_compute_instance_template.properties.workload_identity_config.iden: The service account email to use as the workload identity for the instance. If omitted, the default Compute Engine service account is used.
Whether the identity certificate is enabled for this workload identity configuration.
google_compute_instance_template.source_instance_params.disk_configs.auto: Whether the disk will be auto-deleted when the instance is deleted. When set in source_instance_params.disk_configs, this overrides the corresponding property from the source instance.
google_compute_instance_template.source_instance_params.disk_configs.cust: The custom image to use for this disk when creating the instance template from a source instance. If specified, this overrides the image of the corresponding source disk.
google_compute_instance_template.source_instance_params.disk_configs.devi: The device name of the disk in the source instance to which this disk configuration applies.
google_compute_instance_template.source_instance_params.disk_configs.inst: Specifies how the disk is created from the source instance's disk. Valid values are ATTACH_READ_ONLY (attach read-only), BLANK (create a blank disk), CUSTOM_IMAGE (create from a custom image), DEFAULT (use default behavior), DO_NOT_INCLUDE (exclude the disk), SOURCE_IMAGE (create from the source image), and SOURCE_IMAGE_FAMILY (create from the source image family).

google_compute_instant_snapshot_group.resource_status.source_info.consistency_: The consistency group that the source of this instant snapshot group belongs to, if any. This is a computed output field.
Output only. The identifier of the consistency group associated with this instant snapshot group, used to coordinate group-consistent operations.
google_compute_instant_snapshot_group.source_consistency_group: The self-link of the consistency group (resource policy) used as the source for the instant snapshots in this group. This field is computed and output only, populated when the group is associated with a consistency group.

google_compute_interconnect.application_aware_interconnect.bandwidth: The bandwidth_percentage_policy block configures the bandwidth percentage allocation for an application-aware interconnect.

google_compute_interconnect.application_aware_interconnect.shape_ave: The traffic class (TC1-TC6) to which the average percentage applies.
google_compute_interconnect.circuit_infos.customer_demarc_id: The customer-side demarcation ID for the interconnect circuit.
google_compute_interconnect.circuit_infos.google_demarc_id: The Google-assigned demarcation point ID for this interconnect circuit.
google_compute_interconnect.expected_outages.affected_circuits: The list of circuit names that are affected by this outage.
google_compute_interconnect.expected_outages.end_time: The time at which the expected outage is scheduled to end.
google_compute_interconnect.expected_outages.issue_type: The type of issue causing the expected outage. Possible values are IT_OUTAGE, IT_PARTIAL_OUTAGE, OUTAGE, and PARTIAL_OUTAGE.
google_compute_interconnect.expected_outages.source: The source of the expected outage. Allowed values are GOOGLE for outages initiated by Google, and NSRC_GOOGLE for outages reported by the Network Service Reliability Center.
google_compute_interconnect.expected_outages.start_time: The start time of the outage, in RFC3339 format.
google_compute_interconnect.expected_outages.state: The current state of the expected outage. Possible values are: ACTIVE, CANCELLED, COMPLETED, NS_ACTIVE, NS_CANCELED.
google_compute_interconnect.macsec.pre_shared_keys.name: A user-defined name for this pre-shared key. Must be unique within the interconnect.
google_compute_interconnect.macsec.pre_shared_keys.start_time: The start time for this pre-shared key, in RFC3339 UTC timestamp format. The key becomes active at this time; if omitted, it becomes active immediately.

google_compute_interconnect_attachment.configuration_constraints.bgp_peer_asn_r: The maximum value of the range of allowed BGP peer ASN (Autonomous System Number) values. This defines the upper bound for the ASN range that can be configured for the BGP peer.
The minimum (lower bound) of a BGP peer ASN range. The range is inclusive of this value.
google_compute_interconnect_attachment.l2_forwarding.appliance_mappings.applian: IP address of the appliance inside the customer's network, used for this VLAN attachment mapping.
google_compute_interconnect_attachment.l2_forwarding.appliance_mappings.inner_v: The IP address of the appliance associated with the inner VLAN in this mapping.
A list of inner VLAN tags that are mapped to an appliance in the L2 forwarding appliance mapping. These tags are used to classify traffic for routing to the specified appliance.

google_compute_interconnect_attachment_g.configured.availability_sla.effective_sl: The effective Service Level Agreement (SLA) for the interconnect attachment group, computed by the provider. Possible values: EFFECTIVE_SLA_UNSPECIFIED, NO_SLA, PRODUCTION_CRITICAL, PRODUCTION_NON_CRITICAL.
google_compute_interconnect_attachment_g.configured.availability_sla.intended_sla: Computed list of blockers that would prevent the configured availability SLA from being met.
List of interconnect attachments that are configured as intended blockers for the availability SLA.

The type of blocker preventing the intended SLA from being met. Possible values include: BLOCKER_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED, INCOMPATIBLE_METROS, INCOMPATIBLE_REGIONS, MISSING_GLOBAL_ROUTING, NO_ATTACHMENTS, NO_ATTACHMENTS_IN_METRO_AND_ZONE, and OTHER.
A URL to documentation describing this intended SLA blocker.
A human-readable explanation of the intended SLA blocker, describing why it might prevent meeting the availability SLA.
List of metro locations that are excluded from the availability SLA, as they are considered blockers.

google_compute_interconnect_attachment_g.intent.availability_sla: The availability SLA (service level agreement) for this interconnect attachment. Valid values are: AVAILABILITY_SLA_UNSPECIFIED, NO_SLA, PRODUCTION_CRITICAL, and PRODUCTION_NON_CRITICAL.
google_compute_interconnect_attachment_g.logical_structure.regions: A list of regions where the interconnect attachment group is available, along with the status of the group in each region.
google_compute_interconnect_attachment_g.logical_structure.regions.metros.facilit: A list of physical data center facilities available in the metro for this interconnect attachment group.
The name of the physical facility (data center) within the metro where the interconnect attachment is located.

The availability zone within the facility, typically in the form `<region>-<zone>` (e.g., us-central1-a).
google_compute_interconnect_attachment_g.logical_structure.regions.metros.metro: The name of a metropolitan area (metro) that is associated with a specific region in the logical structure of an Interconnect attachment group.
google_compute_interconnect_attachment_g.logical_structure.regions.region: The Google Cloud region for this logical structure entry. Must be a valid region name, e.g., 'us-central1'.

google_compute_interconnect_group.configured.topology_capability.intended_: A list of reasons that prevent the interconnect group's intended topology capability from being realized. A human-readable explanation of why the intended topology capability is blocked.
List of facility names that are blocking the intended topology capability for this interconnect group.
The list of interconnect names that are blocking the intended topology capability for this interconnect group.

A list of zones in which the intended topology capability is blocked or unavailable, as part of a capability blocker.
google_compute_interconnect_group.configured.topology_capability.supported: The supported service level agreement (SLA) for this topology capability. Possible values are: NO_SLA, PRODUCTION_CRITICAL, PRODUCTION_NON_CRITICAL, UNSPECIFIED.
google_compute_interconnect_group.intent.topology_capability: Specifies the topology capability level for the interconnect group, indicating the required service level. google_compute_interconnect_group.physical_structure.metros: The metropolitan areas where the physical structure of the interconnect group is located. This computed field provides the list of metros supported by the physical infrastructure.
google_compute_interconnect_group.physical_structure.metros.metro: The metropolitan area where the interconnect group's physical structure is located, such as 'london' or 'sydney'.

google_compute_license.resource_requirements: The minimum resource requirements that an instance must meet to use this license. Includes `min_guest_cpu_count` for the minimum number of virtual CPUs and `min_memory_mb` for the minimum memory in megabytes.

google_compute_machine_image.instance_properties: The properties of the source instance used to create the machine image. This is an output-only field that captures the instance configuration for reference.
google_compute_machine_image.instance_properties.disks.architecture: The architecture of the disk, either ARM64 or X86_64, or ARCHITECTURE_UNSPECIFIED if not set.
google_compute_machine_image.instance_properties.disks.auto_delete: Specifies whether this disk will be automatically deleted when the instance is deleted. This controls the disk's lifecycle relative to the instance.
google_compute_machine_image.instance_properties.disks.boot: Indicates whether this disk is a boot disk. A boot disk is the primary disk from which the instance boots.
google_compute_machine_image.instance_properties.disks.device_name: Specifies a unique device name of your choice that is reflected into the /dev/disk/by-id/google-* tree of a Linux operating system running within the instance. This name can be used to reference the device for mounting, resizing, and so on, from within the instance.
google_compute_machine_image.instance_properties.disks.disk_encryptio: The customer-supplied encryption key (CSEK) or Cloud KMS key used to encrypt the disk. This block can contain a raw key, an RSA-encrypted key, or a KMS key self-link.
The full resource name of the Cloud KMS CryptoKey used to encrypt the disk. For example: projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/keyRings/KEY_RING/cryptoKeys/KEY_NAME.
The service account used to encrypt or decrypt the disk with the KMS key. This account must have the required Cloud KMS IAM permissions on the key.
The raw customer-supplied encryption key for the disk, base64-encoded. This is used when providing your own key instead of a KMS key.

The customer-supplied encryption key, encrypted using an RSA public key and encoded in base64, used to protect the disk and its contents. This allows the key to be provided securely without exposing the raw key in plaintext.
The SHA-256 hash of the customer-supplied encryption key. This value is used to verify the key's integrity and to identify the key when the disk is attached to a VM.
google_compute_machine_image.instance_properties.disks.guest_os_featu: The type of guest OS feature to enable on the disk. Must be one of the predefined feature types: BARE_METAL_LINUX_COMPATIBLE, CCA_CAPABLE, FEATURE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED, GVNIC, IDPF, MULTI_IP_SUBNET, SECURE_BOOT, SEV_CAPABLE, SEV_LIVE_MIGRATABLE, SEV_LIVE_MIGRATABLE_V2, SEV_SNP_CAPABLE, SNP_SVSM_CAPABLE, TDX_CAPABLE, UEFI_COMPATIBLE, VIRTIO_SCSI_MULTIQUEUE, WINDOWS.
google_compute_machine_image.instance_properties.disks.index: The zero-based index of this disk in the attached disks list, which determines the device name (e.g., /dev/sda) and boot order.
google_compute_machine_image.instance_properties.disks.initialize_par: Initialize parameters for the disk, including source image, disk size, and disk type, used when creating an instance from this machine image.
The CPU architecture of the disk, indicating compatibility with ARM64 or X86_64. Valid values are ARCHITECTURE_UNSPECIFIED, ARM64, and X86_64.
An optional description for the disk. This is a user-defined field that can be used to provide additional context about the disk.
Specifies the name of the disk. If not set, the default is to use the name of the instance.
The size of the disk in gigabytes (GB). This value is provided as a string, but should represent a numeric size (e.g., '10').
The type of disk to use, such as 'pd-standard' or 'pd-ssd'. This can be a full or partial URL to a disk type resource. If not specified, the default disk type is used.
Whether this disk adds confidential computing capability. Note: This field is only applicable to boot disks of VM instances that use Confidential VMs.
Labels to apply to this disk. A map of key/value pairs that can be used to organize and identify the disk.
A list of URLs referencing license resources that the disk will be subject to when initialized. When specified, these licenses override any licenses inherited from the source image or snapshot.

Specifies the action to take on the disk when its configuration is updated. Possible values: `RECREATE_DISK` (always recreate), `RECREATE_DISK_IF_SOURCE_CHANGED` (recreate only if the source changes), `USE_EXISTING_DISK` (keep the existing disk).
The provisioned I/O operations per second (IOPS) for the persistent disk. This value is represented as a string and determines the disk's performance level when initialized.
The provisioned throughput of the disk in MB/s, used to configure performance for supported disk types such as SSD persistent disks.
Specifies the zones for a regional persistent disk. Provide exactly two zones to create a regional disk; leave unset for a zonal disk.
A map of resource manager tags (key-value pairs) to apply to the disk when it is created. These tags can be used for access control, cost tracking, or resource organization.
List of resource policy self-links to apply to the disk. Resource policies control schedules for snapshots or other disk management operations.
The source image to use for the disk. This can be a full URL, a partial URL, or an image name. The disk is initialized from this image.
Encryption key used to encrypt the source image. If the specified source image is encrypted, this key is required to access it when creating the disk.
The customer-managed encryption key name used to encrypt the source image. Provide the full resource name in the format projects/{project}/locations/{location}/keyRings/{keyRing}/cryptoKeys/{key}.

The service account used to perform cryptographic operations with the KMS key specified in this encryption key block. This is required if the key's permissions are scoped to a specific service account.

The base64-encoded customer-supplied encryption key (256-bit) used to encrypt the source image. This is required when the source image is encrypted with a customer-supplied key rather than a Google-managed key.
The RSA-encrypted (base64-encoded) key used to encrypt the source image. This is an alternative to using `raw_key`.
The SHA-256 hash of the customer-supplied encryption key used to protect the source image.
The source snapshot used to initialize this disk. Provide the full or partial URL of the snapshot resource.
Specifies the customer-supplied encryption key used to decrypt the source snapshot. Required if the source snapshot is protected by a customer-managed encryption key.
The fully-qualified Cloud KMS key name used to decrypt the source snapshot referenced by this initialize parameter.

The service account used to access the Cloud KMS key that encrypts the source snapshot. This is required when the snapshot uses a Customer-Managed Encryption Key (CMEK) and the service account must have permissions to use the KMS key.
The 256-bit customer-supplied encryption key, encoded in RFC 4648 base64, used to decrypt the source snapshot.

Specifies an encryption key wrapped by an RSA public key, as an alternative to supplying the raw key. The RSA public key must be created from a Google Cloud key with algorithm RSA_2048 and padding PKCS1, and the RSA key must be 2048 bits.
The SHA256 hash of the customer-supplied encryption key for the source snapshot. This is used to verify the key and is typically computed when a raw key or RSA-encrypted key is provided.
The URL or name of a storage pool to use for creating this disk. If specified, the disk is provisioned from the given storage pool (e.g., a Hyperdisk storage pool) rather than standard storage.
google_compute_machine_image.instance_properties.disks.interface: The disk interface used for attaching this disk. Valid values are 'NVME' or 'SCSI'.
google_compute_machine_image.instance_properties.disks.kind: The type of the resource. For a disk in instance properties, this is always 'compute#disk'.
google_compute_machine_image.instance_properties.disks.licenses: List of license URIs to apply to this disk, such as operating system licenses.
google_compute_machine_image.instance_properties.disks.mode: The access mode of the disk. Valid values are READ_ONLY and READ_WRITE.
google_compute_machine_image.instance_properties.disks.saved_state: The saved state of the disk when creating a machine image. Set to PRESERVED to preserve the disk's state, or DISK_SAVED_STATE_UNSPECIFIED for the default behavior.
google_compute_machine_image.instance_properties.disks.shielded_insta: The list of UEFI secure boot database (db) entries for this shielded instance initial state. Each entry contains the base64-encoded content and file type (e.g., X509, BIN) for a secure boot database.
The base64-encoded certificate content for the UEFI secure boot database (dbs).
The format of the file. Allowed values are: BIN (binary content), X509 (X.509 certificate), or UNDEFINED (unspecified).
List of X.509 certificates that are revoked for UEFI secure boot (dbx). Each entry includes the certificate content and file type.

google_compute_network.peerings.auto_create_routes: Whether to automatically create routes for the peer network in this VPC peering connection. When true, routes are automatically generated for destinations in the peered network; when false, no automatic route creation occurs. This field is deprecated in favor of export_custom_routes and import_custom_routes.
google_compute_network.peerings.connection_status.consensus_sta: The deletion status of this VPC network peering connection as part of the consensus state between local and peer networks. Possible values: DELETE_ACKNOWLEDGED, DELETE_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED, LOCAL_CANCEL_REQUESTED, LOCAL_DELETE_REQUESTED, PEER_CANCEL_REQUESTED, PEER_DELETE_REQUESTED.

Represents the update status of the peering consensus state. Possible values: IN_SYNC (no pending updates), PENDING_LOCAL_ACKNOWLEDMENT (waiting for local acknowledgment), PENDING_PEER_ACKNOWLEDGEMENT (waiting for peer acknowledgment), UPDATE_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED (unset).
google_compute_network.peerings.connection_status.traffic_confi: The traffic configuration of the peering connection, providing the current traffic state and any associated details.
Indicates whether the VPC network exports its custom routes (routes not automatically generated from subnets) to the peered network.

This boolean flag controls whether subnet routes with public IP addresses are exported to the peer network. When true, the VPC network exports routes to its peer for subnets that have public IPs, allowing the peer to reach these subnets via the peering connection.
When true, this peering connection imports custom routes (non-subnet routes) from the peer network.
A boolean flag indicating whether the peering connection imports subnet routes with public IP addresses from the peer network.
The IP stack type for the traffic over the peering connection, either IPV4_ONLY or IPV4_IPV6.
google_compute_network.peerings.connection_status.update_strate: Determines how updates to the peering are applied. CONSENSUS requires both networks to agree on updates, INDEPENDENT allows either side to update without the other's approval, and UNSPECIFIED indicates no strategy has been set.
google_compute_network.peerings.exchange_subnet_routes: Controls whether subnet routes are exchanged with the peered network. When true (default), subnet routes are automatically advertised to the peer network; setting to false disables the exchange.
google_compute_network.peerings.export_custom_routes: Whether this network exports custom routes (such as dynamic routes and routes learned from other networks) to the peered network. When true, these routes are advertised to the peer.
google_compute_network.peerings.export_subnet_routes_with_publi: Indicates whether subnet routes with public IP addresses are exported to the peer network. When set to true, the peer network can learn these routes; when false, they are not exported.
google_compute_network.peerings.import_custom_routes: Indicates whether custom routes from the peered network are imported into this network's route table. Set to true to enable importing custom routes.
google_compute_network.peerings.import_subnet_routes_with_publi: Whether to import subnet routes with public IP addresses from the peer network. When false, only private subnet routes are imported. Defaults to false.
google_compute_network.peerings.network: The name or self_link of the peer network to create the peering with. This can be a network in the same project or in a different project, and must be specified as a URL if cross-project.
google_compute_network.peerings.peer_mtu: The Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) for the VPC network peering connection, specified in bytes. This is the MTU of the peer network and determines the maximum size of packets that can be sent over the peering link without fragmentation.
google_compute_network.peerings.stack_type: The stack type for the peering, either IPV4_ONLY or IPV4_IPV6, controlling whether IPv6 traffic is supported over the peering.
google_compute_network.peerings.state: Current state of the VPC network peering connection, either ACTIVE or INACTIVE.
google_compute_network.peerings.state_details: The output-only details of the VPC network peering state, providing additional context about the current peering status, such as the reason for the state.
google_compute_network.peerings.update_strategy: Specifies the update strategy for the VPC peering. Possible values are 'CONSENSUS' (updates require agreement from both peering sides), 'INDEPENDENT' (updates can be made independently by either side), and 'UNSPECIFIED' (default, behavior is determined by the API).

google_compute_network_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.match.dest_addres: A list of destination address group names that the packet mirroring rule matches. Traffic to any address group in this list is matched by the rule.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.match.dest_fqdns: Specifies the list of fully qualified domain names (FQDNs) to match as the destination in the packet mirroring rule.
