Each entry must be a fully qualified domain name, and the rule applies to traffic originating from the resolved addresses of these FQDNs.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.match.src_ip_rang: A list of source IP address ranges (in CIDR notation) that this packet mirroring rule matches.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.match.src_network: The source network context for the packet mirroring rule, defining the type of network from which traffic originates. Allowed values are INTERNET, INTRA_VPC, NON_INTERNET, UNSPECIFIED, and VPC_NETWORKS.
The source network type to match for the packet mirroring rule. Allowed values are: INTERNET, INTRA_VPC, NON_INTERNET, UNSPECIFIED, VPC_NETWORKS.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.match.src_region_: List of source region codes (e.g., 'us-central1') that the rule matches. The rule applies to packets originating from any of these regions.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.match.src_secure_: A list of secure tags that source instances must have for the packet mirroring rule to match. Traffic from an instance with any of the listed secure tags is included in the rule.
The name of the secure tag used to match source traffic. This is the full resource name of the tag, for example, 'tagValues/123'.
Indicates whether the secure tag is effective (EFFECTIVE) or ineffective (INEFFECTIVE) for source tag matching in packet mirroring rules.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.match.src_threat_: List of threat intelligence categories to match against the source IP address. When specified, the rule matches only traffic originating from IPs listed in the provided intelligence feeds.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.priority: The priority of the packet mirroring rule. Lower values have higher precedence. Valid range is 0 to 2147483647.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.security_profile_: The name or URL of the security profile group that defines the security profiles to apply to mirrored traffic.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.target_forwarding: List of forwarding rule URLs that the packet mirroring rule applies to.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.target_resources: The list of target resources for the packet mirroring rule. Each entry can be a network tag or an instance group URL.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.target_secure_tag: A list of secure tags that specify the target instances to which this packet mirroring rule applies. Traffic from instances with any of these secure tags will be mirrored.
The resource name of the secure tag value to match, in the format `tagValues/{tag_value_id}` (e.g., `tagValues/123456`). Specifies which tagged instances are targeted by the rule.
The state of the secure tag, indicating whether it is currently active (EFFECTIVE) or not (INEFFECTIVE).
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.target_service_ac: A list of service account email addresses that identify which instances' traffic is mirrored. The packet mirroring rule applies to instances that have one of these service accounts associated.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.packet_mirroring_rules.target_type: The type of target for the packet mirroring rule. Allowed values are INSTANCES (for targeting VM instances) and INTERNAL_MANAGED_LB (for targeting internal managed load balancers).
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.action: The action to take on traffic that matches this rule. Valid values are 'allow' and 'deny'.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.direction: The direction of traffic that the firewall rule applies to. Valid values are EGRESS for outbound traffic and INGRESS for inbound traffic.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.disabled: Whether the rule is disabled. When set to true, the rule is not evaluated against traffic.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.enable_logging: Whether to enable logging for this rule. When enabled, firewall rule logs are exported to Cloud Logging.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.kind: The type of the resource. Always 'compute#firewallPolicyRule' for firewall policy rules.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.match.dest_address_groups: List of destination address groups to match. Each entry is a name or URL of an address group resource.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.match.dest_fqdns: A list of destination fully qualified domain names (FQDNs) that the firewall rule matches. Traffic to any of these FQDNs is subject to the rule's action.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.match.dest_ip_ranges: List of destination IP address ranges in CIDR notation (e.g., '10.0.0.0/24'). The firewall rule applies to traffic whose destination IP address is within any of these ranges.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.match.dest_network_context: The destination network context for the rule, specifying the type of network to which traffic is destined. Valid values are: INTERNET, INTRA_VPC, NON_INTERNET, UNSPECIFIED, VPC_NETWORKS.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.match.dest_network_type: Specifies the destination network type for which the firewall rule applies. Allowed values are: INTERNET, INTRA_VPC, NON_INTERNET, UNSPECIFIED, VPC_NETWORKS.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.match.dest_region_codes: A list of destination region codes to which this firewall policy rule applies. The rule matches traffic destined to these GCP regions.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.match.dest_threat_intelligences: A list of threat intelligence feeds to match against the destination IP address. If specified, the rule only applies to traffic destined to addresses associated with these threat intelligence lists.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.match.layer4_configs: A list of layer4 configurations specifying the IP protocol (e.g., tcp, udp, icmp) and optional destination port ranges that this rule matches.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.match.layer4_configs.ip_protocol: The IP protocol to match. Accepts protocol names like 'tcp', 'udp', 'icmp', 'esp', 'ah', 'ipip', 'sctp', or 'all', or a numeric IP protocol number.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.match.layer4_configs.ports: List of destination ports to match. Each entry can be a single port (e.g., '80') or a range (e.g., '1024-2048'). An empty list matches all ports.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.match.src_address_groups: Specifies the list of source address groups to match against the source IP of the traffic. Each string is the name or URL of an address group resource.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.match.src_fqdns: A list of source fully qualified domain names (FQDNs) that the firewall rule matches. Traffic originating from these FQDNs will match the rule.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.match.src_ip_ranges: List of source IP address ranges in CIDR notation that this firewall policy rule matches. If specified, traffic originating from these ranges is applied to the rule's action.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.match.src_network_context: The source network context to match for the firewall rule. Allowed values: INTERNET, INTRA_VPC, NON_INTERNET, UNSPECIFIED, VPC_NETWORKS.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.match.src_network_type: The source network type to which the firewall rule applies. Valid values are INTERNET, INTRA_VPC, NON_INTERNET, UNSPECIFIED, and VPC_NETWORKS.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.match.src_networks: The list of source network URLs (self-links of VPC networks) that the rule matches. Traffic originating from these networks is evaluated against the firewall policy rule.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.match.src_region_codes: List of source region codes from which traffic must originate for this rule to match. Region codes are strings such as 'us-central1' or 'europe-west1'.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.match.src_secure_tags: List of secure tags that the source of traffic must match for this firewall rule to apply.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.match.src_secure_tags.name: The full resource name of the tag value that defines the source secure tag for the firewall rule, in the format tagValues/{tag_value_id}.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.match.src_secure_tags.state: The state of the secure tag. Possible values are 'EFFECTIVE' (matches resources that have this tag) and 'INEFFECTIVE' (matches resources that do not have this tag).
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.match.src_threat_intelligences: A list of source threat intelligence names used to match against the source IP address of the traffic. This allows the rule to target traffic from IPs associated with known threat categories.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.priority: An integer specifying the evaluation priority of this rule. Lower values have higher priority; the valid range is 0 (highest priority) to 2147483647 (lowest priority).
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.rule_name: The name of the firewall policy rule. Must be unique within the firewall policy and is used to identify the rule.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.rule_tuple_count: The calculated number of tuples (source IP, destination IP, and layer-4 protocol/port combinations) that this rule must be expanded into for evaluation. This is a read-only value determined by the firewall policy backend.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.security_profile_group: Specifies the security profile group to apply to this firewall rule for threat prevention. The value is a full or partial URL of a security profile group resource.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.target_forwarding_rules: List of target forwarding rules (URLs or names) to which this firewall policy rule applies.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.target_resources: A list of target resource URLs (for example, instances or network endpoint groups) to which the firewall policy rule applies. When empty, the rule applies to all resources in the network.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.target_secure_tags: Specifies the secure tags (also known as network tags) attached to VM instances that this firewall policy rule targets. The rule applies to instances that have any of the listed tags; each object contains the 'name' of the secure tag.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.target_secure_tags.name: The name of the secure tag used to identify which resources the firewall rule targets.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.target_secure_tags.state: The state of the secure tag, either EFFECTIVE or INEFFECTIVE, indicating whether the tag is currently active in the firewall policy rule.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.target_service_accounts: List of service account email addresses that this rule applies to. Traffic from instances using one of these service accounts will be matched by the rule.
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.target_type: Specifies the type of target resources that the firewall rule applies to. Valid values are INSTANCES (applies to VM instances) and INTERNAL_MANAGED_LB (applies to internal managed load balancers).
google_compute_network_firewall_policie.rules.tls_inspect: Whether to enable TLS inspection for traffic matching this firewall policy rule. When set to true, the firewall will perform TLS inspection on the rule's matched traffic.

google_compute_node_group.autoscaling_policy: The autoscaling policy of the node group. This output-only field contains the configuration that determines how the node group automatically scales the number of nodes.
google_compute_node_group.fingerprint: The fingerprint of the node group, used for optimistic concurrency control. This is an output-only value generated by the server that changes whenever the node group is updated.
google_compute_node_group.share_settings.project_map.project_id: The Google Cloud project ID for which the share settings are configured in this project map entry.
google_compute_node_group.status: The current lifecycle state of the node group, computed by the provider. Possible values are CREATING, DELETING, INVALID, and READY.

google_compute_node_template.accelerators: A list of accelerator configurations (e.g., GPUs) for the node template. Each object specifies the accelerator type and count. This field is output-only, so it is populated by the API and reflects the actual accelerators associated with the node template.
google_compute_node_template.accelerators.accelerator_count: The number of accelerators of the specified type to attach to nodes created from this node template. This field is part of the accelerators block, which also specifies the accelerator type.
google_compute_node_template.accelerators.accelerator_type: The type of accelerator (GPU) to attach to the node, such as 'nvidia-tesla-a100'. This should be a valid accelerator type identifier supported by Compute Engine.
google_compute_node_template.disks: The list of local disk configurations associated with the node template. This is an output-only field computed by the API, containing the disk type and size for each local disk.
google_compute_node_template.disks.disk_count: The number of disks of the specified type to attach to the node template.
google_compute_node_template.disks.disk_type: The type of disk to attach to the node, such as 'local-ssd'. Defaults to 'local-ssd'.
google_compute_node_template.node_type_flexibility: Node type flexibility settings for the template, allowing the template to be used with a range of node types by specifying a CPU and memory range instead of a fixed node type.
google_compute_node_template.node_type_flexibility.cpus: The number of virtual CPUs to allocate for the node template. Provide a specific integer value as a string (e.g., "8") or use "any" to allow flexible selection based on available resources.
google_compute_node_template.node_type_flexibility.memory: Specifies the amount of memory (in MB) that the flexible node type must have. This is used to define a custom node type for the node template.
google_compute_node_template.server_binding: The server binding configuration of the node template, which controls how nodes are restarted during maintenance events. This field is output-only and reflects the binding type used by the template.
google_compute_node_template.server_binding.type: Specifies the server binding type for the node template, controlling whether the node can be restarted on any server or only on a minimal set of servers. Valid values are RESTART_NODE_ON_ANY_SERVER, RESTART_NODE_ON_MINIMAL_SERVERS, or SERVER_BINDING_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED.

google_compute_organization_security_pol.adaptive_protection_config.layer7_ddos_d: Specifies the confidence threshold (between 0.0 and 1.0) used to decide when Adaptive Protection automatically deploys a mitigation action against a potential DDoS attack.
The length of time in seconds that an automatically deployed adaptive protection mitigation stays active before expiring.
The threshold in requests per second that triggers auto-deploy when the baseline traffic is impacted. This is part of the Layer 7 DDoS defense adaptive protection configuration.

The load threshold in requests per second that triggers automatic deployment of mitigation actions. If traffic load exceeds this value, the adaptive protection system will automatically deploy protections.
Absolute requests-per-second (QPS) threshold that triggers detection of a DDoS attack in the adaptive protection configuration.
The detection load threshold in requests per second. When the traffic load exceeds this value for the associated traffic type, adaptive protection starts detecting potential DDoS attacks.
Detection threshold in queries per second (QPS), expressed as a multiple of the baseline QPS. For example, a value of 1.5 means the detection threshold is 1.5 times the baseline QPS.

A list of traffic granularity configurations for a threshold. Each configuration specifies a granularity type (e.g., SOURCE_IP or COOKIE) and the corresponding value. If not set, traffic granularity defaults to SOURCE_IP.

Whether to evaluate traffic thresholds separately for each unique value of the configured traffic granularity type. When enabled, each unique value is tracked individually; when disabled, traffic is aggregated.

Specifies the granularity type for traffic aggregation in the Layer 7 DDoS defense threshold configuration. Allowed values are HTTP_HEADER_HOST (aggregate by host header), HTTP_PATH (aggregate by request path), and UNSPECIFIED_TYPE (unspecified).
The value for the traffic granularity configuration, such as a specific IP address or user identifier that the threshold applies to.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.advanced_options_config.json_custom_conf: Custom configuration for JSON parsing in the security policy, including the list of content types to be parsed.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.advanced_options_config.json_parsing: Configures JSON payload parsing for the security policy. Allowed values: DISABLED (no JSON parsing), STANDARD (standard JSON parsing), and STANDARD_WITH_GRAPHQL (standard JSON parsing plus GraphQL support).
google_compute_organization_security_pol.advanced_options_config.log_level: The log level for the security policy, controlling the verbosity of logs. Allowed values are 'NORMAL' and 'VERBOSE'.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.associations.attachment_id: The ID of the folder or organization to which the security policy is attached.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.associations.display_name: The display name for the organization security policy association. This is a human-readable name used to identify the association.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.associations.excluded_folders: A list of folder IDs that are excluded from the association's scope.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.associations.excluded_projects: A list of project IDs that are excluded from this association. The organization security policy does not apply to the specified projects.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.associations.security_policy_id: The ID of the security policy that this association belongs to.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.associations.short_name: The short name of the project or folder that this organizational security policy is associated with.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.ddos_protection_config.ddos_adaptive_pro: Configures the adaptive protection mode for DDoS protection. Allowed values: DISABLED, ENABLED, PREVIEW, or UNSPECIFIED_ADAPTIVE_PROTECTION.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.ddos_protection_config.ddos_protection: Enables or configures DDoS protection for the security policy. Allowed values are ADVANCED, ADVANCED_PREVIEW, and STANDARD.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.recaptcha_options_config: Configuration for reCAPTCHA options in the security policy. It includes the enforcement mode and redirect site key used for reCAPTCHA verification.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.action: The action to take when a request matches this rule. Valid values are 'allow', 'deny', and 'goto_next'.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.header_action: The `header_action` block configures modifications to HTTP headers for requests that match the rule. It allows adding or removing request and response headers as defined in the policy.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.header_action.request_headers_to_a: A list of request headers to add to the request when the rule matches. Each object contains 'header_name' and 'header_value' fields specifying the header to insert.
The name of the request header that will be added to the request.
The value to be set for the header added to requests that match the rule.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.match: The match condition that defines which traffic this rule applies to, including source and destination IP ranges, protocols, and ports.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.match.config: The configuration block for the match. It specifies L4 network match criteria, such as source and destination IP ranges and layer 4 protocol/port settings.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.match.config.src_ip_ranges: A list of source IP address ranges in CIDR notation that the rule matches on.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.match.expr: The CEL (Common Expression Language) expression that defines the condition for when this rule matches traffic. This allows custom matching based on request attributes.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.match.expr.expression: The Common Expression Language (CEL) expression that defines which traffic matches this rule. It is evaluated against the request/response attributes to determine if the rule applies.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.match.expr.location: The location of the expression, such as 'global' or a specific GCP region. Defaults to 'global' if not set.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.match.expr.title: An optional title for the expression, providing a short summary of its purpose.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.match.expr_options: The `expr_options` block configures options for the expression used in the match condition. It can contain `recaptcha_options` to control how reCAPTCHA is handled for the rule.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.match.expr_options.recaptcha_optio: List of reCAPTCHA site keys used to verify action tokens for this security policy rule.
A list of site keys to be used during the validation of reCAPTCHA session tokens.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.match.versioned_expr: The version of the match expression syntax. The only supported value is SRC_IPS_V1, which indicates version 1 of the source IP expression format.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.network_match: The network_match block specifies the network-level match criteria for the rule, including source and destination IP ranges or networks that determine when the rule is applied.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.network_match.dest_ip_ranges: A list of destination IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR ranges to which this rule applies. Traffic destined for an IP address within these ranges will be matched.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.network_match.dest_ports: A list of destination port numbers or port ranges (e.g., '80' or '8000-8080') that the rule matches for network traffic.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.network_match.ip_protocols: A list of IP protocol types (e.g., 'tcp', 'udp', 'icmp') that this network match rule applies to.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.network_match.src_asns: A list of source autonomous system numbers (ASNs). The rule matches traffic that originates from any of the specified ASNs.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.network_match.src_ip_ranges: A list of source IP addresses in CIDR notation that the rule matches. If specified, the rule applies only to traffic originating from these IP ranges.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.network_match.src_ports: The list of source ports to match in the network match condition. Each entry is a string that can be a single port (e.g., '80') or a port range (e.g., '443-8443').
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.network_match.src_region_codes: Specifies the source region codes to match for traffic from specific geographic regions. The rule applies to traffic originating from the listed regions, using ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes (e.g., 'US', 'DE').
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.network_match.user_defined_fields: A list of user-defined fields to match against in the network match criteria. Each object typically contains a 'name' and a list of 'values', allowing custom matching beyond standard IP/port fields.
The name of the user-defined field, as defined in the organization security policy, used for matching network traffic.
The list of values to match against for the user-defined field. The rule applies when the field value is one of these strings.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.preconfigured_waf_config.exclusion: A list of exclusions that specify which request components (e.g., headers, cookies, query parameters) should be ignored when the preconfigured WAF rule is evaluated.
A list of request cookies that should not be checked by the preconfigured WAF rules.
The operator to apply for matching the cookie value. Valid values are: CONTAINS, ENDS_WITH, EQUALS, EQUALS_ANY, STARTS_WITH.
The exact value of the cookie to match for exclusion. If specified, only cookies with this value and the corresponding key are excluded; if omitted, all cookies with the specified key are excluded.
A list of request headers to exclude from evaluation by the preconfigured WAF rule. Each object in the list specifies a header that should be ignored.
The operator used to match the request header value to be excluded. Accepted values are: CONTAINS, ENDS_WITH, EQUALS, EQUALS_ANY, and STARTS_WITH.
The value of the request header to exclude from WAF evaluation. Pairs with the header name in the corresponding key field.
Specifies the request query parameters to exclude from the preconfigured WAF rule evaluation. Each item in the list identifies a query parameter to be excluded via a key and an operator.
The operator used to match the query parameter value for exclusion. Valid values are: CONTAINS, ENDS_WITH, EQUALS, EQUALS_ANY, STARTS_WITH.
The value of the query parameter to match for exclusion. If omitted, all values for the specified key are excluded.
A list of objects, each defining a request URI to exclude from the WAF rule evaluation. The excluded URIs will not be subject to the preconfigured WAF rule set.
The operator used to match the request URI to exclude. Allowed values are: CONTAINS, ENDS_WITH, EQUALS, EQUALS_ANY, and STARTS_WITH.
The request URI to exclude from the preconfigured WAF configuration.
A list of preconfigured WAF rule IDs that this exclusion targets. These rules will be exempt from the preconfigured WAF configuration.
The name of the preconfigured WAF rule set to which this exclusion applies, such as 'xss-v33-stable' or 'sqli-v33-stable'.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.preview: Whether the rule is in preview mode. When true, the rule is evaluated but not enforced.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.priority: An integer value that determines the relative priority of this rule. Lower numbers indicate higher priority and are evaluated first. Must be unique within the security policy.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.rate_limit_options: A block for configuring rate limiting on the security policy rule. It defines actions and thresholds for traffic that exceeds the configured rate limit.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.rate_limit_options.ban_duration_se: Specifies the duration in seconds that a client is banned after exceeding the rate limit threshold. This can only be set when the rule action is 'rate_based_ban'.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.rate_limit_options.ban_threshold: Threshold at which a client is banned for exceeding the rate limit, as defined within the rate limit options.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.rate_limit_options.ban_threshold.c: The number of requests that must occur within the specified interval to trigger a ban.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.rate_limit_options.ban_threshold.i: The time interval, in seconds, over which the request count is evaluated to determine if the ban threshold is exceeded.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.rate_limit_options.conform_action: The action to take when a request conforms to the rate limit. Valid values are 'allow' and 'deny'.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.rate_limit_options.enforce_on_key: The key type used for enforcing rate limits, determining how requests are grouped for rate limiting. Allowed values are: ALL, ASN, HTTP_COOKIE, HTTP_HEADER, HTTP_PATH, IP, REGION_CODE, SNI, TLS_JA3_FINGERPRINT, TLS_JA4_FINGERPRINT, USER_IP, XFF_IP.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.rate_limit_options.enforce_on_key_: A list of configurations for enforcing rate limits on specific keys. Each configuration specifies a key type (e.g., IP, HTTP_HEADER) and an optional name, enabling the rate limit to be applied based on different request attributes.
The name of the key to enforce the rate limit on, such as a header name or cookie name, depending on the configured key type.
Specifies the type of key used to identify clients for rate limiting. For example, IP enforces on client IP addresses, HTTP_HEADER on a specific HTTP header, and ASN on autonomous system numbers.
Name of the key to enforce rate limiting on, used when enforce_on_key is set to a value such as HTTP_HEADER.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.rate_limit_options.exceed_action: The action to take when the rate limit is exceeded. Valid values are 'deny' and 'redirect'.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.rate_limit_options.exceed_redirect: Defines the redirect behavior for requests that exceed the configured rate limit. This object specifies how to redirect traffic when the limit is surpassed.
The URL to redirect requests to when the rate limit is exceeded. Required if the redirect type is EXTERNAL_302.

The type of redirect to use when the rate limit is exceeded. Possible values are EXTERNAL_302 (redirect to an external URL via HTTP 302) and GOOGLE_RECAPTCHA (use Google reCAPTCHA to verify the user).
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.rate_limit_options.rate_limit_thre: An object that defines the threshold at which the rate limit rule is triggered, controlling when the rate limiting action is applied to traffic.
The number of requests allowed within the specified rate limit interval before the rate limit action is enforced.
The time interval, in seconds, for the rate limit threshold. This defines the window in which the 'count' of events is measured.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.redirect_options: Nested block that configures the redirect behavior for a security policy rule. It is used when the rule's action is set to redirect, specifying how requests should be redirected.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.redirect_options.target: The URL to redirect traffic to when the redirect type is EXTERNAL_302. This is required for EXTERNAL_302 type redirects.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.rules.redirect_options.type: The type of redirect. Valid values are EXTERNAL_302 (redirect to a custom external URL with HTTP 302) and GOOGLE_RECAPTCHA (redirect to Google reCAPTCHA).
google_compute_organization_security_pol.user_defined_fields.base: The base protocol or address family that the user-defined field applies to. Allowed values are IPV4, IPV6, TCP, and UDP.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.user_defined_fields.mask: The mask specifies the exact field or pattern to extract from the selected base, such as a specific HTTP header name when base is 'request.headers' or a cookie name when base is 'request.cookies'.
google_compute_organization_security_pol.user_defined_fields.offset: The byte offset from the base of the field. Specifies the start position of the user-defined field relative to the base (e.g., REQUEST).
google_compute_organization_security_pol.user_defined_fields.size: The size of the user-defined field in bytes.

google_compute_packet_mirroring.collector_ilb: The internal load balancer (ILB) used as the collector for mirrored traffic. This output-only field identifies the forwarding rule that receives mirrored packets.
google_compute_packet_mirroring.filter: The filter configuration as returned by the API (output only). It defines the criteria that determine which packets are mirrored.
google_compute_packet_mirroring.mirrored_resources: An object defining the instances, subnetworks, or tags whose traffic is mirrored. This field is output-only and reflects the effective mirroring configuration.
google_compute_packet_mirroring.mirrored_resources.instances.canonical_u: Canonical URL of the Compute Engine instance that will have its traffic mirrored. This is the self_link of the instance.
google_compute_packet_mirroring.mirrored_resources.instances.url: The URL of the Compute Engine instance to mirror. This is typically the full self-link of the instance.
google_compute_packet_mirroring.mirrored_resources.subnetworks.canonical: The canonical URL of the subnetwork whose traffic is mirrored.
google_compute_packet_mirroring.mirrored_resources.subnetworks.url: The URL of the subnetwork that this mirroring rule applies to.
google_compute_packet_mirroring.network: The network that the packet mirroring applies to. This field is output-only and contains the URL of the VPC network.

google_compute_public_advertised_prefixe.public_delegated_prefixs.ip_range: The IP address range of the public delegated prefix, expressed in CIDR notation.
google_compute_public_advertised_prefixe.public_delegated_prefixs.project: The project ID where the public delegated prefix is created, allowing the public advertised prefix to be shared with a different project.
google_compute_public_advertised_prefixe.public_delegated_prefixs.region: The region where this delegated prefix is located.

google_compute_public_delegated_prefixe.public_delegated_sub_prefixs.allocatable: The prefix length (in bits) of the sub-prefixes that can be allocated from this delegated sub-prefix. For instance, a value of 26 indicates that /26 CIDR blocks can be allocated.
google_compute_public_delegated_prefixe.public_delegated_sub_prefixs.delegatee_p: The project ID or name to which this sub-prefix is delegated, allowing that project to use the delegated prefix.
google_compute_public_delegated_prefixe.public_delegated_sub_prefixs.ip_cidr_ran: The IP CIDR range of this public delegated sub-prefix.
google_compute_public_delegated_prefixe.public_delegated_sub_prefixs.ipv6_access: The access type for the IPv6 addresses in the sub-prefix. EXTERNAL means the prefix is used for publicly accessible IPv6 addresses, while INTERNAL means it is used for internal/private IPv6 addresses.
google_compute_public_delegated_prefixe.public_delegated_sub_prefixs.is_address: Specifies whether the sub-prefix is an address range (true) or a public delegated prefix (false).
google_compute_public_delegated_prefixe.public_delegated_sub_prefixs.mode: The mode of the sub-prefix, indicating how it is used. Allowed values are: DELEGATION, EXTERNAL_IPV6_FORWARDING_RULE_CREATION, EXTERNAL_IPV6_SUBNETWORK_CREATION, and INTERNAL_IPV6_SUBNETWORK_CREATION.
google_compute_public_delegated_prefixe.public_delegated_sub_prefixs.name: The name of the public delegated sub-prefix. This is used as an identifier for the sub-prefix within the public delegated prefix.
google_compute_public_delegated_prefixe.public_delegated_sub_prefixs.region: The region of the sub-prefix. If not specified, the region of the parent public delegated prefix is used.
google_compute_public_delegated_prefixe.public_delegated_sub_prefixs.status: The status of the public delegated sub-prefix, which can be either ACTIVE or INACTIVE.

google_compute_region_autoscaler.autoscaling_policy.custom_metric_utiliza: A filter string that selects which time series (resources) contribute to the metric for autoscaling decisions, applied using the Cloud Monitoring API syntax.
The name of the metric to use for autoscaling. This corresponds to the Cloud Monitoring metric identifier, typically in the form 'custom.googleapis.com/[metric_name]'.
The number of instances used to calculate the custom metric utilization. If omitted, the metric is calculated across all instances in the group.
The target value for the custom metric that the autoscaler aims to maintain. When the metric value exceeds or falls below this target, the autoscaler adjusts the number of instances accordingly.
Specifies the type of utilization target for the custom metric: GAUGE for instantaneous values, DELTA_PER_MINUTE for the rate per minute, or DELTA_PER_SECOND for the rate per second.
google_compute_region_autoscaler.autoscaling_policy.scaling_schedules.des: An optional description of this scaling schedule.
google_compute_region_autoscaler.autoscaling_policy.scaling_schedules.dis: Whether the scaling schedule is disabled. When set to true, the autoscaler does not apply this schedule. Defaults to false.
google_compute_region_autoscaler.autoscaling_policy.scaling_schedules.dur: The duration of the scaling schedule in seconds. After the scheduled start time (defined by the cron expression in the 'schedule' field), the scaling parameters are applied for this length of time.
google_compute_region_autoscaler.autoscaling_policy.scaling_schedules.min: The minimum number of replicas that must be running during the scheduled time period. This value is used by the autoscaler to ensure capacity during the schedule.
google_compute_region_autoscaler.autoscaling_policy.scaling_schedules.sch: A cron-style schedule string that specifies when the autoscaling policy's scaling schedule takes effect (e.g., '0 9 * * *' means daily at 09:00).
google_compute_region_autoscaler.autoscaling_policy.scaling_schedules.tim: The time zone to use for the scaling schedule, specified as a string from the IANA time zone database (e.g., "UTC", "America/New_York"). This determines how the schedule's start time and duration are interpreted.
google_compute_region_autoscaler.scaling_schedule_status.last_start_time: The last time the scaling schedule started, in RFC3339 UTC format.
google_compute_region_autoscaler.scaling_schedule_status.next_start_time: The next time this scaling schedule is scheduled to become active, in RFC3339 timestamp format.
google_compute_region_autoscaler.scaling_schedule_status.state: The current state of the scaling schedule. Valid values are `ACTIVE` (schedule is active and will be used for autoscaling) and `OBSOLETE` (schedule is no longer active, e.g., due to expiration or deletion).
google_compute_region_autoscaler.status_details.message: The human-readable message describing the status detail, typically containing information about an error or warning condition.
google_compute_region_autoscaler.status_details.type: The type of the autoscaler status detail, indicating a specific condition or reason for the current scaling state. Possible values are: ALL_INSTANCES_UNHEALTHY, BACKEND_SERVICE_DOES_NOT_EXIST, CAPPED_AT_MAX_NUM_REPLICAS, CUSTOM_METRIC_DATA_POINTS_TOO_SPARSE, CUSTOM_METRIC_INVALID, MIN_EQUALS_MAX, MISSING_CUSTOM_METRIC_DATA_POINTS, MISSING_LOAD_BALANCING_DATA_POINTS, MODE_OFF, MODE_ONLY_SCALE_OUT, MODE_ONLY_UP, MORE_THAN_ONE_BACKEND_SERVICE, NOT_ENOUGH_QUOTA_AVAILABLE, REGION_RESOURCE_STOCKOUT, SCALING_TARGET_DOES_NOT_EXIST, SCHEDULED_INSTANCES_GREATER_THAN_AUTOSCALER_MAX, SCHEDULED_INSTANCES_LESS_THAN_AUTOSCALER_MIN, UNKNOWN, UNSUPPORTED_MAX_RATE_LOAD_BALANCING_CONFIGURATION, ZONE_RESOURCE_STOCKOUT.

google_compute_region_backend_bucket.cdn_policy.bypass_cache_on_request_heade: The name of the request header to match. If this header is present in a request, the CDN bypasses the cache for that request.
google_compute_region_backend_bucket.cdn_policy.negative_caching_policy.code: The HTTP status code for which the negative caching TTL applies. This defines which response status codes will be cached negatively with the specified TTL.
google_compute_region_backend_bucket.cdn_policy.negative_caching_policy.ttl: The TTL (in seconds) for caching responses with the corresponding status code.
google_compute_region_backend_bucket.used_by.reference: The URL of the resource that is currently using this backend bucket. This is the full reference to the using resource, such as a URL map or load balancer.

google_compute_region_backend_service.backends.balancing_mode: Defines the balancing mode for this backend, determining how capacity is measured. Allowed values are: CONNECTION (active connections), CUSTOM_METRICS (custom metric-based), IN_FLIGHT (in-flight requests), RATE (requests per second), and UTILIZATION (CPU utilization).
google_compute_region_backend_service.backends.capacity_scaler: A multiplier applied to the backend's service capacity to adjust its weight relative to other backends. Defaults to 1.
google_compute_region_backend_service.backends.custom_metrics: Custom metrics for backend load balancing, used when the backend's balancing_mode is set to 'CUSTOM'. Each object specifies the metric name and optional maximum rate.
google_compute_region_backend_service.backends.custom_metrics.dry_run: If true, the metric is only used for observation; it will not affect load balancing. Defaults to false.
google_compute_region_backend_service.backends.custom_metrics.max_utilization: The maximum utilization for the custom metric, as a fractional value (0.0 to 1.0). This is used to normalize the custom metric value for load balancing when the backend's balancing mode is CUSTOM_METRIC.
google_compute_region_backend_service.backends.custom_metrics.name: The name of the custom metric to use for this backend. This should match the name of a metric defined in the backend service's custom metrics configuration.
google_compute_region_backend_service.backends.failover: Specifies whether this backend is a failover backend. If true, the backend is used only when the primary (non-failover) backends become unhealthy.
google_compute_region_backend_service.backends.group: The fully qualified URL of the instance group or network endpoint group (NEG) that serves as the backend for this region backend service. This is typically the self_link of the resource.
google_compute_region_backend_service.backends.max_connections: The maximum number of simultaneous connections to this backend. This is only used when the balancing mode is CONNECTION.
google_compute_region_backend_service.backends.max_connections_per_endpoint: The maximum number of simultaneous connections that can be established to a single backend endpoint (IP:port). When set, the backend service enforces this limit per endpoint, and traffic is not routed to endpoints that have reached the limit.
google_compute_region_backend_service.backends.max_connections_per_instance: The maximum number of connections per backend instance. This field is only applicable when the backend's balancingMode is 'CONNECTION'.
google_compute_region_backend_service.backends.max_in_flight_requests: The maximum number of in-flight requests that can be sent to the backend at any given time.
google_compute_region_backend_service.backends.max_in_flight_requests_per_endp: The maximum number of outstanding (concurrent) requests that the load balancer forwards to a single backend endpoint. A value of 0 disables the limit.
google_compute_region_backend_service.backends.max_in_flight_requests_per_inst: The maximum number of outstanding requests that a single backend instance can handle. If not set, the default is 0, which means unlimited.
google_compute_region_backend_service.backends.max_rate: The maximum number of requests per second (RPS) that this backend group can handle. This is used when the backend's balancing mode is set to RATE to cap the total traffic sent to this backend.
google_compute_region_backend_service.backends.max_rate_per_endpoint: Maximum requests per second that each individual endpoint (e.g., instance or network endpoint) in the backend is allowed to serve. Used when the backend's balancing mode is RATE and the backend is backed by a network endpoint group (NEG).
google_compute_region_backend_service.backends.max_rate_per_instance: Upper bound for the number of requests per second that can be sent to an instance in this backend. This must be set when the balancing mode is RATE.
google_compute_region_backend_service.backends.max_utilization: The maximum utilization of the backend, expressed as a fraction between 0.0 and 1.0. When the utilization exceeds this value, the load balancer stops sending new requests to the backend.
google_compute_region_backend_service.backends.orchestration_info: Configures the orchestration settings for this backend. Requires that the backend is a network endpoint group (NEG) and specifies the name of the orchestration it belongs to.
google_compute_region_backend_service.backends.preference: The preference for this backend, indicating whether it should be used preferentially over other backends in the backend service. Valid values are DEFAULT (normal preference), PREFERENCE_UNSPECIFIED (no preference), and PREFERRED (traffic is preferentially routed to this backend).
google_compute_region_backend_service.cdn_policy.bypass_cache_on_request_heade: The name of the request header that triggers cache bypass when present in a request.
google_compute_region_backend_service.cdn_policy.negative_caching_policy.code: The HTTP status code that will trigger negative caching for this policy. For example, 404 or 500.
google_compute_region_backend_service.cdn_policy.negative_caching_policy.ttl: The time-to-live (TTL) in seconds for the CDN to cache a negative response (e.g., an HTTP error status code) specified in this policy entry.
google_compute_region_backend_service.custom_metrics.dry_run: If set to true, this metric is used only for logging and not for load balancing decisions.
google_compute_region_backend_service.ha_policy.leader: The leader election configuration for the backend service's high availability policy. It specifies how a leader instance is selected among the backend instances.
google_compute_region_backend_service.ha_policy.leader.network_endpoint: The network endpoint that is designated as the leader in the high availability policy. It identifies the backend endpoint that will act as the leader for the regional backend service.
google_compute_region_backend_service.locality_lb_policies.custom_policy: The custom policy configuration for this locality's load balancing. It allows specifying a user-defined (custom) load balancing policy in place of a predefined one.
google_compute_region_backend_service.locality_lb_policies.custom_policy.data: The optional data to be passed to the custom policy. This is a JSON-encoded string containing the policy configuration.
google_compute_region_backend_service.locality_lb_policies.custom_policy.name: The name of the custom policy used for locality load balancing in the backend service.
google_compute_region_backend_service.locality_lb_policies.policy: The load balancing policy for this locality, including the policy type and any type-specific configuration.
google_compute_region_backend_service.locality_lb_policies.policy.name: The load balancing policy to use. Allowed values: INVALID_LB_POLICY, LEAST_REQUEST, MAGLEV, ORIGINAL_DESTINATION, RANDOM, RING_HASH, ROUND_ROBIN, WEIGHTED_GCP_RENDEZVOUS, WEIGHTED_MAGLEV, WEIGHTED_ROUND_ROBIN.
The name of the HTTP request header to include in logs.
google_compute_region_backend_service.log_config.logging_http_response_headers: The name of an HTTP response header to include in the logs.
google_compute_region_backend_service.network_pass_through_lb_traffic_policy.z: Configuration for zonal affinity in the traffic policy. When enabled, the load balancer prefers backends in the same zone as the client, reducing cross-zone traffic.
google_compute_region_backend_service.subsetting.policy: The subsetting policy for the backend service. Valid values are 'CONSISTENT_HASH_SUBSETTING' and 'NONE'.
google_compute_region_backend_service.tls_settings: TLS settings for the backend service. This field is only relevant if the load balancing scheme is INTERNAL_MANAGED.
google_compute_region_backend_service.tls_settings.subject_alt_names.dns_name: The DNS name to include as a subject alternative name (SAN) for TLS certificate validation against the backend service.
google_compute_region_backend_service.tls_settings.subject_alt_names.uniform_r: A Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) to include as a subject alternative name (SAN) in the TLS certificate. This is used to match the backend service's identity against a URI, such as a SPIFFE ID or other URI-based identity.
google_compute_region_backend_service.used_by.reference: The full URL of the resource that references (uses) this backend service.

google_compute_region_commitment.existing_reservations: The list of existing reservations that are automatically included in this region commitment. This field is output-only and is determined by Google Cloud based on the commitment's resources.
google_compute_region_commitment.reservations.advanced_deployment_control: The operational mode for the reservation. Valid values are ALL_CAPACITY (all capacity is provisioned immediately), HIGHLY_AVAILABLE_CAPACITY (capacity is distributed to support high availability), and RESERVATION_OPERATIONAL_MODE_UNSPECIFIED (mode not set, defaults to ALL_CAPACITY).
google_compute_region_commitment.reservations.aggregate_reservation: The aggregate reservation configuration, used to reserve capacity for a pool of resources (such as CPU and memory) without specifying exact instance shapes. It includes a VM family and a list of reserved resource types with counts, offering flexible capacity reservation for a group of instances.
google_compute_region_commitment.reservations.aggregate_reservation.in_us: Specifies the type of accelerator (GPU) used by the resources currently in use within the aggregate reservation. This value corresponds to the acceleratorType in the machine type, such as 'nvidia-tesla-t4'.
google_compute_region_commitment.reservations.aggregate_reservation.reser: Specifies the resources included in this aggregate reservation. Each entry defines a resource type and the amount to reserve.
The accelerator block specifies the type and count of accelerators to reserve in the aggregate reservation. It includes fields for the accelerator type and the number of accelerators.
The number of accelerators of the specified type to reserve in this resource reservation.
The type of accelerator (e.g., GPU) to reserve in the aggregate reservation.
google_compute_region_commitment.reservations.aggregate_reservation.vm_fa: The family of TPU VMs to reserve capacity for. Valid values include VM_FAMILY_CLOUD_TPU_DEVICE_CT3, VM_FAMILY_CLOUD_TPU_LITE_DEVICE_CT5L, VM_FAMILY_CLOUD_TPU_LITE_POD_SLICE_CT5LP, VM_FAMILY_CLOUD_TPU_LITE_POD_SLICE_CT6E, VM_FAMILY_CLOUD_TPU_POD_SLICE_CT3P, VM_FAMILY_CLOUD_TPU_POD_SLICE_CT4P, VM_FAMILY_CLOUD_TPU_POD_SLICE_CT5P, and VM_FAMILY_CLOUD_TPU_POD_SLICE_TPU7X.
google_compute_region_commitment.reservations.aggregate_reservation.workl: The workload type of the aggregate reservation. Valid values are BATCH, SERVING, or UNSPECIFIED. This determines how the reservation is used for batch or serving workloads.
google_compute_region_commitment.reservations.confidential_compute_type: Specifies the confidential computing type for the reservation. Valid values are CONFIDENTIAL_COMPUTE_TYPE_TDX (for Intel TDX) and CONFIDENTIAL_COMPUTE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED (default, unspecified).
google_compute_region_commitment.reservations.creation_timestamp: Creation timestamp in RFC3339 text format.
google_compute_region_commitment.reservations.delete_after_duration: A duration (seconds and optional nanos) after which the reservation is automatically deleted. If unset, the reservation persists until the commitment ends.
google_compute_region_commitment.reservations.delete_after_duration.nanos: The duration's sub-second component in nanoseconds, ranging from 0 to 999,999,999.
google_compute_region_commitment.reservations.delete_after_duration.secon: The number of seconds in the duration after which the reservation is automatically deleted. Must be a string representation of an integer from 0 to 315,576,000,000 inclusive.
google_compute_region_commitment.reservations.delete_at_time: The time at which the reservation will be automatically deleted, in RFC3339 format.
google_compute_region_commitment.reservations.deployment_type: The deployment type for this reservation. Allowed values are DENSE and DEPLOYMENT_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED.
google_compute_region_commitment.reservations.early_access_maintenance: Specifies the early access mode for maintenance events on this reservation. Valid values are NO_EARLY_ACCESS, WAVE1, and WAVE2, indicating no early access, first wave, or second wave, respectively.
google_compute_region_commitment.reservations.enable_emergent_maintenance: Whether the reservation can be consumed by emergent maintenance requests.
google_compute_region_commitment.reservations.kind: The type of the resource. Always 'compute#reservation' for this resource.
google_compute_region_commitment.reservations.linked_commitments: List of self_links of commitments linked to this reservation. This is used to associate the reservation with one or more commitments so that the commitment's discounts apply to the reserved capacity.
google_compute_region_commitment.reservations.params.resource_manager_tag: Resource manager tags to be bound to the instances created from this reservation. A map of tag key-value pairs, where the value may be an empty string for a tag with only a key.
google_compute_region_commitment.reservations.protection_tier: The protection tier for the reservation, which determines the level of capacity protection. Valid values are `STANDARD`, `CAPACITY_OPTIMIZED`, and `PROTECTION_TIER_UNSPECIFIED` (the latter is the default when unspecified).
Specifies the sharing type for this reservation, controlling which services can use it. ALLOW_ALL permits all services, DISALLOW_ALL blocks all services, and SERVICE_SHARE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED is the default unspecified value.
google_compute_region_commitment.reservations.resource_status.health_info: The number of blocks that are degraded in the resource, as reported in its health information. This value indicates the extent of storage degradation for the resource.
The health status of the resource. Possible values: DEGRADED, HEALTHY, HEALTH_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED.
The number of healthy blocks in the reservation's resource health status.
google_compute_region_commitment.reservations.resource_status.reservation: The number of capacity blocks that this reservation uses.

An object that provides the maintenance status details for the reservation, as part of the reservation's resource status. This is a computed field reflecting the current maintenance state of the reservation.
The number of instances in the reservation that are currently undergoing maintenance, as reported in the reservation maintenance status.
The number of instances in this reservation that have maintenance pending.
The number of resources within this reservation that are currently undergoing maintenance.
The number of instances in this reservation that have a pending maintenance event.

The maintenance scheduling type for the reservation. Possible values are: 'GROUPED' (maintenance is grouped for the reservation), 'INDEPENDENT' (maintenance is handled independently), and 'GROUP_MAINTENANCE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED' (the type is not specified).
The number of ongoing maintenance operations for the subblock infrastructure within the reservation.
The number of pending maintenance items for the subblock infrastructure, as reported in the reservation maintenance status.
Upcoming maintenance information for the entire reservation group, shown in the resource status.
Indicates whether the upcoming group maintenance event can be rescheduled.
The latest time at which the upcoming group maintenance window can start, as reported for this reservation's resource status.
The maintenance status of the upcoming group maintenance, indicating whether it is ONGOING, PENDING, or UNKNOWN.
The type of upcoming maintenance for the reservation group. Possible values are: MULTIPLE, SCHEDULED, UNKNOWN_TYPE, UNSCHEDULED.
The end time of the maintenance window for the upcoming group maintenance event, expressed as a timestamp string.
The start time of the maintenance window for an upcoming maintenance event on the reservation, as a timestamp.
google_compute_region_commitment.reservations.resource_status.specific_sk: The ID of the instance template used to specify the machine type and other properties for this specific SKU allocation in the reservation.
The utilization of the specific SKU reservation, keyed by resource type (e.g., memory). Each value is a fraction of the total capacity of that resource.
google_compute_region_commitment.reservations.satisfies_pzs: Whether this reservation satisfies the requirements for physical zone separation (PZS) for sole-tenant node groups.
google_compute_region_commitment.reservations.scheduling_type: The scheduling type of the reservation. Possible values: INDEPENDENT (reserves capacity for standalone instances), GROUPED (reserves capacity for a group of instances, typically used with managed instance groups), and GROUP_MAINTENANCE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED (the scheduling type is not specified).
google_compute_region_commitment.reservations.share_settings: Configuration for sharing a reservation with other projects. It specifies the share type (LOCAL or SPECIFIC_PROJECTS) and, for SPECIFIC_PROJECTS, the set of projects that can use the reservation.
google_compute_region_commitment.reservations.share_settings.project_map: A map of project IDs to project-specific configuration, used to specify which projects can share this commitment's reservations as part of the sharing settings.
The ID of the Google Cloud project that has shared access to the commitment reservation. This is the key for the project_map entry.
google_compute_region_commitment.reservations.share_settings.share_type: Defines the sharing type for this reservation. Allowed values are: LOCAL (only within the owning project), SPECIFIC_PROJECTS (shared with a list of specific projects), ORGANIZATION (shared with all projects in the organization), and SHARE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED (default, indicating the field is not set).
google_compute_region_commitment.reservations.specific_reservation: Configuration for a specific reservation within the commitment. This block specifies the instance count and instance properties (such as machine type and GPUs) for reserved VMs, which are dedicated to a single project.
google_compute_region_commitment.reservations.specific_reservation.assure: The number of virtual machine instances that are guaranteed to be available in this specific reservation. This value must be less than or equal to the total 'count' of the reservation.
google_compute_region_commitment.reservations.specific_reservation.count: The number of virtual machine instances to reserve in the specific reservation. The value must be a positive integer.
google_compute_region_commitment.reservations.specific_reservation.in_use: Number of reserved instances from this specific reservation that are currently in use.
google_compute_region_commitment.reservations.specific_reservation.instan: The properties of the virtual machines to be reserved in this specific reservation, including machine type, minimum CPU platform, accelerator configuration, and local SSD count.
A list of guest accelerator (GPU) configurations to attach to instances created from this reservation. Each object defines an accelerator type and the number of accelerators.
The number of guest accelerators of the type specified by `accelerator_type` to attach to each instance in the reservation.
The type of GPU accelerator to attach, such as 'nvidia-tesla-t4' or 'nvidia-tesla-p100'. This is specified in the guest accelerator configuration for the instance properties.
A list of local SSD configurations to attach to instances in this specific reservation.
The size of the local SSD disk in gigabytes (GB), expressed as a string.
The interface type for the local SSD. Supported values are `NVME` and `SCSI`.
Optional location hint for the reserved instances, used by Compute Engine to optimize physical placement.
Specifies the machine type for the VM instances in this specific reservation.

Specifies the minimum CPU platform allowed for VM instances in the specific reservation. The value must be a valid CPU platform name (e.g., 'Intel Skylake' or 'AMD Milan') and instances will be guaranteed to use a CPU platform at least as recent as the specified one.
google_compute_region_commitment.reservations.specific_reservation.source: The self-link of an instance template that defines the properties of the instances to be reserved. When specified, the specific reservation is created based on the template's configuration.
google_compute_region_commitment.reservations.specific_reservation_requir: Indicates whether the reservation is a specific reservation (for a specific instance type) or a non-specific reservation (for an instance family). When true, the reservation is specific; when false, it is non-specific.
google_compute_region_commitment.reservations.status: The current status of the reservation, indicating its lifecycle state. Possible values are CREATING, DELETING, INVALID, READY, and UPDATING.
google_compute_region_commitment.reservations.zone: The zone in which the reservation is created, within the commitment's region.
google_compute_region_commitment.resources.accelerator_type: The type of accelerator (GPU) to include in the commitment, e.g., 'nvidia-tesla-v100'. Must be a valid accelerator type available in the region.
google_compute_region_commitment.resources.amount: The quantity of the resource type (e.g., VCPU, MEMORY) to reserve in the commitment.
google_compute_region_commitment.resources.type: The type of resource to commit to. Allowed values are `VCPU`, `MEMORY`, `LOCAL_SSD`, `ACCELERATOR`, and `UNSPECIFIED`.

google_compute_region_disk.async_primary_disk: The async_primary_disk object holds the reference to the primary disk in an asynchronous replication configuration. This field is computed and output-only, reflecting the primary disk associated with this regional disk.
google_compute_region_disk.async_secondary_disks.async_replication_: The URL or name of a resource policy defining a consistency group for the secondary disk. This groups multiple disks to ensure consistent replication.
The ID of the consistency group policy that governs this async replication disk. This policy groups multiple disks to ensure that their replicas are created with point-in-time consistency.
The URL of the secondary disk used for asynchronous replication. This should be a full or partial URL pointing to the disk resource.
The identifier of the secondary disk used for asynchronous replication.
google_compute_region_disk.disk_encryption_key: The disk encryption key for the regional persistent disk. This field is computed and output-only, meaning it is populated by the cloud provider when the disk is created or imported, and it contains the details of the encryption key used to protect the disk's contents.
google_compute_region_disk.guest_os_features.type: The type of guest OS feature to enable on the disk. Valid values include BARE_METAL_LINUX_COMPATIBLE, CCA_CAPABLE, GVNIC, IDPF, MULTI_IP_SUBNET, SECURE_BOOT, SEV_CAPABLE, SEV_LIVE_MIGRATABLE, SEV_LIVE_MIGRATABLE_V2, SEV_SNP_CAPABLE, SNP_SVSM_CAPABLE, TDX_CAPABLE, UEFI_COMPATIBLE, VIRTIO_SCSI_MULTIQUEUE, and WINDOWS.
google_compute_region_disk.resource_status.async_primary_disk: The primary disk in an asynchronous replication configuration. This object contains the URL of the source regional persistent disk for the replication.
google_compute_region_disk.resource_status.async_primary_disk.state: The current state of the asynchronous primary disk, which can be one of the following: ACTIVE, CREATED, STARTING, STATE_UNSPECIFIED, STOPPED, or STOPPING.
google_compute_region_disk.resource_status.async_secondary_disks.st: The current lifecycle state of the async secondary disk, reflecting its replication status.
google_compute_region_disk.source_image_encryption_key: The customer-supplied encryption key for the source image used to create this disk. This field is computed and output only, reporting the encryption key details when the source image was encrypted with a customer-supplied key.
google_compute_region_disk.source_snapshot_encryption_key: The source snapshot's encryption key, used when creating a region disk from an encrypted snapshot. This field is computed and output-only, providing the key details of the source snapshot as returned by the API.

google_compute_region_health_check.grpc_health_check: The gRPC health check configuration for this region health check. This field is output only, meaning it reflects the effective gRPC health check settings as determined by the Google Cloud API.
google_compute_region_health_check.http2_health_check: The computed HTTP/2 health check configuration for this region health check. This field is output-only and is present when the health check is configured to use HTTP/2.
google_compute_region_health_check.http_health_check: Configuration block for HTTP health check parameters. This includes settings such as the port to check, the request path, and expected response behavior. Only one health check type block may be specified within a region health check resource.
google_compute_region_health_check.https_health_check: The configuration block for an HTTPS health check. This field is computed and contains the settings that define the HTTPS health check for this regional health check.
google_compute_region_health_check.ssl_health_check: The SSL health check configuration. This field is present when the health check type is SSL and contains SSL-specific settings. It is computed by the API and output-only.
google_compute_region_health_check.tcp_health_check: The TCP health check configuration. This computed, output-only field provides the current TCP health check parameters (such as port and probe settings) for the region health check, as configured via the TCP health check type.

google_compute_region_instance_group_man.all_instances_config: The computed configuration applied to all instances in this regional instance group manager. This field is output-only and reflects the current all-instances configuration.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.auto_healing_policies.health_check: The health check resource URL (self-link) that determines instance health for auto-healing. Can be specified as a full URL, a self-link, or a name reference.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.auto_healing_policies.initial_delay_sec: The initial delay, in seconds, before an instance is considered available for auto-healing. This is the time to wait after an instance is created or restarted before checking its health for auto-healing purposes.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.current_actions: The current actions on instances in the group, providing counts of pending operations (e.g., creating, deleting, restarting, recreating). This is a computed attribute that reflects the live state of the managed instance group.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.distribution_policy: The distribution policy for the regional instance group manager, defining how instances are distributed across zones in the region.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.distribution_policy.zones.zone: Specifies the zone to which instances are distributed as part of the distribution policy for this regional managed instance group.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.instance_flexibility_policy.instance_sel: List of machine types that can be used for this instance selection. The instance group manager can choose any of these types when provisioning instances according to the flexibility policy.
The priority rank of this instance selection, where lower numbers have higher priority. Must be between 0 and 5.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.instance_lifecycle_policy: The lifecycle policy that determines how the managed instance group handles instance failures, including whether to restart or replace instances. This field is computed and output-only, reflecting the effective policy applied to the group.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.named_ports.name: The symbolic name of the named port, which acts as the key in the named port mapping to a port number.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.named_ports.port: The port number for this named port.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.resource_policies: The resource policies attached to the instances in this regional managed instance group. This field is output-only and reflects the current policies applied to the group's instances.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.standby_policy: The standby policy for the managed instance group, which defines settings for standby instances, such as the initial delay before a standby instance is stopped. This field is output-only and populated by the Google Compute Engine API.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.stateful_policy: The stateful policy configuration for the regional instance group manager. This optional block defines which disks and metadata are preserved for instances during group operations such as Rolling Update or Instance Regeneration.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.stateful_policy.preserved_state.disks.au: Specifies whether the stateful disk should be automatically deleted when the instance is deleted. Accepts 'true' or 'false'.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.stateful_policy.preserved_state.external: Controls whether the associated external IP is automatically deleted when the instance is deleted, or whether it is preserved. In a stateful preserved state configuration, this determines the lifecycle of the external IP for the instance.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.stateful_policy.preserved_state.internal: Controls whether the internal IP address is automatically deleted when its managed instance is deleted. Set to 'true' to delete the IP address automatically, or 'false' to preserve it for reuse.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.status: The current status of the managed instance group, including stability and the state of managed instances. This is a computed field that provides read-only information about the group's runtime state.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.status.all_instances_config: The status of the all-instances configuration for this regional instance group manager, including the fingerprint and the current state of the configuration applied to all instances.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.status.applied_accelerator_topologies.ac: The accelerator topology currently applied to this regional instance group manager. This may differ from the topology specified in the instance template, as it reflects the actual state.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.status.applied_accelerator_topologies.st: The current state of the accelerator topology applied to the instance group. Possible values are: ACTIVATING, ACTIVE, DEACTIVATING, FAILED, INCOMPLETE, and REACTIVATING.
The error object contains details about a failure that occurred while applying an accelerator topology to the instance group, including the error code and message.
A list of errors that occurred while applying accelerator topologies to the instance group. Each error object contains a code and message describing the failure.
A list of objects containing detailed information about the errors that occurred while applying accelerator topologies to the instance group.

google_compute_region_instance_group_man.status.stateful.per_instance_configs: A list of statuses for each per-instance configuration in the regional instance group manager, containing the configuration ID and its current state.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.status.version_target: A map of version names to the target number of instances for each version in the regional instance group manager. This indicates the intended distribution of instances among the configured versions.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.target_size_policy: The target_size_policy block defines the scaling limits for the managed instance group, specifying the minimum and maximum number of instances. This field is computed when not explicitly set, and the API determines the effective policy.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.update_policy: The update policy for the managed instance group, defining how instances are updated (e.g., rolling updates). This field is computed and reflects the current policy applied by the API.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.versions.instance_template: The URL (self_link) of the instance template that defines the configuration for this version of the managed instance group. This template is used to create instances when the group scales or updates to this version.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.versions.target_size: The target size for this version, specified either as a fixed number of instances or as a percentage of the group's total size. This controls how many instances are assigned to this version when using multiple versions.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.versions.target_size.calculated: The number of instances that are created from this version based on the autoscaler's calculated capacity. This value is computed automatically and cannot be set.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.versions.target_size.fixed: The fixed number of instances that this version should maintain. This is used when specifying a non-percentage target size.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.versions.target_size.percent: The percentage of instances in the group that should be running this version. Must be between 0 and 100. Only valid when updating the group.

google_compute_region_instance_group_man.instances.fingerprint: The fingerprint of the instance used for optimistic concurrency control, ensuring the instance hasn't changed since it was last read.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.instances.preserved_state: Configuration for preserving instance state during a resize operation, such as metadata and disk settings.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.instances.preserved_state.disks: Map of disk names to preserved disk state. Each key is the disk name, and the value is an object specifying the source of the disk and optionally the disk mode (READ_ONLY or READ_WRITE).
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.instances.preserved_state.disks.auto_del: Indicates whether the disk is automatically deleted when the instance is deleted (true) or preserved (false).
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.instances.preserved_state.disks.mode: The mode of a preserved disk, indicating whether the disk is attached in read-only or read-write mode. Acceptable values are 'READ_WRITE' and 'READ_ONLY'.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.instances.preserved_state.disks.source: The source disk or image to preserve for the instance's stateful disk, specified as a name, self-link, or partial URL. This disk or image is used to restore the instance's disk state during resize operations.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.instances.preserved_state.external_ips: A map of external IPs to preserve for the instance as part of its preserved state during a resize operation.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.instances.preserved_state.external_ips.a: Indicates whether the external IP is automatically deleted when the instance is deleted. Valid values are 'TRUE' and 'FALSE'.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.instances.preserved_state.external_ips.i: The preserved external IP address configuration for a network interface. This object includes the IP address and its address type (such as INTERNAL or EXTERNAL).
The external IP address to preserve and assign to the instance when the resize request is processed.
The literal IP address value to assign as the preserved external IP address for this instance.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.instances.preserved_state.internal_ips.a: Whether to automatically delete the internal IP address when the instance is deleted. When true, the IP is deleted with the instance; when false, it is preserved.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.instances.preserved_state.internal_ips.i: The IP address value to preserve for the instance's internal IP configuration.
The literal IP address to preserve for the internal IP. This is used when you want to specify the IP address directly as a string, rather than using a reference to another resource.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.instances.preserved_state.metadata: A map of metadata key-value pairs to preserve for the instance when the resize request is applied.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.instances.status: The status of an instance in the resize request. Possible values are: APPLYING, DELETING, EFFECTIVE, NONE, UNAPPLIED, and UNAPPLIED_DELETION.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.status.error.errors.code: The machine-readable error code for the resize request failure, as returned by the Compute Engine API. This string typically identifies the specific error condition.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.status.error.errors.error_details.error_: The logical grouping to which the error belongs, often a service domain such as 'googleapis.com' or 'gke.io'.

The reason that identifies the specific cause of the error. This value is unique within the error's domain and typically follows the pattern `[A-Z0-9_]+` (e.g., 'SERVICE_DISABLED').
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.status.error.errors.error_details.help: An object containing links to documentation that help resolve the error.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.status.error.errors.error_details.help.l: A list of links to helpful resources related to the error, where each link object typically contains a description and a URL.
A human-readable description of the help link, providing context or guidance related to the error.
URL to a help resource related to the error detail.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.status.error.errors.error_details.locali: A localized error message object, typically containing a 'locale' (e.g., 'en-US') and a 'message' string with the error text in that locale.
The locale (language tag, e.g., 'en-US') of the localized error message.
The localized human-readable error message text, provided in the language specified by the corresponding 'locale' field within the localized_message error detail.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.status.error.errors.error_details.quota_: Information about the quota limit that was exceeded, including the metric name, the quota limit, and the current usage.
A map of quota dimension keys to values, such as region, zone, or resource type, that identifies the specific quota limit that was exceeded.
The quota limit that will apply if the resize request is accepted, used in quota error details.
The maximum allowed value for the quota metric, as specified by the quota limit.
