The rollout status of the quota, indicating whether the rollout is in progress. Allowed values: IN_PROGRESS and ROLLOUT_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.status.error.errors.location: The path or field in the request that the error pertains to, typically a JSON Pointer or field name.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.status.error.errors.message: A human-readable error message that explains the failure.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.status.last_attempt: Represents the most recent attempt to resize the instance group, including error details if the attempt failed.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.status.last_attempt.error.errors.code: The error code associated with this error entry, as returned by the Compute Engine API.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.status.last_attempt.error.errors.error_d: A list of structured error details that provide additional information about the failure, such as specific reasons or troubleshooting hints, complementing the error code and message.
The logical grouping to which the error reason belongs. Often a domain name like 'googleapis.com' or a custom service domain.
A map of metadata associated with the error, providing additional context as key-value pairs.

google_compute_region_instance_group_man.status.last_attempt.error.errors.locatio: The location of the error, typically a field path or resource name indicating where the error occurred in the request.
google_compute_region_instance_group_man.status.last_attempt.error.errors.message: A human-readable description of the error that occurred.

google_compute_region_instance_template.properties: The computed properties of the region instance template, containing the effective instance configuration such as machine type, disks, network interfaces, metadata, and scheduling options. This field is output-only and reflects the actual properties used by the template.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.disks.architecture: The CPU architecture for the disk. Allowed values are ARM64 and X86_64. ARCHITECTURE_UNSPECIFIED means the architecture is not explicitly set.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.disks.auto_delete: Whether the disk should be automatically deleted when the instance to which it is attached is deleted.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.disks.boot: Indicates whether this disk is used as a boot disk. Only one disk in a template can be marked as boot.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.disks.device_name: The device name of the disk as seen by the guest OS. This name can be used to reference the disk from within the instance, for example when mounting. If not specified, a default device name is assigned by Google Compute Engine.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.disks.disk_encryption_key: The customer-supplied encryption key used to encrypt the disk. This can include a raw base64-encoded key, an RSA-encrypted key, or a reference to a Cloud KMS key.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.disks.disk_encryption_key.kms: The resource name of the Cloud KMS key used to encrypt the disk. This is a customer-managed encryption key (CMEK).
The service account used for the KMS encryption operation on the disk. If not specified, the Compute Engine default service account is used.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.disks.disk_encryption_key.raw: The raw 256-bit disk encryption key, provided in base64 format, used to encrypt the disk attached to the instance template.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.disks.disk_encryption_key.rsa: The RSA-encrypted customer-supplied encryption key, used as an alternative to raw_key to protect the key in transit. The key is a 256-bit key encoded in RFC 4648 base64, wrapped with the RSA public key provided by Google.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.disks.disk_encryption_key.sha: The SHA256 hash of the customer-supplied encryption key used to encrypt the disk. This is computed automatically from the raw_key and is used for key verification.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.disks.disk_size_gb: The size of the disk in gigabytes. If not specified, the disk size is taken from the source image.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.disks.force_attach: If true, allows the disk to be attached even if it is already attached to another instance.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.disks.guest_os_features: Specifies a list of features that must be enabled on the guest operating system for this disk. This is commonly used to enable UEFI boot or multi-queue SCSI for bootable images.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.disks.guest_os_features.type: The type of guest OS feature. Possible values include: BARE_METAL_LINUX_COMPATIBLE, CCA_CAPABLE, FEATURE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED, GVNIC, IDPF, MULTI_IP_SUBNET, SECURE_BOOT, SEV_CAPABLE, SEV_LIVE_MIGRATABLE, SEV_LIVE_MIGRATABLE_V2, SEV_SNP_CAPABLE, SNP_SVSM_CAPABLE, TDX_CAPABLE, UEFI_COMPATIBLE, VIRTIO_SCSI_MULTIQUEUE, WINDOWS.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.disks.index: The zero-based index of the disk, where index 0 is reserved for the boot disk and subsequent disks are numbered sequentially in the instance's disk list.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.disks.initialize_params.archi: The architecture of the disk, indicating the CPU type. Allowed values are ARCHITECTURE_UNSPECIFIED (default), ARM64, or X86_64.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.disks.initialize_params.disk_: The size of the boot disk, in gigabytes (GB), for the disk initialization parameters.
The type of disk to use. Can be specified as a full or partial URL to a disk type resource, such as 'pd-ssd' or 'zones/us-east1-a/diskTypes/pd-standard'.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.disks.initialize_params.enabl: Enables Confidential Compute for the disk created by this initialization parameter.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.disks.initialize_params.label: A map of key/value pairs to label the disk. Labels can be used to organize and identify the disk.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.disks.initialize_params.licen: A list of license URLs to apply to the disk image. Overrides licenses inherited from the source image.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.disks.initialize_params.on_up: Specifies the action to take on this disk when the instance template is updated. Valid values are RECREATE_DISK (always recreate the disk), RECREATE_DISK_IF_SOURCE_CHANGED (recreate only if the source image or snapshot changes), and USE_EXISTING_DISK (preserve the existing disk).
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.disks.initialize_params.provi: The number of provisioned IOPS (input/output operations per second) for the disk, specified as a string. This is used for disk types that support performance provisioning.
The provisioned throughput of the disk in MB/s, used to configure performance for supported disk types. Only applicable to hyperdisk-balanced and hyperdisk-throughput disks.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.disks.initialize_params.repli: The zones that the regional persistent disk should be replicated across. This is required for regional persistent disks (when the disk type is regional).
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.disks.initialize_params.resou: Resource manager tags to be applied to the disk. These are key-value pairs used for organizing and controlling access to resources.
List of resource policy self-links (e.g., snapshot schedule policies) to be attached to the disk.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.disks.initialize_params.sourc: The source image to use for this disk. Can be a full image URL, self link, or image name in the same project or a shared image family.
The customer-supplied encryption key used to decrypt the source image when creating the disk. This is required if the source image is encrypted with a customer-managed key.

The name of the Cloud KMS customer-managed encryption key (CMEK) used to encrypt the source image. Must be specified as a resource name in the format 'projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/keyRings/KEY_RING/cryptoKeys/KEY'.
The service account being used for the encryption request for the given KMS key. If absent, the Compute Engine default service account is used.
The base64-encoded 256-bit AES key used to decrypt the source image. Must be kept secret.
The RSA-wrapped customer-supplied encryption key, base64-encoded, used to decrypt the source image when creating a disk from an encrypted image.
SHA-256 hash of the customer-supplied encryption key used to encrypt the source image. This value is used to verify the key identity without exposing the key itself.
The customer-supplied encryption key used to decrypt the source snapshot when creating this disk. This is required if the source snapshot is encrypted with a customer-supplied key.

The name of the encryption key that is stored in Google Cloud KMS. This key is used to encrypt the source snapshot. For example: 'projects/{project}/locations/{location}/keyRings/{keyRing}/cryptoKeys/{key}'.
The service account being used for the KMS key to decrypt the source snapshot.
The raw 256-bit key (base64 encoded) used to encrypt or decrypt the source snapshot.
The RSA-encrypted customer-supplied encryption key used to decrypt the source snapshot. Provide the key base64-encoded.
The SHA256 hash of the customer-supplied encryption key that was used to encrypt the source snapshot.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.disks.initialize_params.stora: The URL of the storage pool in which the disk is created. If not specified, the default storage pool is used.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.disks.interface: The disk interface type. Valid values are 'NVME' and 'SCSI', which determine the protocol used to communicate with the attached disk.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.disks.kind: The type of the resource. For attached disks in instance templates, this is always 'compute#attachedDisk'.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.disks.licenses: A list of license URIs associated with the disk, typically inherited from the source image and used to identify applicable software licenses.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.disks.mode: The disk mode, either READ_ONLY or READ_WRITE. Specifies whether the disk is attached as read-only or read-write.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.disks.saved_state: Indicates the saved state of the disk. Valid values are `PRESERVED` to preserve the disk state and `DISK_SAVED_STATE_UNSPECIFIED` for the default unspecified state.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.disks.shielded_instance_initi: This block configures the initial trusted state of the shielded instance for this disk, including integrity measurements used to verify the boot chain. It is only supported for the boot disk of a shielded VM instance.
The list of database certificates (DBs) for the shielded instance initial state. Each object in the list specifies a base64-encoded certificate content and its file type.
The base64-encoded content of the database (db) file for the Shielded VM initial state.
The file type of the database file, indicating how the content is encoded. Allowed values are BIN (binary), X509 (certificate), and UNDEFINED.
A list of DBX (denied boot) binaries to include in the shielded instance initial state. Each object contains the file content and type (e.g., BINARY or X509).
The base64-encoded content of the database exchange (dbx) file for the shielded instance initial state.
The type of the file, indicating whether it is a binary file (BIN) or an X509 certificate (X509). The value UNDEFINED indicates that the type is not specified.
A list of key exchange keys (KEKs) for the shielded VM initial state. Each item is an object representing a key entry within the shielded instance initial state.
The content of the Key Encryption Key (KEK) used in the shielded instance initial state.
The format of the key or certificate file. Valid values are BIN (raw binary), X509 (PEM-encoded certificate), or UNDEFINED (default, if not set).
The Platform Key (PK) certificate used by Secure Boot to verify the boot loader and OS kernel. This object contains the certificate content and its file type.
The raw content of the platform key (PK) certificate in the secure keys file format, used for the shielded VM initial state.
The format of the certificate file. Valid values are BIN (binary), X509 (PEM encoded), and UNDEFINED.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.disks.source: The URL or name of the source disk to use for this disk. This is used when creating a disk from an existing persistent disk.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.disks.type: The type of disk. Valid values are PERSISTENT and SCRATCH.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.guest_accelerators.accelerato: Specifies the number of accelerator cards of the specified type to attach to the instance.

The type of accelerator (GPU) to attach to the instance. Specify the accelerator type as a full or partial URL, for example 'nvidia-tesla-t4' or 'projects/project/zones/zone/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-t4'.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.metadata.items.key: The key of this metadata entry. Each item in the metadata is a key-value pair.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.metadata.items.value: The value of the metadata item, paired with the associated key in the instance template's metadata.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.network_interfaces.access_con: List of access configurations for this network interface, used to assign external IP addresses. Each access config can specify a NAT IP and network tier.
The external IPv6 address to assign to the instance's network interface access config. If not specified, an IPv6 address is automatically allocated when IPv6 is enabled on the network.
The length, in bits, of the external IPv6 prefix associated with this access configuration.
The kind of the access config, which is always 'compute#accessConfig'.
The external IP address to assign to the instance's network interface. If unset, an ephemeral external IP is assigned automatically.
The network tier to assign to this access config. Valid values are PREMIUM, STANDARD, FIXED_STANDARD, and STANDARD_OVERRIDES_FIXED_STANDARD. If unspecified, defaults to PREMIUM.
Sets a custom PTR (reverse DNS) record for the external IP address of this access config. When specified, the instance's public IP will resolve to this domain name in reverse DNS lookups.
The Google Cloud Armor security policy to apply to this access config. Specify the security policy name or URL.
Specifies whether a public DNS PTR record should be created for the external IP address assigned to this access config.
The type of access configuration. Valid values are ONE_TO_ONE_NAT for external NAT (IPv4) and DIRECT_IPV6 for direct IPv6 access.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.network_interfaces.alias_ip_r: A list of alias IP ranges for this network interface. Each alias IP range specifies an IP range (in CIDR format) to assign to this interface and optionally a subnetwork secondary range name.
The IP CIDR range for the alias IP. This range must be within the primary or secondary IP ranges of the subnetwork.
The name of a subnetwork secondary IP range from which to allocate an IP address range. If not specified, the primary IP range of the subnetwork is used.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.network_interfaces.alias_ipv6: The IPv6 CIDR range (in CIDR notation, e.g., /64) for the alias IPv6 range associated with the network interface. The range must be within the IPv6 address range of the subnet.
The name of the subnetwork's secondary IP range to use for the alias IPv6 range. This must correspond to a secondary range of the subnetwork that the network interface is attached to.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.network_interfaces.enable_vpc: Enables VPC-scoped DNS on this network interface. When set to true, the instance uses the VPC's DNS settings to resolve internal hostnames.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.network_interfaces.igmp_query: Controls whether IGMP query is enabled on this network interface and which version is used. Valid values are IGMP_QUERY_DISABLED (no IGMP query) and IGMP_QUERY_V2 (enable IGMPv2 query).
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.network_interfaces.internal_i: The prefix length in bits for the internal IPv6 range assigned to the network interface. When set, this determines the size of the IPv6 subnet; the only supported value is /96.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.network_interfaces.ipv6_acces: A list of IPv6 access configurations for the network interface. Each configuration specifies the external IPv6 address and network tier.
The external IPv6 address assigned to the instance via this IPv6 access configuration.
The prefix length of the external IPv6 address. Valid values are 32, 64, 96, and 128.
The type of the resource. For IPv6 access configurations, this is always 'compute#ipv6AccessConfig'.
The name of the IPv6 access configuration. It is used to identify the access config within the network interface.
The network tier for this IPv6 access config. Valid values are FIXED_STANDARD, PREMIUM, STANDARD, and STANDARD_OVERRIDES_FIXED_STANDARD.
The domain name to be used for reverse DNS lookup (PTR record) for the IPv6 address. If not specified, no reverse DNS record is created.
The URL or reference of a Compute Engine security policy to apply to this IPv6 access configuration. It allows you to attach a security policy to the external IPv6 address.
When true, sets a public DNS PTR record for the external IPv6 address associated with this access config. When false (default), no public PTR record is created.
The type of IPv6 access configuration. Valid values are `DIRECT_IPV6` for direct IPv6 access and `ONE_TO_ONE_NAT` for one-to-one NAT.
The access type for IPv6 addresses on this network interface. Valid values are EXTERNAL (default) and INTERNAL.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.network_interfaces.kind: The resource type, always compute#networkInterface for network interface resources.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.network_interfaces.network: The name or self_link of the network to attach this interface to.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.network_interfaces.network_at: The URL of the network attachment resource that this network interface should be attached to. When set, the interface connects to a VPC via the specified network attachment.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.network_interfaces.network_ip: The private IPv4 address to assign to the interface. If not specified, an ephemeral address is automatically allocated from the subnet.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.network_interfaces.nic_type: The type of network interface controller (NIC) to attach. Allowed values: GVNIC, IDPF, IRDMA, MRDMA, UNSPECIFIED_NIC_TYPE, VIRTIO_NET.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.network_interfaces.queue_coun: The number of queues for this network interface. If not specified, the number of queues is automatically selected based on the machine type.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.network_interfaces.stack_type: The stack type for the network interface. Valid values are IPV4_IPV6 (dual-stack), IPV4_ONLY, and IPV6_ONLY.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.network_interfaces.subnetwork: The name or self-link of the subnetwork to attach this network interface to. Must be in the same region as the instance template.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.network_interfaces.vlan: The VLAN ID to associate with this network interface when using a network attachment. Required if network_attachment is specified.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.network_performance_config.to: Specifies the tier for total egress bandwidth for the instance. Allowed values are DEFAULT and TIER_1.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.scheduling.node_affinities.ke: The key for the node affinity label, used to match instances to node groups.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.scheduling.node_affinities.op: Specifies the operator for the node affinity. Possible values are IN (match the given values), NOT_IN (do not match the given values), and OPERATOR_UNSPECIFIED.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.scheduling.node_affinities.va: Specifies the values of the node affinity key. These are the actual label values used to match nodes.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.service_accounts.email: The email address of the service account to assign to the instance. If not specified, the default Compute Engine service account is used.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.service_accounts.scopes: The list of OAuth scopes to be granted to the service account. These scopes determine the API access permissions for the instance.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.workload_identity_config: Configures the workload identity settings for the instance template, enabling workload identity on instances created from it.
google_compute_region_instance_template.properties.workload_identity_config.iden: Enables the identity certificate for the workload identity configuration. When set to true, the instance template will use an identity certificate, which is typically used with Google Kubernetes Engine to provide a stable identity for workloads.
google_compute_region_instance_template.source_instance_params.disk_configs.auto: Whether the disk should be automatically deleted when the instance is deleted. Set to true to delete the disk along with the instance, or false to retain it.
google_compute_region_instance_template.source_instance_params.disk_configs.devi: The device name to assign to the disk, used to identify the disk inside the instance.
google_compute_region_instance_template.source_instance_params.disk_configs.inst: Specifies how the disk is instantiated from the source instance in a region instance template. Valid values are: ATTACH_READ_ONLY (attach the disk as read-only), BLANK (create an empty disk), CUSTOM_IMAGE (use a custom image), DEFAULT (use the default behavior), DO_NOT_INCLUDE (omit the disk from the template), SOURCE_IMAGE (use the source instance's boot image), and SOURCE_IMAGE_FAMILY (use the source image family).

google_compute_region_instant_snapshot_g.resource_status.source_info.consistency_: The name of the consistency group associated with the source of the regional instant snapshot group.

Output only. The ID of the consistency group associated with this instant snapshot group's source, if the group was created from a consistency group. This is part of the source status information for the resource.
google_compute_region_instant_snapshot_g.source_consistency_group: The self-link of the source consistency group used to create this instant snapshot group. This field is output-only and identifies the consistency group resource from which the group was derived.

google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.associations.attachment_target: The VPC network to which the firewall policy is attached. This can be a network name or a self-link.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.associations.display_name: A human-readable name for the firewall policy association, used as a display label to identify the association in user-facing contexts.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.associations.firewall_policy_id: The ID of the firewall policy to which the network is being associated.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.associations.name: The name of the firewall policy association, which uniquely identifies it within the regional network firewall policy.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.packet_mirroring_rules.action: The action to apply to packets that match this packet mirroring rule. Valid values are 'mirror' to mirror the traffic and 'do_not_mirror' to exclude the traffic from mirroring.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.packet_mirroring_rules.direction: Direction of traffic to which this packet mirroring rule applies. Valid values are INGRESS (incoming traffic) and EGRESS (outgoing traffic).
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.packet_mirroring_rules.disabled: If set to true, the rule is disabled and will not be considered for packet mirroring.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.packet_mirroring_rules.enable_logging: Whether to enable logging for the packet mirroring rule. When set to true, logs are generated for traffic that matches this rule.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.packet_mirroring_rules.match.dest_addres: List of destination address group URLs that the packet mirroring rule matches. Traffic destined to these address groups is selected for mirroring.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.packet_mirroring_rules.match.dest_fqdns: A list of destination fully qualified domain names (FQDNs) to match against in the packet mirroring rule. Traffic destined to any of these FQDNs matches the rule.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.packet_mirroring_rules.match.dest_ip_ran: A list of destination IP address ranges in CIDR notation that this packet mirroring rule matches.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.packet_mirroring_rules.match.dest_networ: Specifies the network context of the destination traffic to match for packet mirroring. Allowed values are INTERNET, INTRA_VPC, NON_INTERNET, UNSPECIFIED, and VPC_NETWORKS.
The destination network type to which the packet mirroring rule applies. Valid values are: INTERNET, INTRA_VPC, NON_INTERNET, UNSPECIFIED, VPC_NETWORKS.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.packet_mirroring_rules.match.dest_region: Lists destination region codes that the packet's destination IP must be within for the mirroring rule to match. For example, 'us-central1'.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.packet_mirroring_rules.match.dest_threat: A list of threat intelligence categories used to match the destination IP address of a packet. When specified, only packets whose destination IP is associated with one of these categories are affected (e.g., mirrored).
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.packet_mirroring_rules.match.layer4_conf: Layer 4 configurations to match, where each configuration specifies an IP protocol (such as tcp, udp, or icmp) and optionally a list of ports to match.
The IP protocol to which this layer4 config applies. Can be one of the well-known protocol strings (e.g., "tcp", "udp", "icmp", "esp", "ah", "ipip", "sctp") or "all" to match all IP protocols.
List of destination port numbers or ranges (e.g., '80', '1000-2000') for the layer4 config. Required when the protocol is TCP, UDP, or SCTP; must be empty for other protocols.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.packet_mirroring_rules.match.src_address: List of source address groups that this packet mirroring rule uses for matching. When specified, only traffic originating from addresses in these groups will be affected by the rule.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.packet_mirroring_rules.match.src_fqdns: List of fully qualified domain names (FQDNs) used as a source match condition. When specified, only traffic originating from these FQDNs will be mirrored.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.packet_mirroring_rules.match.src_ip_rang: List of source IP address ranges (in CIDR format) that this packet mirroring rule matches. Packets originating from these source IPs will match the rule.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.packet_mirroring_rules.match.src_network: The source network context to match against for this packet mirroring rule. Allowed values are INTERNET, INTRA_VPC, NON_INTERNET, UNSPECIFIED, and VPC_NETWORKS. This restricts the rule to traffic originating from the specified network context.

The type of source network from which the traffic originates. Valid values are: INTERNET (traffic from the internet), INTRA_VPC (traffic within the same VPC network), NON_INTERNET (traffic from non-internet sources such as on-premises or other networks), VPC_NETWORKS (traffic from other VPC networks), and UNSPECIFIED (no source network type specified).
The list of source network resource URLs that packets must come from for this packet mirroring rule to match. If this field is empty, the rule matches from all source networks.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.packet_mirroring_rules.match.src_region_: A list of source region codes (e.g., 'US', 'EU') that the traffic's source region must match for this rule to apply.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.packet_mirroring_rules.match.src_secure_: A list of secure tags that the source instance must have for the packet to match this rule.
The name of the source secure tag, in the format `tagKeys/{resource_id}` or `tagValues/{resource_id}`.
The current state of the secure tag, either EFFECTIVE or INEFFECTIVE, indicating whether the tag is currently in effect.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.packet_mirroring_rules.match.src_threat_: A list of source threat intelligence lists used to match the source IP address of the packet. The source IP must be present in one of the specified threat intelligence lists.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.packet_mirroring_rules.priority: The priority of the packet mirroring rule, which determines the order in which rules are evaluated. Lower numbers are evaluated first and take precedence.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.packet_mirroring_rules.security_profile_: The security profile group to apply to this packet mirroring rule. This should be a self link (URL) to a SecurityProfileGroup resource.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.packet_mirroring_rules.target_forwarding: A list of forwarding rule URLs that this packet mirroring rule applies to. The rule will mirror traffic for the specified forwarding rules.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.packet_mirroring_rules.target_resources: Specifies the list of resources (such as Compute Engine instances) whose traffic will be mirrored by this packet mirroring rule. Each resource should be provided as a fully-qualified URL.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.packet_mirroring_rules.target_secure_tag: A list of secure tags that identify the target instances to which this packet mirroring rule applies. Traffic matching the rule and destined for instances with these tags is mirrored.
The name of the secure tag to match for this packet mirroring rule.
The current state of the target secure tag, indicating whether it is active (EFFECTIVE) or inactive (INEFFECTIVE) for this rule.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.packet_mirroring_rules.target_service_ac: A list of service account emails that the packet mirroring rule applies to. The rule matches traffic from instances running as one of these service accounts.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.packet_mirroring_rules.target_type: The target type of a packet mirroring rule, indicating which type of resource the rule applies to. Allowed values are `INSTANCES` (for VM instances) and `INTERNAL_MANAGED_LB` (for internal managed load balancers).
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.packet_mirroring_rules.tls_inspect: If set to true, enables TLS inspection for traffic matching this packet mirroring rule.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.action: The action to apply when a packet matches this rule, such as 'allow' or 'deny'.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.description: A human-readable explanation of the firewall policy rule.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.direction: Specifies the direction of traffic to which this rule applies: INGRESS for inbound or EGRESS for outbound.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.disabled: Denotes whether the firewall rule is disabled. When set to true, the firewall rule is not enforced.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.enable_logging: Whether to enable logging for this firewall policy rule. When set to true, firewall logs are generated for traffic that matches this rule.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.kind: The kind of the rule, which is always 'compute#firewallPolicyRule'.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.match: The match block defines the traffic criteria (such as source and destination IP ranges and protocol/port) that determine whether this firewall policy rule applies.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.match.dest_address_groups: List of destination address groups that the rule matches. Address groups should be referenced by their full or partial URLs.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.match.dest_fqdns: List of destination fully qualified domain names (FQDNs) to match for egress traffic in this firewall policy rule. When specified, the rule applies only to traffic destined for these domains.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.match.dest_ip_ranges: A list of destination IP address ranges (in CIDR notation) to which this firewall policy rule applies. Traffic is matched based on the destination IP address being within one of these ranges.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.match.dest_network_context: Specifies the destination network context for the firewall rule. Valid values are INTERNET, INTRA_VPC, NON_INTERNET, UNSPECIFIED, and VPC_NETWORKS.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.match.dest_network_type: The type of destination network that the firewall rule matches. Allowed values are: INTERNET, INTRA_VPC, NON_INTERNET, UNSPECIFIED, and VPC_NETWORKS.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.match.dest_region_codes: A list of destination region codes. When specified, the rule matches only traffic destined for resources in those regions.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.match.dest_threat_intelligences: A list of threat intelligence feed names (e.g., 'iplist-known-malicious-ips') that the destination IP address must match for the rule to apply. If omitted, no threat intelligence matching is performed on the destination address.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.match.layer4_configs: A list of layer 4 configurations for the match condition. Each configuration specifies an IP protocol and optional destination port ranges to match.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.match.layer4_configs.ip_protocol: The IP protocol to match. Can be a well-known protocol name such as tcp, udp, icmp, esp, ah, ipip, sctp, or a custom IP protocol number.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.match.layer4_configs.ports: An optional list of destination ports to which this layer4 config applies. This field is only valid for TCP or UDP protocols. Each entry can be an integer (e.g., '80') or a range (e.g., '1024-2048'). If omitted, the rule applies to all ports.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.match.src_address_groups: List of source address groups (IP addresses or CIDR blocks) used to match the source of traffic for this firewall rule.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.match.src_fqdns: A list of fully qualified domain names (FQDN) to match as source in the firewall policy rule.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.match.src_ip_ranges: A list of source IP address ranges in CIDR notation that the firewall rule matches. Traffic from any of these source IPs will be evaluated against the rule's action.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.match.src_network_context: Specifies the network context that the source of the traffic must match. Valid values are INTERNET, INTRA_VPC, NON_INTERNET, UNSPECIFIED, and VPC_NETWORKS.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.match.src_network_type: The source network type to match against. Valid values are INTERNET, INTRA_VPC, NON_INTERNET, UNSPECIFIED, and VPC_NETWORKS.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.match.src_networks: A list of source network resource URLs to match against. Each network is specified in the format projects/{project}/global/networks/{network}.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.match.src_region_codes: Specifies the source region codes that traffic must originate from for the rule to match. The list can contain GCP region codes such as 'us-central1' or 'europe-west1'.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.match.src_secure_tags: List of secure tag objects that the source of the traffic must match for the firewall policy rule to apply.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.match.src_secure_tags.name: The full resource name of the secure tag value, for example `tagValues/123456`. This tag value is used to match traffic originating from resources that have this tag applied.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.match.src_secure_tags.state: The state of the secure tag, indicating whether it is currently effective (EFFECTIVE) or ineffective (INEFFECTIVE) for the firewall policy rule.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.match.src_threat_intelligences: A list of threat intelligence list names used to match the source IP of traffic. The rule applies when the source IP appears in any of the specified threat intelligence lists.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.priority: Integer priority for this firewall rule. Lower values are evaluated first and indicate higher priority. Must be an integer between 0 and 2147483647.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.rule_tuple_count: The number of tuples that the firewall policy rule applies to. This is a computed (read-only) field; a value of 1 indicates the rule applies to a single tuple.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.security_profile_group: This field specifies the security profile group to apply to the firewall rule. It must be set when the rule action is `apply_security_profile_group`, and the value should be a full URL of the form `projects/{project_id}/locations/{location}/securityProfileGroups/{security_profile_group_name}`.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.target_forwarding_rules: A list of forwarding rule URLs that this regional network firewall policy rule applies to.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.target_resources: A list of URLs to target resources (such as Compute Engine instances) that this firewall policy rule applies to. The rule is evaluated for traffic to these resources.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.target_secure_tags: A list of secure tags that control which instances this firewall rule applies to, by matching resources that have at least one of the specified secure tags.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.target_secure_tags.name: The name of the secure tag that this firewall policy rule targets.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.target_secure_tags.state: The state of the secure tag, indicating whether it is currently effective or ineffective. Allowed values are: EFFECTIVE and INEFFECTIVE.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.target_service_accounts: A list of service accounts. When specified, the rule applies only to traffic from instances whose service account is in this list. If empty, the rule applies to all instances.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.target_type: Specifies the target type of the rule. Valid values are INSTANCES and INTERNAL_MANAGED_LB.
google_compute_region_network_firewall_p.rules.tls_inspect: If true, the rule applies only to traffic that has been TLS-inspected. If false, the rule applies only to traffic that has not been TLS-inspected.

google_compute_region_security_policie.adaptive_protection_config.layer7_ddos_d: The confidence threshold percentage that triggers auto-deployment of adaptive protection. Must be a number between 0 and 100.
Duration in seconds after which the auto-deployed adaptive protection mitigation expires. This sets how long the mitigation remains active before being automatically withdrawn.

Threshold for the ratio of impacted baseline traffic that triggers automatic deployment of the DDoS defense. When the measured impacted baseline exceeds this value, the adaptive protection automatically deploys the defense.
The load threshold in requests per second per backend instance that triggers automatic deployment of Layer 7 adaptive protection.

The absolute QPS threshold (in requests per second) that triggers adaptive protection detection. When traffic to the protected resource exceeds this rate, the system may consider it anomalous and apply DDoS defense actions.
The minimum number of requests per second that triggers adaptive protection detection for this threshold configuration.

Detection threshold relative to the baseline queries per second (QPS). A value of 1.0 means the threshold equals the baseline QPS; values greater than 1.0 require proportionally more traffic to trigger detection.
A unique name for this threshold configuration, used to identify it within the layer 7 DDoS defense settings of the adaptive protection config.

A list of traffic granularity configurations for a layer 7 DDoS defense threshold. These configs define how traffic is aggregated or segmented (e.g., by source IP or range) when determining whether a threshold is exceeded, enabling granular control over adaptive protection rules.

When set to true, traffic is tracked separately for each unique value of the configured traffic granularity type (e.g., each unique HTTP header host). When false, traffic is aggregated according to the granularity type.

The type of traffic granularity to use for the layer 7 DDoS defense threshold. This can be HTTP_HEADER_HOST to group traffic by host header, HTTP_PATH to group by request path, or UNSPECIFIED_TYPE if not set.
The IP address or CIDR range for this traffic granularity configuration. The interpretation depends on the associated type field (IP or CIDR).
google_compute_region_security_policie.advanced_options_config.json_custom_conf: Custom configuration for JSON parsing, used in the advanced options of a security policy. It typically specifies content types that should be parsed as JSON.
google_compute_region_security_policie.advanced_options_config.json_parsing: Configures JSON parsing mode for the security policy: DISABLED (no JSON parsing), STANDARD (standard JSON parsing), or STANDARD_WITH_GRAPHQL (standard JSON parsing with GraphQL support).
google_compute_region_security_policie.advanced_options_config.log_level: The logging level for the security policy. Valid values are NORMAL and VERBOSE, where VERBOSE enables more detailed logging.
google_compute_region_security_policie.associations.attachment_id: The ID of the resource to which the regional security policy is associated, typically the self_link of a backend service.
google_compute_region_security_policie.associations.display_name: The display_name is an optional user-defined name for the association, used for display purposes. It does not affect the association's identity, which is determined by the name field.
google_compute_region_security_policie.associations.excluded_folders: List of folder IDs to exclude from the association when the target is an organization or a folder. Resources in these excluded folders will not have the security policy applied.
google_compute_region_security_policie.associations.excluded_projects: An optional list of project IDs that are excluded from this security policy association. When the association targets a project or organization, these projects will not have the policy applied.
google_compute_region_security_policie.associations.security_policy_id: The ID of the security policy to associate with the target in this association block.
google_compute_region_security_policie.ddos_protection_config.ddos_adaptive_pro: The mode of DDoS adaptive protection for this region security policy. Set to DISABLED to turn it off, ENABLED to turn it on, or PREVIEW to test without enforcing. The UNSPECIFIED values are placeholders for internal use.
google_compute_region_security_policie.ddos_protection_config.ddos_protection: The DDoS protection tier to use for the regional security policy. Valid values are STANDARD, ADVANCED, and ADVANCED_PREVIEW.
google_compute_region_security_policie.recaptcha_options_config: The reCAPTCHA options configuration for the region security policy. This output-only object is populated by the API and includes settings such as whether to fail open when reCAPTCHA is unavailable.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.action: The action to perform when a request matches the rule. Allowed values are 'allow' or 'deny', with an optional custom HTTP status code for deny (e.g., 'deny(403)').
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.description: An optional description of the security policy rule.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.header_action: Specifies the header action to apply to requests that match this rule. This block allows you to add or remove HTTP headers using request_headers_to_adds and request_headers_to_remove.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.header_action.request_headers_to_a: A list of request headers to add to the request. Each element in the list contains a header_name and header_value.
The name of the HTTP request header to add to the request. For example, 'X-Forwarded-For'.
The value of the custom header to be added to requests.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.kind: The kind of the resource, set to 'compute#securityPolicyRule' for a region security policy rule.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.match: The match criteria for this security policy rule. It defines the conditions under which the rule is applied, such as source IP ranges, ports, or request expressions.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.match.config: The configuration for the match condition, specifying the source and destination IP ranges to match.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.match.config.src_ip_ranges: A list of source IP address ranges in CIDR format. The rule matches requests whose source IP address falls within any of these ranges.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.match.expr: The expr block provides a Common Expression Language (CEL) expression that defines the matching condition for the security policy rule. The rule is applied when the expression evaluates to true.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.match.expr.expression: The Common Expression Language (CEL) expression that defines the criteria for matching this security policy rule.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.match.expr.location: The source location of the expression, used for debugging. This may specify a file name, line number, or other identifier of where the expression was defined.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.match.expr.title: A short, human-readable title for the expression. This is optional and helps identify the purpose or meaning of the match expression.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.match.expr_options: Options for the expression in the match rule, such as reCAPTCHA configuration.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.match.expr_options.recaptcha_optio: A list of reCAPTCHA Enterprise site keys used for action tokens. These keys are used to validate the action token in the request.
A list of site keys used to verify reCAPTCHA session tokens.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.match.versioned_expr: The versioned expression for the match rule. Must be set to SRC_IPS_V1 when using source IP-based matching; this is the only supported value.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.network_match: The network match configuration for the rule, specifying network conditions like source IP ranges, source region codes, and user-defined fields that the request must satisfy for the rule to apply.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.network_match.dest_ip_ranges: Destination IP address ranges in CIDR format for matching network traffic.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.network_match.dest_ports: A list of destination ports to match, where each entry is a single port (e.g., '80') or a range (e.g., '80-90'). Used in L4 network match conditions for security policy rules.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.network_match.src_asns: A list of source Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) to match. The rule applies to requests originating from networks belonging to any of the specified ASNs.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.network_match.src_ip_ranges: A list of source IP address ranges (CIDR format) that the rule matches for incoming traffic.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.network_match.src_ports: A list of source ports to match for this rule. Each entry can be a single port number or a port range (e.g., '80' or '80-90'). If unspecified, all source ports are matched.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.network_match.src_region_codes: A list of source region codes to match against the source region of the traffic.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.network_match.user_defined_fields: A list of user-defined field configurations used to match network traffic within a security policy rule. Each configuration specifies a field name and a list of values to match against.
The name of the user-defined field to match in the request. This corresponds to the field name as defined in the security policy's user-defined fields.
A list of values to match the user-defined field against. The incoming packet matches if the field value equals any of the specified values.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.preconfigured_waf_config: The preconfigured_waf_config block configures settings for the preconfigured WAF rules applied to this security policy rule. It allows you to customize the inspection behavior, such as defining exclusions to skip certain parts of requests from WAF evaluation.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.preconfigured_waf_config.exclusion: A list of exclusion rules for this preconfigured WAF rule, specifying request attributes (e.g., headers, cookies, query parameters) that should be ignored during WAF evaluation to avoid false positives or allow specific traffic.
A list of request cookies to exclude from WAF evaluation. Each exclusion specifies an operator (EQUALS or STARTS_WITH) and a value representing the cookie name to match.
The operator to apply when matching the request cookie value. Allowed values are CONTAINS, ENDS_WITH, EQUALS, EQUALS_ANY, STARTS_WITH.

The value of the request cookie to exclude from WAF evaluation. When specified, only cookies whose value exactly matches this field are excluded; when omitted, the exclusion applies to any cookie with the matching key.

A list of request headers to exclude from the preconfigured WAF rule evaluation. Each object specifies a header key, a match operator, and a value; the operator can be one of EQUALS_TO, EQUALS_ANY, STARTS_WITH, ENDS_WITH, or CONTAINS.
The operator to apply when matching the request header. Valid values are: CONTAINS, ENDS_WITH, EQUALS, EQUALS_ANY, STARTS_WITH.
A list of query parameters to exclude from WAF evaluation, allowing specific query parameters to be ignored by preconfigured WAF rules.
The operator used to match the query parameter in the exclusion rule. Valid values are `CONTAINS`, `ENDS_WITH`, `EQUALS`, `EQUALS_ANY`, and `STARTS_WITH`.

The value of the query parameter to exclude from WAF evaluation. If a request query parameter matches this value, the parameter (or key-value pair) is excluded from the preconfigured WAF rule evaluation.
A list of request URIs to exclude from the preconfigured WAF rule evaluation. Each object specifies a URI matching condition, typically including a value and an operator.
The operator used to match the request URI. Allowed values are: CONTAINS, ENDS_WITH, EQUALS, EQUALS_ANY, STARTS_WITH.
The URI value to be excluded from the preconfigured WAF rule evaluation.
List of target rule IDs for the exclusion. When empty, all preconfigured WAF rules are excluded.
The target WAF rule set to which the exclusion applies.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.preview: Whether the rule is in preview mode. Preview rules are not enforced, but their actions are still logged and can be used to test rule behavior before enabling enforcement.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.priority: An integer that specifies the evaluation priority of the rule. Lower values are evaluated first. Must be unique within the security policy.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.rate_limit_options.ban_duration_se: The duration in seconds that a client is banned after exceeding the ban threshold. Only applicable when exceed_action is set to 'ban'.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.rate_limit_options.ban_threshold: Threshold that, when exceeded, triggers banning of clients. This nested block is part of rate limit options; when a client surpasses the specified count within the interval, the client is banned.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.rate_limit_options.ban_threshold.c: The number of requests that must be exceeded within the configured interval to trigger a ban. Used in the ban_threshold of rate limiting for a security policy rule.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.rate_limit_options.ban_threshold.i: The time interval, in seconds, over which the ban threshold count is measured before a ban is enforced.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.rate_limit_options.conform_action: The action to take when a request is within the allowed rate limit. For rate limiting, this must be set to 'allow'.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.rate_limit_options.enforce_on_key: Specifies the key type used to identify requests for rate limiting enforcement. Accepted values are: ALL, ASN, HTTP_COOKIE, HTTP_HEADER, HTTP_PATH, IP, REGION_CODE, SNI, TLS_JA3_FINGERPRINT, TLS_JA4_FINGERPRINT, USER_IP, and XFF_IP.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.rate_limit_options.enforce_on_key_: Specifies a list of key configurations used to enforce the rate limit. Each configuration contains the key type (e.g., IP, HTTP_HEADER) and an optional key name.
The name of the key (e.g., HTTP header or cookie name) to enforce rate limiting on. Required when enforce_on_key_type is HTTP_HEADER or COOKIE.

The type of key on which to enforce rate limiting. This specifies which request attribute (e.g., source IP, HTTP header, path) is used to identify and group clients for rate limiting. Valid values are: ALL, ASN, HTTP_COOKIE, HTTP_HEADER, HTTP_PATH, IP, REGION_CODE, SNI, TLS_JA3_FINGERPRINT, TLS_JA4_FINGERPRINT, USER_IP, XFF_IP.
The name of the header or cookie to enforce the rate limit on. This field is required when enforce_on_key is set to HTTP_HEADER or HTTP_COOKIE.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.rate_limit_options.exceed_action: The action to take when a request exceeds the rate limit defined in these rate limit options.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.rate_limit_options.exceed_redirect: Specifies the redirect action for requests that exceed the configured rate limit. This object defines the redirect type (e.g., EXTERNAL_302) and the target URL to redirect excess traffic to.
The URL to which requests that exceed the rate limit are redirected. This is used when the redirect type is set to EXTERNAL_302.
The type of redirect action to take when the rate limit is exceeded. Allowed values are EXTERNAL_302 and GOOGLE_RECAPTCHA.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.rate_limit_options.rate_limit_thre: Configuration for the rate limit threshold, specifying the maximum number of requests allowed within a given time interval before triggering the configured action. Typically includes fields like count and interval.
The number of requests allowed within the specified time interval before the rate limit action is enforced.
The interval in seconds over which the rate limit count is enforced.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.redirect_options.target: The target URL to redirect to when the redirect type is EXTERNAL_302. Only set this when the redirect type is EXTERNAL_302.
google_compute_region_security_policie.rules.redirect_options.type: The type of redirect to apply. If set to EXTERNAL_302, the request is redirected to the specified external target with a 302 status. If set to GOOGLE_RECAPTCHA, the request is redirected to a Google reCAPTCHA page.
google_compute_region_security_policie.user_defined_fields.base: The base protocol or address family that the user-defined field applies to. Valid values are IPV4, IPV6, TCP, UDP.
google_compute_region_security_policie.user_defined_fields.mask: A string representation of the bitmask used to extract the user-defined field from the network packet. The mask is applied to the field specified by the base, offset, and size to select the relevant bits for matching.
google_compute_region_security_policie.user_defined_fields.offset: The byte offset from the specified base (e.g., IP header) where the user-defined field begins. Used together with `base` and `size` to define a custom packet field for matching.
google_compute_region_security_policie.user_defined_fields.size: The size of the user-defined field in bytes, which specifies how many bytes of the named field to inspect.

google_compute_region_snapshot.guest_os_features.type: The guest OS feature type to enable for the snapshot. Possible values include: BARE_METAL_LINUX_COMPATIBLE, CCA_CAPABLE, FEATURE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED, GVNIC, IDPF, MULTI_IP_SUBNET, SECURE_BOOT, SEV_CAPABLE, SEV_LIVE_MIGRATABLE, SEV_LIVE_MIGRATABLE_V2, SEV_SNP_CAPABLE, SNP_SVSM_CAPABLE, TDX_CAPABLE, UEFI_COMPATIBLE, VIRTIO_SCSI_MULTIQUEUE, WINDOWS.
google_compute_region_snapshot.snapshot_encryption_key: The customer-managed encryption key used to encrypt this region snapshot.
google_compute_region_snapshot.source_disk_encryption_key: The customer-supplied encryption key details for the source disk. This field is output-only and reflects the encryption key used by the source disk when it is protected by a customer-supplied encryption key.
google_compute_region_snapshot.source_instant_snapshot_encryption_key: The customer-supplied encryption key of the source instant snapshot. This key is required if the source instant snapshot is encrypted with a customer-managed key, and it is also exposed as an output when populated by the API.

google_compute_region_ssl_policie.warnings.code: The warning code, identifying the type of warning. Possible values include CLEANUP_FAILED, DEPRECATED_RESOURCE_USED, DEPRECATED_TYPE_USED, DISK_SIZE_LARGER_THAN_IMAGE_SIZE, EXPERIMENTAL_TYPE_USED, EXTERNAL_API_WARNING, FIELD_VALUE_OVERRIDEN, INJECTED_KERNELS_DEPRECATED, INVALID_HEALTH_CHECK_FOR_DYNAMIC_WIEGHTED_LB, LARGE_DEPLOYMENT_WARNING, LIST_OVERHEAD_QUOTA_EXCEED, MISSING_TYPE_DEPENDENCY, NEXT_HOP_ADDRESS_NOT_ASSIGNED, NEXT_HOP_CANNOT_IP_FORWARD, NEXT_HOP_INSTANCE_HAS_NO_IPV6_INTERFACE, NEXT_HOP_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND, NEXT_HOP_INSTANCE_NOT_ON_NETWORK, NEXT_HOP_NOT_RUNNING, NOT_CRITICAL_ERROR, NO_RESULTS_ON_PAGE, PARTIAL_SUCCESS, QUOTA_INFO_UNAVAILABLE, REQUIRED_TOS_AGREEMENT, RESOURCE_IN_USE_BY_OTHER_RESOURCE_WARNING, RESOURCE_NOT_DELETED, SCHEMA_VALIDATION_IGNORED, SINGLE_INSTANCE_PROPERTY_TEMPLATE, UNDECLARED_PROPERTIES, and UNREACHABLE.
google_compute_region_ssl_policie.warnings.data: A list of key-value pairs providing additional details about the warning.
google_compute_region_ssl_policie.warnings.data.key: The key of the warning data entry, providing additional details about the warning.
google_compute_region_ssl_policie.warnings.data.value: The value component of a key-value pair in the warning data, providing additional information about the warning.
google_compute_region_ssl_policie.warnings.message: A human-readable warning message describing the issue and suggested action.

google_compute_region_url_map.default_custom_error_response_policy.err: A list of HTTP status codes that this error response rule matches. When a backend returns one of these response codes, the custom error response is used. For example, "404" or "500".
The HTTP status code that the URL Map should return to the client when the error occurs. The value must be between 100 and 599. If not specified, the original error code is returned.

The path to the custom error page for this error response rule. This is typically a relative URL path (e.g., '/custom-error.html') that serves the error response from the backend or a static content bucket.
google_compute_region_url_map.default_route_action: Specifies the default route action for the region URL map, applied to requests that do not match any other route rule. This is an output-only field, populated by the API with the computed default action configuration.
google_compute_region_url_map.default_route_action.cache_policy.negati: HTTP status code for which the negative caching policy applies.
The duration for which a negative cache entry is retained. This is a Duration object containing 'seconds' and 'nanos' fields.
The nanosecond portion of the TTL duration. Must be an integer between 0 and 999,999,999 inclusive.
The number of seconds for the negative caching policy's TTL (time-to-live) duration, expressed as a string.
google_compute_region_url_map.default_route_action.weighted_backend_se: The name of the backend service that receives traffic for this weighted backend service entry.
Defines the header modifications to apply to requests and responses for the corresponding weighted backend service in the region URL map.
The list of headers to be added to the request before it is forwarded to the backend service for this weighted backend service configuration.
The name of the HTTP header to add to the request. Must be a valid header name, typically containing only letters, digits, and hyphens (e.g., 'X-Forwarded-For').
The value of the request header to add. This value is sent to the backend service along with the header name.
If true, the header value replaces an existing header with the same name. If false, the header is added as an additional header.
A list of HTTP request header names to remove from the request before forwarding to the backend service.

A list of response headers to add, with each item specifying a header name and value. These headers are added to HTTP responses sent to the client when the request is served by this weighted backend service.
The name of the HTTP response header to add to responses from the backend service.
The value of the response header to add, paired with the specified header_name.
If true, replaces an existing response header with the same name; if false, appends the new header value to any existing values.
Specifies a list of response header names to remove before sending the response back to the client.
Specifies the relative weight for this backend service. Traffic is distributed proportionally to the weights of all backend services in the weighted_backend_services list.
google_compute_region_url_map.header_action.request_headers_to_add.hea: The name of the request header to add to the outgoing request.
The value of the header to be added to requests.
google_compute_region_url_map.header_action.request_headers_to_add.rep: If false, the header value is appended to any existing values for the same header. If true, the header value replaces any existing values for that header.
google_compute_region_url_map.header_action.response_headers_to_add.he: The name of the response header to add, as specified in the response_headers_to_add header action of the URL map.
The value of the response header to add. This value is paired with the header_name in the same response_headers_to_add block to define a custom header for responses.
google_compute_region_url_map.header_action.response_headers_to_add.re: Indicates whether to replace the existing response header with the provided value. If set to false, the header is added only if it is not already present.
google_compute_region_url_map.host_rules.hosts: The list of host patterns to match. The request's Host header must match one of these patterns (e.g., 'example.com' or '*.example.com') for this host rule to apply.
google_compute_region_url_map.host_rules.path_matcher: The name of the path matcher to use for this host rule. This must match the name of a path matcher defined in the region URL map's path_matchers list.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.default_custom_error_respo: Defines the default custom error response policy for this path matcher, controlling how errors from backend services are customized, such as serving a custom error page or redirecting. If this policy is not set, the URL map's default custom error response policy is used.
A list of error response rules that define custom error handling for specific HTTP error codes. Each rule specifies which response codes to match and the path to the custom error page.
A list of HTTP response codes that this error response rule should match. When a backend returns any of these codes, the specified custom error response is served.
The HTTP status code to return to the client in place of the original error code. If not specified, the original error code is used.
The request path to match for this error response rule. Must start with a forward slash (/).
A reference to a backend service or Cloud Storage bucket that serves the custom error response for this path matcher.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.default_route_action: The default route action for the path matcher, applied when no path rule matches the request.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.default_route_action.cache: The cache policy for the route action, used to configure Cloud CDN cache key generation for requests matched by this path matcher. It defines which parts of the request (host, protocol, query string, headers) are included in the cache key.
List of HTTP request header names that, when present in a request, cause the cache to be bypassed for that request.
Configures the cache key for this route's cache policy, controlling which request attributes are used to form the cache key and thus determine cache hits.
A list of query parameters to exclude from the cache key. Requests that differ only in these parameters will share the same cached response, improving the cache hit ratio.
Specifies whether to include the Host header in the cache key.
Specifies whether to include the protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) in the cache key. If set to true, requests with different protocols are cached separately; if false, they share the same cache entry.
Whether to include the query string in the cache key. If set to false, the query string is excluded, which can improve cache hit rates for URLs that differ only by query parameters.
A list of cookie names to include in the cache key. Cookies not listed here are excluded from the cache key, allowing you to vary cached responses based on specific cookie values.
A list of request header names to include in the cache key. Requests with different values for these headers will be cached as separate entries.
Specifies the list of query parameter names to include in the cache key. If empty, all query parameters are included.

Specifies how responses are cached. Possible values are `CACHE_ALL_STATIC` (caches static content), `FORCE_CACHE_ALL` (caches all responses regardless of headers), and `USE_ORIGIN_HEADERS` (caches according to the origin's Cache-Control headers).
The time-to-live (TTL) for cached responses served to clients. This specifies how long a cached response remains valid for client requests before it must be revalidated.
The fractional second component of the client TTL, specified in nanoseconds. Used together with the 'seconds' field to define the cache duration.
The seconds component of the client TTL duration, specifying how long a response is considered fresh in the cache. This is used together with the nanos field to define the full duration.
The default time-to-live (TTL) for cached responses in this cache policy, used when no per-key or per-route TTL is configured.
The nanoseconds component of the TTL duration. Must be between 0 and 999,999,999, representing the sub-second part of the duration.
The number of seconds for the default time-to-live (TTL) of the cache policy. This value is provided as a string and determines how long cached content is served before revalidation.
The maximum time-to-live (TTL) for cached responses, expressed as a Duration object with `seconds` and `nanos` fields.
The fractional seconds component of the maximum TTL, specified in nanoseconds. This value supplements the 'seconds' field to form the full duration, and must be between 0 and 999,999,999.
The number of seconds for the maximum TTL duration in the cache policy. The value is provided as a string.
When true, enables negative caching, causing responses with status codes 404, 405, 410, and 421 to be cached (unless overridden by Cache-Control headers from the origin).
A list of negative caching policies for the cache policy. Each object in the list defines an HTTP status code and the corresponding time-to-live (TTL) for caching responses with that status code.
The HTTP status code to which this negative caching policy applies. Typically used for status codes like 404 and 500.
The time-to-live (TTL) for the negative cache entry, specified as a duration object with 'seconds' and 'nanos' fields.
The fractional seconds component of the TTL duration, expressed in nanoseconds. Valid range is 0 to 999,999,999.
The seconds component of the TTL (as a string) for the negative caching policy, representing the duration in whole seconds.
If true, requests to the backend will be coalesced together when the cache is enabled, reducing the number of requests sent to the backend. Defaults to true.
This block configures serving stale content while revalidating the cache with the origin. It can specify how long stale responses are served and how often to revalidate.
Specifies the fractional seconds, in nanoseconds, for the serve-while-stale duration. Used together with the seconds field to define the total duration.

The seconds component of the serve-while-stale duration, encoded as a string (e.g., '3600' for one hour). This is part of a protobuf Duration, where the total duration is the sum of this seconds value and any nanos component.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.default_route_action.cors_: The Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) policy for this route action. It specifies allowed origins, methods, headers, and credentials for cross-origin requests, or disables CORS if not configured.

Specifies whether the browser is allowed to send credentials (such as cookies and HTTP authentication) with cross-origin requests. When set to true, the Access-Control-Allow-Credentials response header is set.
Specifies the list of HTTP headers that the origin is allowed to include in CORS requests.
The list of HTTP methods that are allowed for cross-origin requests. This field configures which methods (e.g., GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) are permitted by the CORS policy.
A list of regular expressions that match origins allowed to make CORS requests.
Specifies the list of origins that are allowed to make cross-origin requests. An origin is a combination of scheme, host, and port.
Whether the CORS policy is disabled. When true, the CORS policy is not applied to requests.
Specifies the response headers that are exposed to the client in a CORS response.
Specifies how long (in seconds) the results of a preflight request can be cached in the CORS policy.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.default_route_action.fault: The fault injection policy for this route action, used to test service resilience by introducing delays or aborting a subset of requests.
The specification for how client requests are aborted as part of fault injection.
The HTTP status code used to abort the request. Must be between 200 and 599 inclusive.
The percentage of requests to abort, expressed as a number from 0 to 100. For example, a value of 10 aborts 10% of requests.
Defines the delay fault injection policy. Can set a fixed delay duration and the percentage of traffic to which the delay is applied.
Specifies a fixed delay for fault injection. This object typically contains the delay duration and the percentage of requests to which the delay applies.
The fractional seconds component of the delay, in nanoseconds. Must be between 0 and 999,999,999 inclusive.
Span of time at a resolution of a second. Must be from 0 to 315,576,000,000 inclusive.
The percentage of traffic (between 0.0 and 1.0) to which the delay fault is applied. For example, 0.5 delays 50% of requests.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.default_route_action.max_s: The maximum duration a stream (connection) may remain open before being terminated, specified as an object with 'seconds' and 'nanos'. This is part of the route action for a path matcher in a regional URL map; if unset, the stream duration is unlimited.
The number of nanoseconds (fractional seconds) in the max stream duration. Valid values are from 0 to 999,999,999 inclusive.
Span of time at a resolution of seconds. Must be from 0 to 315,576,000,000 inclusive.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.default_route_action.reque: The request mirroring policy for the default route action. Specifies a backend service to which mirrored requests are sent.
The backend service resource to which mirrored traffic is sent. This can be a full or partial URL to a BackendService resource, e.g., 'projects/{{project}}/global/backendServices/{{name}}'.
The percentage of requests to be mirrored to the mirror backend service. Valid values are from 0 to 100, where 0 means no requests are mirrored and 100 means all requests are mirrored.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.default_route_action.retry: Specifies the retry policy for the default route action, including the number of retries, per-try timeout, and retry conditions.
Specifies the number of retries to attempt. Must be greater than 0; if not specified, defaults to 1.
Specifies the timeout for each retry attempt. This is a Duration object that includes 'seconds' and 'nanos' fields to define the length of time.
The nanosecond component of the per-try timeout duration, used together with the seconds field. Must be between 0 and 999,999,999 inclusive.
The seconds portion of the per-try timeout duration for the retry policy. The value is specified as a string, e.g., '30' for 30 seconds.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.default_route_action.timeo: The timeout for this route action, specified as a Duration object with 'seconds' and 'nanos' fields, defining how long the backend service should wait before considering the request timed out.
The fractional seconds component of the timeout duration, in nanoseconds. Must be between 0 and 999,999,999 inclusive.
The number of seconds for the timeout duration, specified as a string.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.default_route_action.url_r: Configures the URL rewrite settings for the default route action of the path matcher, allowing modifications to the host header and path prefix before the request is forwarded.
The value to rewrite the Host header to. If specified, the host header is rewritten to this value before the request is forwarded to the backend service.
Specifies the value to substitute for the matched path prefix in the request URL. The original matched path prefix is replaced with this string.
Specifies a template for rewriting the URL path. The template can include variables in curly braces that capture parts of the original request path, for example /products/{product}.
A regex rewrite rule that rewrites the URL path based on a regular expression match. Typically contains a `regex` pattern and a `substitution` string to replace the matched portion of the path.
The substitution text to replace the matched path pattern. Capture groups from the path_pattern can be referenced with backslash-number syntax (e.g., \1, \2).
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.default_route_action.weigh: Specifies a list of weighted backend services that determine how traffic is distributed among them. Each item includes a backend service and a weight, where the weight controls the proportion of traffic sent to that service.
The name or self_link of the backend service that this weighted backend service entry routes traffic to. This is the target service for the weighted distribution.
Configures the header modifications for this weighted backend service. This block allows adding, overwriting, or removing request and response headers for traffic routed to the backend.

Specifies the fraction of traffic sent to this backend service, computed as weight / (sum of all weights in the weighted backend service group). Must be between 0 and 1000.

google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.default_url_redirect.prefi: The prefix used to replace the matched path prefix in the redirect target URL. When set, the redirected URL's path starts with this prefix instead of the original matched prefix.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.default_url_redirect.redir: Specifies the HTTP redirect response code to use for the default URL redirect. Valid values are FOUND (302), MOVED_PERMANENTLY_DEFAULT (301), PERMANENT_REDIRECT (308), SEE_OTHER (303), and TEMPORARY_REDIRECT (307).

google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.description: An optional description of the path matcher.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.header_action: Configures the request header modifications (additions or removals) applied to requests that match this path matcher, before they are forwarded to the backend service.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.header_action.request_head: A list of request headers to add to requests that match this path matcher. Each object in the list specifies a header name and value to be added.

google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.name: The name of the path matcher.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.path_rules: Path rules within a path matcher. Each rule contains a list of paths and the corresponding service (backend) to which traffic matching those paths should be routed.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.path_rules.custom_error_re: The custom error response policy for this path rule. It defines how to customize responses for specific HTTP error codes, such as the error page content and response code to serve.

google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.path_rules.route_action: Specifies the route action to take for requests that match this path rule, such as forwarding to a backend service, configuring weighted backend services, URL rewrite, or setting timeouts.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.path_rules.route_action.ca: Configures the cache key policy for this route. It determines which parts of a request (such as query parameters, headers, and cookies) are used in the cache key for CDN caching.
