The list of cookie names to include in the cache key. If empty, no cookies are included in the cache key.
A list of HTTP header names to include in the cache key. The values of these headers will be incorporated into the cache key, affecting cache hits.
Specifies a list of query string parameters to include in the cache key. When non-empty, only these parameters are used to construct the cache key; all other query parameters are ignored.

The cache mode determines what type of responses are cached. CACHE_ALL_STATIC automatically caches static content, FORCE_CACHE_ALL caches all content regardless of origin headers, and USE_ORIGIN_HEADERS relies on the origin's Cache-Control headers.

Specifies the time-to-live (TTL) for cached responses in the client's cache, determining how long a client can serve a response before revalidating with the origin. This is configured within the cache policy of a URL map route action.
The fractional part of the duration in nanoseconds, in the range 0 to 999,999,999. This represents the sub-second component of the client TTL cache policy duration.
The default time-to-live (TTL) for cached responses, represented as a duration object.
The fractional second component of the default TTL, in nanoseconds. This is combined with the seconds field to specify the time-to-live for the cache policy.
The whole seconds portion of the default TTL duration for the cache policy. Provided as a string representation of an integer number of seconds (e.g., '30').
The nanosecond component of the maximum TTL duration for cached responses. Valid range is 0 to 999,999,999.
The seconds component of the maximum TTL duration for cached responses. Must be a non-negative integer represented as a string.
Enables negative caching, which caches HTTP error responses (e.g., 404) for a short duration. Defaults to false when not specified.
Defines caching policies for error responses (negative caching). Each entry specifies an HTTP status code and a TTL (in seconds) for which responses with that code are cached.
The HTTP status code (e.g., 404, 301) for which negative caching is enabled. This code determines which responses are cached according to the negative caching policy.

The time-to-live (TTL) for caching a negative response for the specified status code. As a Duration object, it specifies how long the negative cache entry remains valid, with a valid range of 0 to 3600 seconds.
The fractional seconds component of the TTL, in nanoseconds. The valid range is 0 to 999,999,999.
The seconds component of the TTL duration for negative caching. The negative cache entry expires after this many seconds.

If set to true (default), enables request coalescing for the cache policy. When a cached object goes stale and multiple requests for it arrive, Cloud CDN coalesces them into a single request to the origin, reducing backend load.
Specifies how long the CDN can serve a stale cached response while attempting to revalidate the content with the origin server. Used in the cache_policy of path rules for a regional URL map.
The nanosecond component of the serve_while_stale duration. Together with the seconds field, it specifies the length of time to serve stale content.
The duration in seconds for serving stale content when the origin is unavailable, expressed as a string. This is part of the CDN cache policy's serve_while_stale setting.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.path_rules.route_action.co: The CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) policy for this route action, specifying how the backend responds to cross-origin requests. This object defines allowed origins, methods, headers, and whether credentials are allowed.

The list of HTTP headers that are allowed in cross-origin requests. This corresponds to the Access-Control-Allow-Headers header in the CORS response.
Specifies the list of HTTP methods that are allowed for cross-origin requests in the CORS policy. For example, GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, etc.

google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.path_rules.route_action.fa: Configures the fault injection policy for this route action, allowing the introduction of delays or aborts to simulate failures for testing resilience.

google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.path_rules.route_action.re: This block configures request mirroring for the route action, allowing incoming traffic to be copied to a separate backend service for observation or analysis.

google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.path_rules.route_action.ti: The timeout for requests routed by this path rule. This object represents a Duration, containing 'seconds' and 'nanos' fields, and specifies how long to wait for a backend response before considering the request timed out.

google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.path_rules.route_action.ur: The url_rewrite block configures rewriting of the request URL for matched requests. It can set a new host header and path prefix that will be used when forwarding the request to the backend service.

google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.path_rules.service: The backend service or backend bucket to use when the path matches this rule. Specify the self_link or name of a regional backend service or backend bucket.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.path_rules.url_redirect: Specifies a redirect for requests that match this path rule. When set, matched requests are redirected according to the configured redirect behavior instead of being forwarded to a backend service.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.path_rules.url_redirect.ho: The host that will be used in the redirect response instead of the one that was supplied in the request.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.path_rules.url_redirect.ht: If set to true, the URL scheme in the redirected request is set to https. If set to false, the scheme remains unchanged.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.path_rules.url_redirect.pa: The path portion of the URL to redirect to. If set, the original request path is replaced with this value when the redirect is applied.

google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.path_rules.url_redirect.re: The HTTP redirect status code. Valid values are FOUND (302), MOVED_PERMANENTLY_DEFAULT (301), PERMANENT_REDIRECT (308), SEE_OTHER (303), and TEMPORARY_REDIRECT (307).

google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules: List of route rules that define how requests are matched and routed to backend services within the path matcher. Each route rule specifies match criteria and a corresponding service.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.custom_error_r: The custom_error_response_policy block configures custom error responses for this route rule, allowing you to define custom error pages or redirects for specific HTTP error codes returned by the load balancer.

google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.description: An optional, human-readable description of this route rule.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.header_action: Defines the header actions for this route rule, including adding and removing request and response headers.

The name of the HTTP header to add to the request.

google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.match_rules: List of match rules that define the conditions under which incoming requests are matched to this route rule. google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.match_rules.fu: Specifies the full request path that must exactly match for this match rule to apply. This is an exact match on the entire path, as opposed to prefix or regex matching.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.match_rules.he: Defines a list of HTTP header match conditions. The request must satisfy all specified header conditions for the match rule to be considered a match.

google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.match_rules.ig: Indicates whether to ignore case when matching the request path. When set to true, the match is case-insensitive.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.match_rules.me: A list of metadata filters that requests must match. Each filter specifies a list of labels and a match criterion (MATCH_ALL or MATCH_ANY) to determine whether all or any labels must match.

google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.match_rules.pa: Specifies a path template to match against the request path. The template can include variables in curly braces (e.g., /users/{id}) that match any value in that segment, enabling flexible path-based routing.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.match_rules.pr: Specifies the prefix of the request path to match. The path must begin with this prefix, and the match is case-sensitive.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.match_rules.qu: A list of query parameter match criteria for this match rule. Each entry specifies a query parameter name and value to match, with an optional exactMatch flag to control whether the match is exact or uses regular expressions.

google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.match_rules.re: A regular expression that the entire request path must match. This is used to determine if the route rule applies.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.priority: The priority for this route rule, as an integer from 0 to 2147483647. Lower values are evaluated first, and priorities must be unique within the path matcher.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.route_action: The action to be performed when a request matches this route rule, which may include URL rewriting, routing to weighted backend services, or other routing policies.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.route_action.c: Specifies the list of request header names that cause the cache to be bypassed for requests containing them. Such requests are forwarded to the origin rather than served from cache.

A list of query parameter names to exclude from the cache key. Requests that differ only in these parameters will share the same cached response.

Controls whether the query string from the request URI is included in the cache key. When set to false, the cache key ignores query string parameters.

The nanosecond component of the client TTL (time-to-live) duration, representing fractional seconds. Valid range is 0 to 999999999.
The number of seconds in the TTL duration for the client cache. Must be a non-negative integer expressed as a string.
The default time-to-live for cached responses in the CDN cache, applied when the response does not specify explicit cache directives. The value is a duration object.
The fractional seconds component of the TTL duration, in nanoseconds. Must be between 0 and 999,999,999 inclusive.
The number of seconds in the default TTL duration, as a string. For example, '60' represents 60 seconds.
The maximum time for which the content can be cached. This is a Duration object with 'seconds' and 'nanos' fields. It must be greater than the default TTL if a default is set.
The nanosecond part of the maximum TTL duration, in the range 0-999,999,999. Used together with the seconds value to specify the total max_ttl duration.

Whether to cache responses that are considered errors (e.g., HTTP 404, 502). Setting this to true enables negative caching.
A list of negative caching policies that configure a cache TTL for specific HTTP status codes when negative caching is enabled. Each policy sets a TTL for a given HTTP status code.
The HTTP status code to define a negative caching TTL for. Valid values are 300, 301, 308, 404, 405, 410, 421, 451, and 501.
The nanosecond component of the TTL duration, ranging from 0 to 999999999.
The number of seconds in the TTL duration for the negative caching policy. Valid values range from 0 to 315576000000 (about 10 years), represented as a string.
If true, requests for the same resource from different hosts are coalesced into a single cache entry, reducing the number of cache lookups. The default is false.

The CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) policy for this route action. Configures how requests from different origins are handled, including allowed origins, methods, headers, and credentials.

The list of HTTP headers that the CORS policy allows. This corresponds to the Access-Control-Allow-Headers header in CORS responses, indicating which headers are permitted in the actual request.

Specifies a list of regular expressions that matchallowed origins for CORS requests. A request's Origin header is allowed if it matches any of the provided regexes.
Specifies the list of origins that are allowed to make cross-origin requests as part of the CORS policy for this route rule.
Indicates whether the CORS policy is disabled. When set to true, the CORS policy is not applied to the route.
A list of response headers that browsers are allowed to expose to the client. These headers appear in the Access-Control-Expose-Headers response header.
The maximum time (in seconds) that the client can cache the response to a preflight request. Must be a non-negative integer.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.route_action.f: The fault injection policy for this route action. It can be used to simulate failures by delaying or aborting requests, helping test the resilience of your backend services.
Configures abort fault injection, returning a specified HTTP status code to a percentage of requests.
The HTTP status code to return when aborting the request, typically a 4xx or 5xx code to simulate an upstream error.
The percentage of traffic on which the abort fault is injected. Must be a number between 0.00 and 100.00 inclusive.
Configuration for delay fault injection, specifying the fixed delay amount (in Duration format) and the percentage of requests to which the delay is applied.
The fixed_delay block specifies the fixed amount of delay to inject into requests, expressed as a duration with 'seconds' and 'nanoseconds' fields.
The fractional seconds component of the delay duration, in nanoseconds. Valid values are 0 to 999,999,999.
The whole seconds component of the fixed delay duration. For example, a 1.5-second delay uses seconds: "1" and nanos: "500000000".
Percentage of requests that will get the delay fault injection. Must be between 0 and 100.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.route_action.m: A duration object specifying the maximum time a stream can remain open before being terminated. Contains 'seconds' and 'nanoseconds' fields. This value is ignored for non-streaming requests.
The fractional seconds component of the max stream duration, expressed in nanoseconds. This value is combined with the seconds component to specify the total duration.
The number of seconds in the max stream duration. Must be from 0 to 315,576,000,000 inclusive.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.route_action.r: Request mirroring policy for the route action. When set, incoming requests are mirrored to the backend service specified in the policy's `backend_service` field, while the original request proceeds normally, allowing traffic inspection without altering the response.
The regional backend service that will receive mirrored traffic. This field is required and must reference an existing backend service resource.
The percentage of requests to mirror to the backend service, as a number from 0.0 to 100.0 inclusive.

The retry policy for the route rule's route action. It determines the number of retries, the timeout per retry attempt, and the conditions (such as HTTP status codes) under which a request is retried.
Number of retry attempts to perform before the request is considered failed.
The timeout for each retry attempt in the retry policy, specified as a Duration object (for example, seconds). This applies per individual attempt, separate from the overall request timeout.
The number of nanoseconds in the `per_try_timeout` duration. Must be an integer between 0 and 999,999,999, representing the fractional seconds part of the timeout.

The number of seconds (as a string) for the per-try timeout duration. This is part of the retry policy and sets the maximum time a single retry attempt is allowed to take before it is considered failed.

A list of conditions that trigger a retry for the associated route, such as specific HTTP status codes (e.g., '5xx') or connection errors (e.g., 'connect-failure', 'reset'). These conditions are evaluated in the retry policy of the route action.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.route_action.t: Specifies the timeout for the request to the backend service. It is a duration defined in seconds and nanoseconds. If not set, the backend service's default timeout is used.
The fractional seconds component of the timeout duration, in nanoseconds. Valid range is 0 to 999,999,999.
The seconds component of the timeout duration for this route action. For example, '30' means 30 seconds. This is part of a duration that may also include a nanos component.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.route_action.u: The URL rewrite configuration for this route action. It defines how to rewrite the request's host header and path prefix before forwarding to the target service.
Specifies the value of the Host header that will be set in the request. If not specified, the original Host header is used.
Specifies the path prefix to use when rewriting the URL before forwarding the request to the backend. If not set, the original path prefix is preserved.
Defines a template for rewriting the request URL path. Variables from the matched path template (using pathTemplateMatch) can be referenced in the rewrite template.
Specifies a regex rewrite rule for the URL rewrite action. This rule defines a regular expression pattern and a substitution string used to rewrite the URL path.

The regular expression pattern to match against the request path. It must be a valid RE2 expression, between 1 and 1024 characters long, and is used to determine which portions of the URL path to rewrite.
Substitution string for the path regex rewrite. Can reference capture groups from the match regex using backslash-number syntax (e.g., \1).
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.route_action.w: A list of weighted backend services used to distribute traffic proportionally across multiple backend services. Each entry specifies a backend service and a weight; traffic is routed based on the relative weights.
The name or self_link of the regional backend service that this weighted entry routes traffic to.
The header action for this weighted backend service. This specifies custom headers to add, set, or remove on requests forwarded to the backend service.

This block configures a list of request headers to add to the request before it is sent to the backend service. Each object contains 'header_name' and 'header_value' fields, specifying the header to add and its value.
The name of the HTTP header to add to the request.
The value of the request header to add. This pairs with the header name (set in a sibling field) to define a header that will be appended to requests routed to the backend service.
A list of header names to be removed from the request before forwarding to the backend service. These headers are stripped from the request when routed to the associated weighted backend service.
A list of response headers to add. Each entry specifies a header name, header value, and a boolean indicating whether to replace existing headers with the same name.
The name of the HTTP response header to add.
The value of the response header to add.
If set to true, the added response header will replace an existing header with the same name; otherwise, the value is appended to the existing header.
A list of response header names to remove. These headers are stripped from the response before it is sent to the client.
The weight of this backend service in the weighted group, determining the proportion of traffic routed to it relative to the total weight of all services in the group.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.service: The full or partial URL (or name) of the backend service to which traffic matching this rule is routed.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.url_redirect: A block that defines a URL redirect action for this route rule. When specified, requests matching this rule are redirected to the URL specified by the redirect parameters. If url_redirect is set, neither the service nor the urlRewrite action may be set for the same rule.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.url_redirect.h: Specifies the host to use in the redirect response. If not set, the request's original host is used.
If set to true, the redirect uses the HTTPS protocol; otherwise it uses the same protocol as the request.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.url_redirect.p: The path to which the request should be redirected. If specified, the redirect URL uses this exact path; cannot be used together with prefix_redirect.
Specifies the prefix used for the redirect URL. This value replaces the matched prefix in the original request path.
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.url_redirect.r: The HTTP redirect response code to use for the redirect. Allowed values: FOUND (302), MOVED_PERMANENTLY_DEFAULT (301), PERMANENT_REDIRECT (308), SEE_OTHER (303), TEMPORARY_REDIRECT (307).
google_compute_region_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.url_redirect.s: If set to true, any accompanying query portion of the original URL is removed before redirecting. If set to false, the query string is preserved. Defaults to false.
google_compute_region_url_map.tests.description: An optional description for a test case in the URL map, used to provide additional context or document the test's purpose.
google_compute_region_url_map.tests.headers: A list of HTTP request headers that must be present for the URL map test to match. Each item in the list is an object with a header name and value.
google_compute_region_url_map.tests.headers.name: The name of the request header to match against in the test.
google_compute_region_url_map.tests.host: The hostname or host pattern to match in the test request for validating URL map routing rules.
google_compute_region_url_map.tests.path: The URL path to be used in the test request. For example, '/path'.
google_compute_region_url_map.tests.service: A reference to the backend service that the test expects to handle requests for the specified host and path.

google_compute_reservation.aggregate_reservation.in_use_resources.a: Configuration for the accelerator attached to this in-use resource, specifying the accelerator type and the number of accelerators.
The number of accelerators of the specified type that are currently in use by the reservation.
The type of accelerator (GPU) used by this in-use resource within the aggregate reservation, such as 'nvidia-tesla-t4' or 'nvidia-tesla-a100'.
google_compute_reservation.aggregate_reservation.reserved_resources: An object that specifies the type and number of accelerators (GPUs) to reserve within this aggregate reservation's reserved resources.
google_compute_reservation.confidential_compute_type: The type of confidential compute technology used for the reservation. Possible values are CONFIDENTIAL_COMPUTE_TYPE_TDX (Intel TDX) and CONFIDENTIAL_COMPUTE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED.
google_compute_reservation.reservation_sharing_policy: An output-only object that describes the sharing policy of the Compute Engine reservation, including whether it is shared with specific projects or the entire organization, and which projects can use the reserved capacity.
The current maintenance status for the upcoming group maintenance, with possible values ONGOING, PENDING, or UNKNOWN.
google_compute_reservation.share_settings.project_map.project_id: The ID of the project with which the reservation is shared, used in the project_map for specific project sharing.
google_compute_reservation.specific_reservation.instance_properties: The number of accelerators of the specified type to attach to the instance.
Specifies the accelerator type resource for the guest accelerator. This can be a full or partial URL to an accelerator type resource (e.g., 'nvidia-tesla-p100').
The size of the local SSD in GB. Valid values are multiples of 375, from 375 to 3000 inclusive. Defaults to 375.
The interface type for the local SSD, either `NVME` or `SCSI`. This determines the storage protocol used for the local SSD devices.

google_compute_resource_policie.description: An output-only description of the resource policy, as returned by the Google Cloud API.
google_compute_resource_policie.region: The Google Cloud region where the resource policy is located. This field is computed by the provider and is output-only, meaning it is not user-configurable and reflects the region determined by the provider configuration.
google_compute_resource_policie.snapshot_schedule_policy.schedule.weekly: The day of the week on which the snapshot is taken. Allowed values are MONDAY, TUESDAY, WEDNESDAY, THURSDAY, FRIDAY, SATURDAY, SUNDAY, and INVALID.
The duration of the time window during which the snapshot schedule is active on this day of the week, specified as an ISO 8601 duration (e.g., 'PT1H' for one hour).
The time of day, in HH:MM format using a 24-hour clock, at which the snapshot is taken on the specified day of the week (in UTC).

google_compute_rollout_plan.waves.number: The wave number, represented as a string, indicating the sequential order of the wave within the rollout plan.
google_compute_rollout_plan.waves.orchestration_options.delays.delim: Specifies the grouping delimiter for delay execution. Valid values: DELIMITER_BATCH (delay applies per batch), DELIMITER_LOCATION (delay applies per location), DELIMITER_UNSPECIFIED (no specific grouping).
google_compute_rollout_plan.waves.orchestration_options.delays.durat: The duration of the delay, specified as a string with a time unit (e.g., '30s' or '5m').
google_compute_rollout_plan.waves.orchestration_options.delays.type: The type of delay for this orchestration step. Allowed values are TYPE_MINIMUM (minimum delay), TYPE_OFFSET (offset delay), and TYPE_UNSPECIFIED (not specified).
google_compute_rollout_plan.waves.orchestration_options.max_concurre: The maximum number of locations (zones) that can be updated concurrently during this wave of the rollout. The value can be a fixed number or a percentage of the total locations, e.g., '5' or '25%'.
google_compute_rollout_plan.waves.selectors.location_selector.includ: A list of Google Cloud locations (regions or zones) to include in this location selector. Resources in these locations will be selected for the rollout wave.
google_compute_rollout_plan.waves.selectors.resource_hierarchy_selec: A list of folder resource names (or IDs) to include in the resource hierarchy selector. Resources contained within these folders are selected for the rollout wave.
The list of organization IDs to include in the rollout wave's resource hierarchy selector. Only the resources within these organizations are targeted by the wave.
A list of GCP project identifiers to include in the resource hierarchy selector. The rollout plan will apply to resources in these projects.
google_compute_rollout_plan.waves.validation: Configures the validation procedure for this wave, specifying how the rollout verifies the health and readiness of the instances in the wave before advancing to the next wave.
google_compute_rollout_plan.waves.validation.time_based_validation_m: The duration to wait as part of time-based validation, represented as a string.

google_compute_route.as_paths.as_lists: A list of autonomous system (AS) numbers that form the AS path for the route, ordered according to the path segment type (AS_SEQUENCE or AS_SET).
google_compute_route.as_paths.path_segment_type: The type of BGP AS path segment, indicating the ordering and confederation scope of the AS numbers in the segment. Possible values are: AS_SEQUENCE (ordered set of AS numbers), AS_SET (unordered set), AS_CONFED_SEQUENCE (ordered set within a confederation), AS_CONFED_SET (unordered set within a confederation).
google_compute_route.warnings.code: A warning code that identifies the type of warning. Possible values include CLEANUP_FAILED, DEPRECATED_RESOURCE_USED, DEPRECATED_TYPE_USED, DISK_SIZE_LARGER_THAN_IMAGE_SIZE, EXPERIMENTAL_TYPE_USED, EXTERNAL_API_WARNING, FIELD_VALUE_OVERRIDEN, INJECTED_KERNELS_DEPRECATED, INVALID_HEALTH_CHECK_FOR_DYNAMIC_WIEGHTED_LB, LARGE_DEPLOYMENT_WARNING, LIST_OVERHEAD_QUOTA_EXCEED, MISSING_TYPE_DEPENDENCY, NEXT_HOP_ADDRESS_NOT_ASSIGNED, NEXT_HOP_CANNOT_IP_FORWARD, NEXT_HOP_INSTANCE_HAS_NO_IPV6_INTERFACE, NEXT_HOP_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND, NEXT_HOP_INSTANCE_NOT_ON_NETWORK, NEXT_HOP_NOT_RUNNING, NOT_CRITICAL_ERROR, NO_RESULTS_ON_PAGE, PARTIAL_SUCCESS, QUOTA_INFO_UNAVAILABLE, REQUIRED_TOS_AGREEMENT, RESOURCE_IN_USE_BY_OTHER_RESOURCE_WARNING, RESOURCE_NOT_DELETED, SCHEMA_VALIDATION_IGNORED, SINGLE_INSTANCE_PROPERTY_TEMPLATE, UNDECLARED_PROPERTIES, UNREACHABLE.
google_compute_route.warnings.data: A list of key-value pairs containing additional details about the warning. Each object in the list has a 'key' and a 'value' field that provide context for the warning message.
google_compute_route.warnings.data.key: The key of the key-value pair that provides additional information in the warning data.
google_compute_route.warnings.data.value: The value associated with a key in a warning data pair. This provides additional machine-readable details about the warning.
google_compute_route.warnings.message: A human-readable warning message describing the issue or condition associated with the route, as returned by the Compute Engine API.

google_compute_router.bgp: BGP configuration for the Cloud Router, including the autonomous system number (ASN), advertised route settings, and other BGP parameters. This field is optional when creating a router and is computed by the provider when not explicitly set.
google_compute_router.bgp.advertised_ip_ranges.range: The IP range in CIDR notation (e.g., 192.168.0.0/16) that the router advertises to BGP peers.
google_compute_router.bgp_peers.advertise_mode: The route advertisement mode for the BGP peer. Use DEFAULT to advertise the provider's default route set, or CUSTOM to define specific routes via the advertised_ip_ranges field.
google_compute_router.bgp_peers.advertised_groups: Specifies the list of prefix groups to advertise in custom mode. Valid values are 'ALL_SUBNETS', 'ALL_VPC_SUBNETS', and 'ALL_PEER_SUBNETS'. This field can only be populated when advertise_mode is 'CUSTOM'.
google_compute_router.bgp_peers.advertised_ip_ranges: A list of custom IP ranges to advertise to the BGP peer. Each object contains a CIDR 'range' (required) and an optional 'description'.
google_compute_router.bgp_peers.advertised_ip_ranges.descripti: An optional, user-defined description for the advertised IP range.
google_compute_router.bgp_peers.advertised_ip_ranges.range: The IP range to advertise, specified in CIDR notation (e.g., '192.168.0.0/16').
google_compute_router.bgp_peers.advertised_route_priority: The priority of routes advertised to this BGP peer. In the case of multiple BGP peers advertising the same route, the route with the lowest priority is preferred.
google_compute_router.bgp_peers.bfd: Configures Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) settings for this BGP peer.
google_compute_router.bgp_peers.bfd.min_receive_interval: The minimum interval, in milliseconds, between received BFD control packets for this BGP peer. This setting controls how quickly the router detects a peer failure.
google_compute_router.bgp_peers.bfd.min_transmit_interval: The minimum interval (in milliseconds) between BFD transmissions for this BGP peer. The value must be between 100 and 30000 milliseconds.
google_compute_router.bgp_peers.bfd.multiplier: The number of consecutive BFD control packets that must be missed before BFD declares the peer down.
google_compute_router.bgp_peers.bfd.session_initialization_mod: The BFD session initialization mode. Valid values are ACTIVE, DISABLED, and PASSIVE. ACTIVE initiates the BFD session, PASSIVE waits for the peer to initiate, and DISABLED disables BFD.
google_compute_router.bgp_peers.custom_learned_ip_ranges: A list of custom learned route IP address ranges for this BGP peer.
google_compute_router.bgp_peers.custom_learned_ip_ranges.range: The IP range in CIDR notation to use as a custom learned IP range for the BGP peer.
google_compute_router.bgp_peers.custom_learned_route_priority: User-specified priority for routes learned from this BGP peer. Must be between 0 and 65535 inclusive, defaults to 100.
google_compute_router.bgp_peers.enable: Indicates whether the BGP peer is enabled. The allowed values are TRUE and FALSE.
google_compute_router.bgp_peers.enable_ipv4: Enables IPv4 on the BGP peer. This flag is set to true by default.
google_compute_router.bgp_peers.enable_ipv6: Enables IPv6 for the BGP peer. Set to true to allow the BGP peer to exchange IPv6 routes.
google_compute_router.bgp_peers.export_policies: List of names of Cloud Router route policies to apply to outgoing routes advertised to this BGP peer.
google_compute_router.bgp_peers.import_policies: A list of Cloud Router route policy names that this BGP peer applies to incoming routes. These policies control which routes are accepted from the BGP peer.
google_compute_router.bgp_peers.interface_name: The name of the router interface the BGP peer is associated with. This must match the name of an existing interface on the same Compute Router.
google_compute_router.bgp_peers.ipv4_nexthop_address: The IPv4 address that this BGP peer uses as the next hop for advertised routes.
google_compute_router.bgp_peers.ipv6_nexthop_address: The IPv6 address used as the next-hop for routes advertised to this BGP peer. If not specified, the default IPv6 next-hop (typically the interface's address) is used.
google_compute_router.bgp_peers.management_type: The management type of the BGP peer, which indicates whether the peer is managed by the associated attachment or by the user. Valid values are 'MANAGED_BY_ATTACHMENT' and 'MANAGED_BY_USER'.
google_compute_router.bgp_peers.md5_authentication_key_name: The name of the MD5 authentication key to use for this BGP peer. The key must be defined in the router's BGP configuration.
google_compute_router.bgp_peers.peer_asn: The autonomous system number (ASN) of the BGP peer. Required when configuring a BGP peer on a Compute Router.
google_compute_router.bgp_peers.peer_ip_address: The IP address of the BGP peer that this router will establish a BGP session with.
google_compute_router.bgp_peers.peer_ipv4_nexthop_address: The IPv4 address of the BGP peer, used as the next hop for routes learned from this peer.
google_compute_router.bgp_peers.router_appliance_instance: The URI of the VM instance that is the router appliance for this BGP peer.
google_compute_router.interfaces.ip_range: The IP address and range for the router interface, used for BGP sessions. This can be a single IP address or a CIDR range in the form of 'IP/30'. If not specified, GCP will assign an IP address automatically.
google_compute_router.interfaces.ip_version: The IP version used by this interface. Valid values are IPV4 and IPV6.
google_compute_router.interfaces.linked_interconnect_attachmen: The URL of the interconnect attachment to link with this router interface. This is used when the interface is for a VLAN attachment on an Interconnect.
google_compute_router.interfaces.linked_vpn_tunnel: The name of the VPN tunnel that this interface is linked to. Use this when the interface is of type 'tunnel'.
google_compute_router.interfaces.management_type: Indicates who manages this interface: MANAGED_BY_ATTACHMENT means the interface is managed by a VLAN attachment (Cloud Interconnect), while MANAGED_BY_USER means it is configured by the user.
google_compute_router.interfaces.private_ip_address: The private IP address of the Compute Router interface.
google_compute_router.interfaces.redundant_interface: The name of another interface in the same router that serves as the redundancy pair for this interface. When set, this interface is configured as part of a redundant BGP session.
google_compute_router.interfaces.subnetwork: The name or self-link of the subnetwork to which this router interface is attached. This field is used when the interface is associated with a subnetwork, such as for router appliance interfaces.
google_compute_router.md5_authentication_keys.key: The shared secret key used for MD5 authentication in the BGP session. This value is provided to the peer to authenticate the router.
google_compute_router.md5_authentication_keys.name: The name of the MD5 authentication key. It uniquely identifies the key within the router's BGP configuration.
google_compute_router.nats.auto_network_tier: Specifies the network tier for the NAT. Allowed values are FIXED_STANDARD, PREMIUM, STANDARD, and STANDARD_OVERRIDES_FIXED_STANDARD.
google_compute_router.nats.drain_nat_ips: A list of external IP addresses to be drained from the NAT. These IPs will no longer be used for new connections but will continue to serve existing connections until they are closed.
google_compute_router.nats.effective_tcp_time_wait_timeout_sec: The effective TCP TIME_WAIT timeout in seconds for Cloud NAT connections, reflecting the actual value in use (either the configured value or the default).
google_compute_router.nats.enable_dynamic_port_allocation: If set to true, the NAT gateway dynamically allocates ports for each VM from a shared pool instead of using static port allocation. Defaults to false.
google_compute_router.nats.enable_endpoint_independent_mapping: Whether to enable endpoint independent mapping for the NAT gateway. When enabled, the NAT gateway maps each internal IP and port pair to a unique external IP and port, independent of the destination.
google_compute_router.nats.endpoint_types: The list of endpoint types supported by this NAT configuration, controlling which types of network endpoints can use the NAT.
google_compute_router.nats.icmp_idle_timeout_sec: The idle timeout for ICMP connections in seconds. This controls how long an ICMP session is kept alive in the NAT without traffic before being closed.
google_compute_router.nats.log_config: Configuration for NAT logging. This block allows enabling or disabling logging for the NAT gateway and specifying a filter to determine which connections are logged.
google_compute_router.nats.log_config.enable: Whether to enable logging for the NAT gateway. When set to true, logs are generated according to the filter specified in the log_config block.
google_compute_router.nats.log_config.filter: Determines which NAT logs are exported. Valid values: ALL (log all NAT traffic), ERRORS_ONLY (log only failed translations), TRANSLATIONS_ONLY (log successful translations only).
google_compute_router.nats.max_ports_per_vm: Maximum number of ports per VM used by the NAT configuration, per subnet. Defaults to 2048, with an allowed range of 64 to 65536.
google_compute_router.nats.min_ports_per_vm: The minimum number of ports allocated to each VM in the NAT configuration.
google_compute_router.nats.name: The name of the Cloud NAT. This name must be unique within the parent router.
google_compute_router.nats.nat64_subnetworks: A list of subnetworks (self-links) to be used for NAT64. NAT64 enables IPv6-only resources to communicate with IPv4-only services by mapping IPv6 addresses to IPv4 addresses. Each listed subnetwork must be configured with an IPv6 address range.
google_compute_router.nats.nat64_subnetworks.name: The name of the subnetwork to use for NAT64.
google_compute_router.nats.nat_ip_allocate_option: Specifies how NAT IP addresses are allocated. AUTO_ONLY automatically allocates NAT IPs; MANUAL_ONLY requires you to specify them in nat_ips.
google_compute_router.nats.nat_ips: List of self-links of external IP addresses to be used for NAT. Only valid when nat_ip_allocate_option is set to MANUAL_ONLY; if empty, an automatically allocated IP is used.
google_compute_router.nats.rules: A list of custom NAT rules. Each rule specifies a rule number, a match expression, and an action (e.g., translation or no translation) to control how traffic is routed through the NAT.
google_compute_router.nats.rules.action: The action configuration for this NAT rule, defining how traffic matching the rule's match condition is NATed. It specifies the source NAT IPs (active and drain) to use.
google_compute_router.nats.rules.action.source_nat_active_ips: The list of IP addresses to use as source NAT IPs for active connections when this NAT rule is applied.
google_compute_router.nats.rules.action.source_nat_active_rang: The list of source NAT IP ranges (in CIDR format) to use as the active NAT addresses for packets matching this rule. Required for the action block of a NAT rule.
google_compute_router.nats.rules.action.source_nat_drain_ips: List of source NAT IP addresses to be drained. These IPs will not be used for new connections, but existing connections will continue to use them until they are removed or connections terminate.
google_compute_router.nats.rules.action.source_nat_drain_range: A list of source NAT IP ranges to be drained. These ranges are used to gracefully terminate existing connections during a migration or deactivation of NAT IPs.
google_compute_router.nats.rules.description: A user-defined, human-readable description for the NAT rule.
google_compute_router.nats.rules.match: An expression in Common Expression Language (CEL) that defines which traffic this NAT rule applies to. It can match on packet attributes like source or destination IP, protocol, and ports, e.g., `inIpRange(destination.ip, '203.0.113.0/24')`.
google_compute_router.nats.rules.rule_number: The unique number assigned to this NAT rule. Rules are evaluated in ascending order, and this number must be unique within the NAT configuration.
google_compute_router.nats.source_subnetwork_ip_ranges_to_nat: Specifies which IP ranges of the subnets are eligible for NAT. Valid values are: ALL_SUBNETWORKS_ALL_IP_RANGES, ALL_SUBNETWORKS_ALL_PRIMARY_IP_RANGES, and LIST_OF_SUBNETWORKS.
google_compute_router.nats.source_subnetwork_ip_ranges_to_nat6: Controls which IPv6 subnetwork IP ranges are eligible for NAT64. Set to ALL_IPV6_SUBNETWORKS to use all IPv6 subnets in the region, or LIST_OF_IPV6_SUBNETWORKS to use only the specific subnets listed in the associated subnetwork configuration.
google_compute_router.nats.subnetworks: The list of subnetworks that this NAT configuration applies to. Each object specifies a subnetwork and its NAT settings.
google_compute_router.nats.subnetworks.name: The name of the subnetwork to include in the NAT configuration for this router NAT.
google_compute_router.nats.subnetworks.secondary_ip_range_name: List of the secondary ranges of the subnetwork that are allowed to use NAT. This can be provided only when 'LIST_OF_SECONDARY_IP_RANGES' is used for source_ip_ranges_to_nat.
google_compute_router.nats.subnetworks.source_ip_ranges_to_nat: List of source IP ranges in the subnetwork that should be NATed. Valid values are 'ALL_IP_RANGES', 'PRIMARY_IP_RANGE', and 'LIST_OF_SECONDARY_IP_RANGES'. If 'LIST_OF_SECONDARY_IP_RANGES' is used, you must also specify `secondary_ip_range_names`.
google_compute_router.nats.tcp_established_idle_timeout_sec: Timeout in seconds for established TCP connections before they are considered idle and closed. Defaults to 1200 seconds.
google_compute_router.nats.tcp_time_wait_timeout_sec: Timeout for TCP connections in the TIME_WAIT state, specified in seconds, within the router's NAT configuration.
google_compute_router.nats.tcp_transitory_idle_timeout_sec: The timeout in seconds for TCP transitory idle connections. A transitory connection is one that is in the process of being established (e.g., during the TCP handshake); if no traffic is seen within this timeout, the connection is dropped. Defaults to 30 seconds.
google_compute_router.nats.type: The type of NAT configuration. Valid values are `PRIVATE` and `PUBLIC`.
google_compute_router.nats.udp_idle_timeout_sec: The timeout (in seconds) for UDP connections through the NAT. Defaults to 30 seconds if not specified.

google_compute_security_policie.adaptive_protection_config.layer7_ddos_d: The minimum confidence score (between 0 and 1) that adaptive protection requires before automatically deploying mitigation rules for layer 7 DDoS defense.
The number of seconds that the auto-deploy system waits before automatically deploying the mitigation rules. If not set, the default value is 3600 seconds.

Specifies the traffic load threshold in requests per second that triggers automatic deployment of Layer 7 DDoS adaptive protection. When traffic exceeds this threshold and other conditions are met, Google Cloud Armor may automatically enable mitigation.
The absolute queries per second (QPS) threshold that triggers detection of a layer 7 DDoS attack.

The load threshold in requests per second that triggers detection of a potential DDoS attack by the layer 7 adaptive protection. Exceeding this threshold causes the system to start monitoring traffic for attack indicators.
Detection threshold in queries per second (QPS) relative to the baseline traffic level for triggering adaptive protection. A value greater than 1 indicates a multiple of the baseline QPS.

A list of traffic granularity configurations for the threshold. Each configuration defines a traffic type (such as SOURCE_IP or USER_AGENT) and a value to specify the granularity of traffic to which the threshold applies.
If true, the threshold is applied to each unique value (e.g., each source IP) independently, instead of aggregating all traffic together.

The type of traffic granularity. Valid values are `HTTP_HEADER_HOST` (group traffic by the HTTP Host header), `HTTP_PATH` (group traffic by the HTTP request path), and `UNSPECIFIED_TYPE` (default, unspecified).
google_compute_security_policie.advanced_options_config.json_parsing: Controls the JSON payload parsing mode for the security policy. Possible values: DISABLED (no JSON parsing), STANDARD (standard JSON parsing), or STANDARD_WITH_GRAPHQL (standard JSON plus GraphQL parsing).
google_compute_security_policie.advanced_options_config.log_level: Specifies the log level for the security policy, controlling how much detail is logged. Valid values are NORMAL and VERBOSE.
google_compute_security_policie.associations.attachment_id: The ID of the resource (e.g., backend service or target instance) to which the security policy is attached.
google_compute_security_policie.associations.display_name: The display name of the security policy association. This is a user-defined name used to identify the association.
google_compute_security_policie.associations.excluded_projects: A list of project IDs or project numbers to exclude from this security policy association. This is used when the security policy is associated with a parent resource such as an organization or folder, to prevent the policy from applying to the specified projects.
google_compute_security_policie.associations.security_policy_id: The ID of the security policy that is being associated.
google_compute_security_policie.ddos_protection_config: Configuration for DDoS protection on the security policy, containing the protection class. This field is computed and output-only, so it cannot be set in configuration.
google_compute_security_policie.ddos_protection_config.ddos_adaptive_pro: Configures the adaptive protection mode for DDoS attacks. Allowed values are DISABLED, ENABLED, PREVIEW, and UNSPECIFIED_ADAPTIVE_PROTECTION (the default, which uses the provider's unspecified behavior).
google_compute_security_policie.ddos_protection_config.ddos_protection: Specifies the Google Cloud Armor DDoS protection tier for this security policy. Valid values are ADVANCED, ADVANCED_PREVIEW, and STANDARD.
google_compute_security_policie.recaptcha_options_config: Configuration for reCAPTCHA options in the security policy. This field is computed, meaning it is populated by the API and cannot be set manually.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.action: The action to take when a request matches the rule.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.header_action: The header_action block configures the request headers to add or remove for requests that match this security policy rule.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.header_action.request_headers_to_a: A list of request headers to be added to matching requests. Each object specifies a header name and its value.
The name of the header to add to the request. For example, 'X-Frame-Options'.
The value of the request header to add. This is the literal string value that will be sent with the header.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.kind: The type of the resource. Always 'compute#securityPolicyRule'.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.match: The match block configures the request criteria that trigger the rule. It can contain either a config block for source IP ranges or an expr block for a CEL expression, depending on the policy version.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.match.config: The match configuration for the rule, which defines the traffic to match using parameters such as source IP ranges, versioned expression, and layer 4 configs.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.match.config.src_ip_ranges: List of source IP address ranges (in CIDR notation) that the rule uses to match traffic.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.match.expr: The expr block defines a match expression in Common Expression Language (CEL) that is evaluated against incoming requests. If the expression evaluates to true, the rule is applied.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.match.expr.description: A human-readable description of the expression, used to document the purpose or intent of the match condition.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.match.expr.expression: The CEL expression that defines the match condition for the security policy rule. This expression is evaluated against incoming requests to determine if the rule applies.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.match.expr.location: Optional string that identifies the source location (e.g., file and line) of the CEL expression, used for error reporting and debugging.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.match.expr.title: The title for the match expression, providing a human-readable name to identify the expression in the security policy rule.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.match.expr_options.recaptcha_optio: A list of site keys to be used for validating reCAPTCHA action tokens.
Specifies a list of reCAPTCHA site keys used to verify session tokens for this rule.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.match.versioned_expr: The version of the expression to use for the match rule. Currently, only 'SRC_IPS_V1' is supported, which matches on source IP addresses.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.network_match: Defines the network match criteria for a security policy rule, specifying conditions such as source and destination IP ranges, IP protocols, and ports that determine when the rule applies.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.network_match.dest_ip_ranges: List of destination IP ranges (in CIDR format) that this network match rule applies to. Each entry can be an IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR block, e.g., '192.0.2.0/24' or '2001:db8::/32'. Traffic whose destination IP falls within any of these ranges will match the rule.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.network_match.dest_ports: An optional list of destination ports to match. Each element may be a single port number (e.g., '80') or a range of ports (e.g., '80-90'). If not specified, all destination ports are matched.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.network_match.ip_protocols: A list of IP protocols that the rule matches. Traffic must use one of the specified protocols to match the rule; if omitted, the rule matches all IP protocols.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.network_match.src_asns: List of source Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) that the source IP address of the request must belong to for the rule to match.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.network_match.src_ip_ranges: A list of source IP address ranges in CIDR notation that incoming traffic must match for the rule to apply.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.network_match.src_ports: A list of source ports or port ranges (e.g., '80' or '80-90') to match in the network rule.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.network_match.src_region_codes: List of source region codes (two-letter ISO 3166 alpha-2 country codes) used to match requests based on the geographic location of the source IP address.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.network_match.user_defined_fields: A list of user-defined fields for matching network traffic. Each object contains a field name and optional values to match against.
Identifies the user-defined field to match in network traffic.
A list of string values to match against the referenced user-defined field. The rule matches when the field value is equal to one of these values.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.preconfigured_waf_config: Configuration block for preconfigured WAF (Web Application Firewall) rules. This block contains exclusions that allow selectively disabling specific preconfigured WAF rules or parts of them for this security policy rule.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.preconfigured_waf_config.exclusion: A list of exclusions for the preconfigured WAF configuration. Each exclusion defines rules or rule sets that are excluded from the managed preconfigured WAF rules.
A list of request cookies to exclude from the preconfigured WAF rule evaluation. Each object defines a cookie to be ignored when the rule inspects incoming requests.
The match operator to use for the cookie, such as CONTAINS, ENDS_WITH, EQUALS, EQUALS_ANY, or STARTS_WITH.
The value of the request cookie to exclude.
Specifies a list of request headers to exclude from the preconfigured WAF rule evaluation. When configured, these headers are not inspected by the WAF rules, helping to avoid false positives.
The operator used to match the request header value for exclusion from the preconfigured WAF rules. Valid values are CONTAINS, ENDS_WITH, EQUALS, EQUALS_ANY, and STARTS_WITH.
The value of the request header to exclude from the preconfigured WAF rule.
A list of request query parameters to exclude from evaluation by the preconfigured WAF rule. Each object defines a query parameter that should be ignored when the rule is applied.
The operator used to match the request query parameter name to exclude. Allowed values are: CONTAINS, ENDS_WITH, EQUALS, EQUALS_ANY, STARTS_WITH.

The value of the query parameter to be excluded. This is used together with the key to specify a particular query parameter and value that should be excluded from evaluation by the preconfigured WAF rules.

A list of request URIs to exclude from matching the preconfigured WAF rule. Each item defines a specific URI that should be excluded from evaluation, so requests to these URIs will not be blocked or flagged by this rule.
The operator used to match the request URI to exclude. Valid values are CONTAINS, ENDS_WITH, EQUALS, EQUALS_ANY, and STARTS_WITH.
A request URI to exclude from the preconfigured WAF rule's evaluation.
The list of specific rule IDs to exclude from the preconfigured WAF configuration. These are the target rules that the exclusion applies to.
The name of the predefined WAF rule set that this exclusion applies to.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.preview: If true, the rule is in preview mode, meaning the action is not enforced but traffic is logged for testing.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.priority: The priority of this rule. Rules are evaluated in order from lowest to highest value (i.e., lower numbers have higher precedence). The priority must be an integer between 0 and 2147483647.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.rate_limit_options: This block configures the rate limiting behavior for the rule, including parameters like the threshold and enforcement key.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.rate_limit_options.ban_duration_se: The duration in seconds that a client is banned when the rule action is 'rate_based_ban'.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.rate_limit_options.ban_threshold: The threshold that triggers a temporary ban for an IP address that has exceeded the rate limit. It includes a count of requests and an interval in seconds over which the count is measured.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.rate_limit_options.ban_threshold.c: The number of requests that must be exceeded to trigger the ban threshold.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.rate_limit_options.ban_threshold.i: The time interval in seconds during which the number of requests (count) is evaluated to determine if the ban threshold is exceeded. For example, an interval_sec of 60 means the count must be exceeded within a 60-second rolling window.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.rate_limit_options.conform_action: Action to take for requests that are within the configured rate limit (i.e., do not exceed the threshold).
google_compute_security_policie.rules.rate_limit_options.enforce_on_key: The key type on which the rate limit is enforced. Valid values are ALL, ASN, HTTP_COOKIE, HTTP_HEADER, HTTP_PATH, IP, REGION_CODE, SNI, TLS_JA3_FINGERPRINT, TLS_JA4_FINGERPRINT, USER_IP, and XFF_IP.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.rate_limit_options.enforce_on_key_: A list of configurations that specify the keys on which to enforce the rate limit. Each configuration includes a key type (e.g., IP, HTTP_HEADER, HTTP_COOKIE) and can optionally define exclusions for the rate limit.
The name of the key to enforce rate limiting on, such as the header name or cookie name, as specified by the corresponding enforce_on_key_type field.

The type of request key to enforce rate limiting on. Valid values include: ALL, ASN, HTTP_COOKIE, HTTP_HEADER, HTTP_PATH, IP, REGION_CODE, SNI, TLS_JA3_FINGERPRINT, TLS_JA4_FINGERPRINT, USER_IP, XFF_IP.
The name of the key to enforce the rate limit on, used when the enforceOnKey field requires a key name (e.g., the HTTP header name when enforceOnKey is HTTP_HEADER).
google_compute_security_policie.rules.rate_limit_options.exceed_action: Action to take when the rate limit threshold is exceeded. Valid values are 'deny(403)' and 'rateBasedBan'.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.rate_limit_options.exceed_redirect: Options for the redirect action taken when requests exceed the rate limit threshold. Used when the exceed action is set to redirect, specifying the redirect type and target URL.
The target URL to redirect to when the rate limit is exceeded. Required when the redirect type is EXTERNAL_302.
The type of redirect to use when the rate limit is exceeded. Possible values are EXTERNAL_302, which redirects to an external URL, and GOOGLE_RECAPTCHA, which presents a Google reCAPTCHA challenge.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.rate_limit_options.rate_limit_thre: An object defining the request threshold that triggers rate limiting. It specifies the number of requests (count) allowed within a given time interval (interval_sec).
The number of requests allowed within the configured interval before the rate limit action is applied.
The time interval in seconds over which the rate limit count is measured. The rate limit is triggered when the number of requests within this interval reaches the specified count.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.redirect_options: Configuration for the redirect action to take when this rule matches. Contains settings such as redirect type and target.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.redirect_options.target: The URL to redirect the request to when the redirect type is set to EXTERNAL_302. It specifies the destination for the redirect action.
google_compute_security_policie.rules.redirect_options.type: The type of redirect action. Valid values are EXTERNAL_302, which redirects to an external URL with HTTP 302, and GOOGLE_RECAPTCHA, which redirects to Google reCAPTCHA.
google_compute_security_policie.user_defined_fields.base: The base protocol or address family on which this user-defined field operates. Valid values are IPV4, IPV6, TCP, and UDP.
google_compute_security_policie.user_defined_fields.mask: The mask that identifies the field to extract from the request or response, such as an HTTP header name when base is 'request'.
google_compute_security_policie.user_defined_fields.offset: The byte offset from the start of the selected base (e.g., TCP header) where the user-defined field begins. Offsets are zero-based; an offset of 0 refers to the first byte.
google_compute_security_policie.user_defined_fields.size: Specifies the fixed length in bytes to extract from the base (e.g., TCP or UDP header) when defining a user-defined field by size. This is mutually exclusive with 'match' and is used to capture a fixed-size portion of the packet.

google_compute_service_attachment.connected_endpoints.consumer_network: The URL of the consumer network that is connected to this service attachment, e.g. projects/{project}/global/networks/{network}.
google_compute_service_attachment.connected_endpoints.endpoint: The URL of the consumer endpoint (for example, a forwarding rule) that is connected to the service attachment.
google_compute_service_attachment.connected_endpoints.nat_ips: The list of NAT IP addresses allocated for the consumer endpoint.
google_compute_service_attachment.connected_endpoints.propagated_connectio: The number of connections that have been propagated to the consumer network from the producer network for this connected endpoint.
google_compute_service_attachment.connected_endpoints.psc_connection_id: The unique identifier for the Private Service Connect connection associated with this connected endpoint.
google_compute_service_attachment.connected_endpoints.status: The current status of the connected endpoint. Possible values are: ACCEPTED, CLOSED, NEEDS_ATTENTION, PENDING, REJECTED, and STATUS_UNSPECIFIED.
google_compute_service_attachment.consumer_accept_lists.connection_limit: The maximum number of connections allowed for the consumer in the accept list. A value of 0 means no limit.
google_compute_service_attachment.consumer_accept_lists.network_url: The URL of the network that is allowed to connect to this service attachment.
google_compute_service_attachment.consumer_accept_lists.project_id_or_num: The project ID or project number of a consumer project that is allowed to connect to the service attachment. Used in the consumer accept list to identify the allowed project.
google_compute_service_attachment.psc_service_attachment_id.low: The lower 32 bits of the 64-bit PSC service attachment ID, represented as a decimal string.

google_compute_snapshot.guest_os_features.type: The type of guest OS feature. This specifies a feature that the guest OS supports or requires. Valid values are: BARE_METAL_LINUX_COMPATIBLE, CCA_CAPABLE, FEATURE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED, GVNIC, IDPF, MULTI_IP_SUBNET, SECURE_BOOT, SEV_CAPABLE, SEV_LIVE_MIGRATABLE, SEV_LIVE_MIGRATABLE_V2, SEV_SNP_CAPABLE, SNP_SVSM_CAPABLE, TDX_CAPABLE, UEFI_COMPATIBLE, VIRTIO_SCSI_MULTIQUEUE, WINDOWS.
google_compute_snapshot.snapshot_encryption_key: The encryption key used to encrypt the snapshot. This field is computed and output-only, meaning the provider populates it with the key information returned from the API.
google_compute_snapshot.source_disk_encryption_key: The customer-supplied encryption key used to encrypt the source disk from which the snapshot was created. This field is output-only and reflects the key details as used by the API.
google_compute_snapshot.source_instant_snapshot_encryption_key: The encryption key information for the source instant snapshot used to create this snapshot. This is a computed, output-only field that provides the customer-supplied encryption key (CSEK) details if the source instant snapshot was encrypted with one.

google_compute_ssl_policie.warnings.code: The warning type code, such as DEPRECATED_RESOURCE_USED or RESOURCE_NOT_DELETED.
google_compute_ssl_policie.warnings.data: A list of key-value pairs providing additional details about a warning.
google_compute_ssl_policie.warnings.message: A human-readable message describing the warning returned by the API.

google_compute_storage_pool.share_settings.project_map.project_id: The unique identifier of the Google Cloud project to which these share settings apply.

google_compute_subnetwork.purpose: The purpose of the subnetwork, indicating how it is used. Valid values include GLOBAL_MANAGED_PROXY, INTERNAL_HTTPS_LOAD_BALANCER, PEER_MIGRATION, PRIVATE, PRIVATE_NAT, PRIVATE_RFC_1918, PRIVATE_SERVICE_CONNECT, and REGIONAL_MANAGED_PROXY. When not set, the default is PRIVATE.
google_compute_subnetwork.secondary_ip_ranges.ip_cidr_range: The CIDR range for the secondary IP range, specified in CIDR notation (e.g., '10.0.1.0/24'). This range must not overlap with the primary or other secondary IP ranges in the subnetwork.
google_compute_subnetwork.secondary_ip_ranges.ip_collection: The name of the IP collection to use for this secondary IP range.
google_compute_subnetwork.secondary_ip_ranges.ip_version: The IP version of this secondary IP range. Allowed values are IPV4, IPV6, or IP_VERSION_UNSPECIFIED.
google_compute_subnetwork.secondary_ip_ranges.range_name: The name of the secondary IP range. Must be unique within the subnetwork.
google_compute_subnetwork.secondary_ip_ranges.reserved_internal_ra: Reference to a reserved internal range (by name or URI) used to allocate this secondary IP range. Specify this instead of ip_cidr_range to use a pre-reserved internal range for the secondary range.
google_compute_subnetwork.utilization_details.external_ipv6_instan: The lower bound of the free external IPv6 address range, represented as an IP address string.
google_compute_subnetwork.utilization_details.external_ipv6_lb_uti: The lower bound of the range of free IPv6 addresses available for external load balancer utilization.
google_compute_subnetwork.utilization_details.internal_ipv6_utiliz: The total number of internal IPv6 addresses allocated in the subnetwork, as part of utilization details.
The lower 64 bits of the total allocated IPv6 address count, expressed as a decimal string.
The lower 64 bits of the total number of free IPv6 addresses in the subnet, represented as a decimal string.
google_compute_subnetwork.utilization_details.ipv4_utilizations.ra: The name of the IP range (e.g., primary or a specific secondary range) for which this IPv4 utilization is reported.
google_compute_subnetwork.utilization_details.ipv4_utilizations.to: The total number of IPv4 addresses allocated in the subnetwork, represented as a string.
The total number of free (unassigned) IPv4 addresses in the subnet's utilization range, represented as a string.

google_compute_url_map.default_custom_error_response_policy.err: A list of HTTP response codes (as strings) that this error response rule applies to. When a backend returns one of these codes, the corresponding custom error response is served. For example, '404' or '503'.
The HTTP status code that will be returned to the client instead of the original error code when this error response rule is matched.
The full path to the file to use as the custom error page, for example /errors/my-error.html.
google_compute_url_map.default_route_action: The default route action for the URL map, applied to traffic that does not match any host or path rules. This computed field is populated by the API with the actual default action configuration.
google_compute_url_map.default_route_action.cache_policy.negati: The HTTP status code to cache as a negative response. For example, 404 or 500.
The fractional seconds component of the TTL duration, in nanoseconds. Must be between 0 and 999,999,999 inclusive.
The number of seconds in the TTL duration for the negative caching policy, represented as a string (e.g., "300").
google_compute_url_map.default_route_action.weighted_backend_se: The name or full URL of the backend service to which traffic is routed for this weighted entry.

The header_action block configures request and response header modifications for this weighted backend service. It allows adding or removing custom headers on requests to and responses from the backend service.
List of request headers to add or override before the request is forwarded to the backend service. Each object in the list specifies a header name and a header value.
The name of the request header to add to the request before forwarding it to the backend service.
The value to assign to the request header specified by header_name.
If set to true, the header value replaces any existing value for the header; if false, the value is appended to existing values.
Specifies a list of HTTP header names that will be removed from the request before it is forwarded to the backend service. These headers are stripped from the incoming request headers.
Configures the response headers to add. Each object defines a header name and value to be appended to the response before it is sent to the client.
The name of the response header to add. This is the header key (e.g., 'X-Custom-Header') that will be appended to the response.
The value of the response header to be added. This is used with header_name in the response_headers_to_add block.
Indicates whether to replace the existing response header value (true) or append the new value to it (false). If false, multiple values are added for the same header.
List of response header names to remove. These headers are stripped from the response before it is returned to the client.
The weight of this backend service, used to determine the proportion of traffic that it receives relative to other weighted backend services. Must be an integer between 0 and 1000.
google_compute_url_map.header_action.request_headers_to_add.hea: The name of the HTTP header to add to the request. For example, 'X-Custom-Header'.
The value of the header to add to the request.
google_compute_url_map.header_action.request_headers_to_add.rep: Indicates whether to replace an existing request header with the same name. If set to true, existing headers with the same name are removed before the new header is added; if false, the new header is added without removing existing ones.
google_compute_url_map.header_action.response_headers_to_add.he: The name of the response header to add.
The value of the header to add to the response.
google_compute_url_map.header_action.response_headers_to_add.re: If true, replaces an existing response header with the same name. If false, adds the header without replacing.
google_compute_url_map.host_rules.description: An optional description for this host rule.
google_compute_url_map.host_rules.hosts: The list of host patterns to match against the Host header of incoming requests. Each host must be a fully qualified domain name (FQDN), optionally starting with a wildcard `*.` to match subdomains.
google_compute_url_map.host_rules.path_matcher: The name of the PathMatcher to use for this host rule. This must reference a path matcher defined in the url_map's path_matcher block.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.default_custom_error_respo: The default custom error response policy for the path matcher's default service. This policy defines custom error response rules that override the default HTTP error responses for requests routed to the default service.
A list of HTTP response codes to match for this error response rule. When the origin returns a code in this list, the custom error response is used.
Specifies the HTTP status code to return when this error response rule is matched, overriding the original error code. Must be a valid HTTP status code (e.g., 404, 500).
The request path that this error response rule applies to. If left empty, the rule applies to all paths.

The full or partial URL to the BackendBucket that serves custom error responses for this path matcher's default policy. For example, a full URL like 'https://www.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/project/global/backendBuckets/backendBucket' or a partial URL such as 'backendBucket'.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.default_route_action: The default route action to apply when no path rule matches in this path matcher. This object can define actions such as URL rewrites, header modifications, and redirects.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.default_route_action.cache: Defines the cache policy for the default route action, controlling how responses from backend services are cached. It includes options for cache mode and time-to-live (TTL) settings.
Specifies a list of HTTP request header names. If any of these headers is present in a request, the request bypasses the CDN cache and is forwarded to the origin server.
The cache key policy for the cache policy, specifying which parts of the request (such as host, protocol, query string, headers, and cookies) are used to construct the cache key.

The list of query parameters to exclude from the cache key. Any query parameters in this list will not be included when constructing the cache key, allowing different requests with different values for these parameters to share a cached response.
If true, includes the Host header in the cache key, meaning requests with different Host values are cached separately.

Indicates whether the request protocol (e.g., HTTP or HTTPS) should be included in the cache key. When set to true, the protocol is part of the cache key, causing separate cache entries for different protocols.
Specifies whether query strings are included in the cache key. If false, requests with different query strings will share the same cached response.
Specifies the list of cookie names that should be included in the cache key. If this list is empty, no cookies are included. Any cookies not listed are not part of the cache key.
A list of HTTP header names to include in the cache key. These headers are used to vary the cache key by their values.
A list of query parameters to include in the cache key. When set, only these parameters and their values are used to form the cache key; all other query parameters are ignored.

Specifies the cache mode for the backend. Allowed values are CACHE_ALL_STATIC (automatically caches static content), FORCE_CACHE_ALL (caches all content regardless of headers), and USE_ORIGIN_HEADERS (caches based on origin response headers).
The nanoseconds component of the TTL duration for cached responses, representing the fractional second part of the time-to-live.
The seconds component of the client TTL duration, representing the whole-second value of the time-to-live in the cache policy.
The default time-to-live (TTL) for cached responses, expressed as a duration object (e.g., seconds and nanoseconds). It is applied when no other TTL is specified by the client or origin.
The nanosecond component of the TTL duration, representing the fractional seconds (0-999999999).
The seconds component of the default TTL duration. Must be a string representation of an integer between 0 and 315,576,000,000 inclusive.
The maximum amount of time for which a cached response will be served, expressed as a duration (an object with seconds and nanos). This overrides any default TTL in the cache policy.
The nanosecond component of the max_ttl duration, representing the fractional seconds. Valid range is 0 to 999,999,999. Together with seconds, it defines the maximum time-to-live for cached content.

The number of whole seconds in the maximum time-to-live duration for the cache policy. This is the seconds component of the duration, which together with the nanos component determines how long a cache entry remains valid.
Indicates whether the cache policy uses negative caching, which caches responses with error status codes (e.g., 404, 502). When enabled, such responses are cached according to the negative_ttl field.

A list of objects that configure how long negative responses (such as HTTP error status codes) are cached, allowing different TTLs per status code. Applies to the cache policy of the URL map path matcher's default route action.
The HTTP status code (between 300 and 599) for which the negative caching policy applies.
The time-to-live for cached negative responses. This is a Duration object specifying how long to cache an error response before checking the backend again.
The fractional seconds component of the TTL duration. Valid values are 0 to 999,999,999.
The seconds component of the negative caching TTL, representing the duration in seconds for which the negative cache entry is valid.
If true, multiple concurrent requests for the same resource are coalesced into a single request to the origin, reducing load on the origin server when there is a cache miss.
The fractional seconds component of the serve-while-stale duration, in nanoseconds. Valid values are between 0 and 999,999,999 inclusive.
The duration in seconds for which the cache will continue to serve stale content after the original TTL has expired.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.default_route_action.cors_: The specification for allowing client side cross-origin requests. This policy defines CORS settings for the route action, including allowed origins, methods, and headers.

Specifies whether the client is allowed to send credentials (such as cookies or HTTP authentication) with cross-origin requests. When set to true, the Access-Control-Allow-Credentials header is included in responses.
The list of HTTP headers that are allowed in cross-origin requests. This sets the Access-Control-Allow-Headers header in the CORS policy.
Specifies the list of HTTP methods allowed for CORS requests. For example, GET, PUT, POST, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS, and PATCH.
A list of origin regular expressions that are allowed to make CORS requests. An origin matches if it matches any of the listed regular expressions.
Specifies a list of origins that are permitted to make cross-origin requests. Each item is a string representing an origin, such as a domain name.
If true, the CORS policy is disabled.
Specifies the headers that the browser is allowed to access in the response, as part of the CORS policy. This corresponds to the Access-Control-Expose-Headers header.
Specifies how long (in seconds) the results of a preflight request can be cached by the client.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.default_route_action.fault: The fault injection policy for the default route action. Can be used to delay or abort requests that match this route, helping to test resiliency.
Configuration for aborting requests as part of fault injection, used to simulate service failures by returning a specific HTTP status code.
The HTTP status code used to abort the request. The value must be between 100 and 599.
The percentage of inbound requests to which the abort fault is applied, as a number between 0.0 and 100.0 inclusive.
The delay block configures a fixed delay before forwarding requests. It includes settings for the delay amount and the percentage of requests to which the delay applies.
Specifies a fixed delay duration for requests when fault injection is enabled, expressed as an object containing seconds and nanoseconds.
The fractional seconds component of the fixed delay, in nanoseconds. Must be a non-negative integer between 0 and 999,999,999 inclusive.
The seconds component of the fixed delay duration before forwarding the request. Combined with the nanos field, it specifies the total delay.
