The percentage of requests that will be delayed by the fault injection policy. Must be a number between 0.0 and 100.0.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.default_route_action.max_s: The maximum duration for a stream (request/response) before the connection is closed. This is a Duration object containing 'seconds' and 'nanos' fields.
The fractional seconds component of the maximum stream duration, expressed in nanoseconds. Valid values are from 0 to 999,999,999.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.default_route_action.reque: The request mirroring policy for this route action, which sends a copy of incoming requests to a separate backend service for monitoring or analysis without affecting the response to the original request.
The backend service that receives mirrored traffic. This can be a full or partial URL to a backend service resource.
The percentage of requests to mirror to the backend service specified in the request mirror policy. Must be between 0 and 100, where 0 mirrors no requests and 100 mirrors all requests.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.default_route_action.retry: Specifies the retry policy for this route action, including retry conditions (e.g., connect-failure, refused-stream, unavailable) and the maximum number of retries.
The number of retries to attempt before the request is considered failed.
The timeout for each retry attempt, specified as a duration string (e.g., '30s'). If unset, the default per-try timeout for the route is applied.
The fractional part of the per-try timeout duration, specified in nanoseconds. Valid values range from 0 to 999,999,999.
The retry conditions that define which errors or status codes should cause a retry.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.default_route_action.timeo: Specifies the timeout for the selected route, as a duration. This sets the maximum time for the backend to respond before the request is considered timed out.
The fractional part of the duration in nanoseconds, allowing sub-second precision for the timeout value.
The seconds portion of the timeout duration. The total timeout is the sum of this value and the nanos field (if specified).
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.default_route_action.url_r: Defines the URL rewrite rules to apply to requests matched by this default route action, allowing modification of the host and path before forwarding the request to the backend service.
Specifies the value to replace the Host header in the request with for URL rewriting. This is used in the default route action of a path matcher to rewrite the host portion of the request URL.
Specifies the path prefix that replaces the matched path prefix before the request is forwarded to the backend service. This allows rewriting the URL path for the backend.
Specifies the template that the request path is rewritten to as part of the URL rewrite action.
Defines a regex-based URL path rewrite. The regex field specifies the pattern to match, and the substitution field provides the replacement string.
The regular expression pattern to match against the URL path for the regex rewrite operation. Only paths that match this pattern will be rewritten according to the rewrite rule.
The substitution string used to replace the part of the request path matched by the specified regex in this regex rewrite. It defines the rewritten path segment for the URL rewrite.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.default_route_action.weigh: A list of weighted backend services that handle traffic when a path matcher's default route action is used. Each entry specifies a backend service and a weight to control proportional traffic distribution.

The name or URL of the backend service to which traffic is routed. This must reference an existing backend service in the same project; the load balancer applies any header transformations defined on that service before forwarding requests.
Defines the header action for this weighted backend service, specifying request and response headers to add or remove.
The name of the HTTP request header to add to the request before it is sent to the backend service.
The value of the request header to be added to the request.
If true, replaces an existing request header with the same name; if false, appends the header value to any existing values.
A list of request header names to remove before forwarding the request to the backend service.

A list of headers to add to the response before it is sent to the client. Each object in the list contains a header name and value, and the headers are applied to responses from the associated weighted backend services.
The name of the response header to add.
The value to assign to the response header specified by the corresponding header_name in the response_headers_to_add list.
If true, the header value replaces the existing header value with the same name. If false, the value is appended to the existing header value.
List of header names to remove from the response before it is sent to the client.

The weight of this backend service, used for weighted traffic distribution. Must be an integer between 0 and 1000, with a default of 100. Traffic is routed proportionally based on the weights of all backend services in the weighted_backend_services list.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.default_service: The default backend service or backend bucket to use if no path rules match. This must be a full or partial URL to a backend service or backend bucket.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.default_url_redirect: Defines a default URL redirect for the path matcher. When a request does not match any route rule, this redirect action is applied, allowing configuration of host, path, prefix, HTTPS redirect, response code, and query string handling.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.default_url_redirect.host_: The host that will be used in the redirect response instead of the one that was supplied in the request.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.default_url_redirect.https: If set to true, the URL scheme in the redirected request is set to HTTPS. If false or unset, the scheme remains the same as the original request (typically HTTP).
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.default_url_redirect.path_: The path that the request will be redirected to.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.default_url_redirect.prefi: The prefix to substitute for the matched path prefix in the redirect URL. If set, only one of prefix_redirect or path_redirect can be specified.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.default_url_redirect.redir: The HTTP redirect response code used when the defaultUrlRedirect is applied. Valid values are: FOUND, MOVED_PERMANENTLY_DEFAULT, PERMANENT_REDIRECT, SEE_OTHER, and TEMPORARY_REDIRECT.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.default_url_redirect.strip: If set to true, the query string from the original request is removed before constructing the redirect URL.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.header_action: The header_action block configures header transformations (both request and response) for this path matcher.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.header_action.request_head: A list of request headers to add to the request before forwarding it to the backend service. Each object defines a header name and value.
The name of the HTTP request header to add.
The value of the HTTP request header to add. This is used in conjunction with header_name to set a custom header on requests routed by this path matcher.
A boolean that determines whether the header value should replace any existing header values with the same name. If false, the value is appended to existing values; if true, the value replaces them.
A list of header names to remove from the request before it is forwarded to the backend service.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.header_action.response_hea: List of response headers to add or overwrite. Each object includes headerName, headerValue, and optionally replace, specifying whether to overwrite an existing header.
The name of the response header to add.
The value of the response header to add.
If true, replaces an existing response header with the same name using the specified value. If false, appends the value to the existing header, which may result in multiple header values.
A list of response header names to remove from the response before sending it back to the client.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.name: The name of the path matcher. This must be a unique identifier within the URL map and is referenced by host rules.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.path_rules: The list of path rules that map URL paths to backend services or backend buckets.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.path_rules.custom_error_re: Defines a custom error response policy for this path rule. It includes error response rules that map specific HTTP status codes to custom error pages, and optionally specifies an error service to serve those responses.

A list of rules that define custom error responses for the path rule. Each rule specifies which HTTP response codes to match (e.g., 404, 500) and the path to the custom error page to serve for those codes.
The HTTP response codes that this error response rule applies to. When a backend returns one of these codes, the custom error response is used.
The HTTP status code to override the original error response with. When specified, this code replaces the original error response code for the matched error condition.
The backend service that serves the custom error responses for this path rule. It must be a reference to an existing backend service resource.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.path_rules.paths: A list of URL path patterns (e.g., '/home', '/static/*') that this path rule matches. Requests whose paths match any pattern in this list are handled according to this rule.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.path_rules.route_action: The route action for this path rule, specifying how matching requests are handled, including backend service, timeout, retry policy, request mirroring, CORS, and other settings.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.path_rules.route_action.ca: Defines the Cloud CDN cache policy for this route action, determining how responses are cached for matching path rules.
List of request header names that, when present in a request, cause the request to bypass the cache. Requests containing any of these headers will not use cached content.
The cache key policy, which controls how Cloud CDN constructs cache keys by specifying included components like host, protocol, query string, headers, and cookies.
A list of query parameter names to exclude from the cache key. When set, requests that differ only by these parameters are served from the same cached response.
Specifies whether the origin host should be included in the cache key. When set to true, requests with different Host headers are cached separately.

If true, the request protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) is included in the cache key, so requests with different protocols are cached separately. If false, the protocol is not included, and HTTP/HTTPS requests for the same resource share a cache entry.
If true, requests with different query string values are cached separately. If false, all requests with the same path are cached together regardless of query string.
The names of cookies to include in the cache key. Only cookies with these exact names are included; other cookies are ignored.

The list of HTTP header names to include in the cache key. Specifies which request headers are used to form the cache key, so that requests with different values for these headers are cached separately.
A list of query parameter names to include in the cache key. Requests with these query parameters will have them considered part of the cache key determination.

The cache mode for the route action. Valid values are CACHE_ALL_STATIC (cache static content), FORCE_CACHE_ALL (cache all content regardless of headers), and USE_ORIGIN_HEADERS (respect origin cache headers).
Specifies the maximum amount of time (TTL) that cached responses are served to clients. The object uses the duration format with `seconds` and `nanos` fields representing the time period.
The nanosecond component of the client TTL duration, providing sub-second precision. Valid range is 0 to 999,999,999 nanoseconds.
The seconds component of the client TTL duration, represented as a string to accommodate large values.

The default amount of time that a cached response is stored by the cache, specified as a Duration object with a 'seconds' field (and optionally 'nanos'). This TTL applies when the response has no explicit Cache-Control headers.
The fractional second component of the default cache TTL, expressed in nanoseconds. Valid values range from 0 to 999,999,999 nanoseconds.
The seconds component of the default TTL (time-to-live) duration for cached responses in the path rule's cache policy. Despite being typed as a string, it represents an integer number of seconds.
The nanosecond component of the maximum time-to-live (TTL) duration. Specifies the fractional second part of the cache TTL, used together with the seconds field.
The seconds component of the max_ttl duration, specified as a 64-bit integer encoded as a string. This determines the maximum time (in seconds) that a cached response is considered fresh.
When true, enables negative caching for the path rule, which caches HTTP error responses (such as 404 or 502) for the specified path.
Specifies the negative caching settings for HTTP error responses. Each entry defines a response code and its time-to-live (TTL) for caching error responses.
The HTTP status code for which negative caching is enabled. For example, 404 or 500.
The non-negative fractional seconds in nanoseconds for the negative caching TTL. Valid values are from 0 to 999,999,999 nanoseconds.
Specifies the time-to-live (TTL) for the negative caching policy in seconds.

If set to true, enables request coalescing, which combines multiple requests for the same cacheable resource into a single request sent to the backend, reducing load. If false, disables this behavior.
The nanoseconds component of the serve-while-stale duration. Valid values range from 0 to 999,999,999.
The duration, in seconds, for which stale cached content is served while the origin is unavailable. This value is specified as a string.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.path_rules.route_action.co: The Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) policy for this route action, defining allowed origins, methods, headers, and other CORS settings.
Whether to allow credentials (cookies, authorization headers, etc.) to be sent with cross-origin requests. If true, the Access-Control-Allow-Credentials response header is set to 'true'.
Specifies the list of headers that the origin may include in CORS requests. This corresponds to the Access-Control-Allow-Headers header in the response.
Specifies the list of HTTP methods allowed for CORS requests, such as GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, or '*' to allow all methods.
Specifies a list of origin regexes that are allowed to make CORS requests. A request's Origin header must match one of these regexes for the CORS policy to permit the request.
Specifies the list of origins allowed to make cross-origin requests. Each origin is a string, such as 'https://example.com'.
If true, the CORS policy is disabled for this route and no CORS headers will be applied to responses.
Specifies the response headers that are exposed to the browser and can be accessed by client-side scripts, as part of the CORS policy for this path rule.
The maximum age, in seconds, that the browser should cache preflight request results, as defined by the Access-Control-Max-Age header. A value of -1 disables caching.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.path_rules.route_action.fa: Configuration for injecting faults into requests matched by this route action. This block allows specifying delay and abort behaviors to simulate failures, useful for testing service resilience.
Abort fault injection configuration. When specified, the policy aborts requests with a configured HTTP status code to simulate service failures.
The HTTP status code that will be returned to the client when the fault injection abort is triggered.
The percentage of requests that will be aborted. Must be a number between 0.0 and 100.0.
Configuration for injecting delay faults into requests. Specifies the fixed delay amount and the percentage of requests to which the delay is applied.

Specifies a fixed delay duration (in seconds and nanos) that is applied to a percentage of requests for fault injection. This object defines the amount of delay to inject before forwarding the request.
The nanosecond portion of the fixed delay duration. Valid values range from 0 to 999,999,999 inclusive.
The seconds component of the fixed delay. Accepts a string representation of an integer from 0 to 315576000000 inclusive.
The percentage of requests to which the delay is applied in the fault injection policy. A value of 10 means 10% of requests are delayed.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.path_rules.route_action.ma: Specifies the maximum duration for a stream to be active. The object contains 'seconds' and 'nanos' fields that together define the duration (for example, 30 seconds).
The fractional second component of the duration, measured in nanoseconds. Valid values range from 0 to 999,999,999.

The seconds component of the maximum stream duration. This is the whole-number part of the duration in seconds, specified as a decimal string (e.g., '10' for 10 seconds). Fractional seconds are handled by the associated 'nanos' field.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.path_rules.route_action.re: The request_mirror_policy block specifies a backend service to which requests are mirrored. This allows traffic shadowing, where a copy of the matched requests is sent to the specified backend service in addition to the original destination.
The backend service to which to mirror traffic. This can be specified as a name or a fully-qualified URL.
The percentage of requests (0-100) to mirror to the mirrored backend. For example, set to 50 to mirror half of the requests.
The retry policy for this route action, defining the conditions that trigger a retry and the maximum number of retry attempts.
The number of retries before the request is considered failed. This value must be a non-negative integer.
Specifies the timeout for each retry attempt. This is a Duration object with integer fields 'seconds' and 'nanos' that together determine the maximum time a single retry can take.
The nanoseconds component of the per-try timeout duration. Must be between 0 and 999,999,999 inclusive.
The whole seconds component of the per-try timeout duration, used to specify the timeout length.
Specifies one or more conditions when this retry policy applies. Valid values are: '5xx', 'gateway-error', 'connect-failure', 'refused-stream', 'reset', 'http-error', and 'internal'.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.path_rules.route_action.ti: Configures the timeout for the route action. This is a Duration object that specifies the maximum time allowed for the request to complete, typically containing 'seconds' and 'nanos' fields.

The fractional seconds component of the timeout duration, expressed in nanoseconds. This field, along with `seconds`, defines the total timeout period, with valid values ranging from 0 to 999,999,999.
The seconds component of the timeout duration. This is a string representation of an integer number of seconds, and must be non-negative.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.path_rules.route_action.ur: Specifies a URL rewrite action for requests matched by this path rule. Within it, you can set hostRewrite and pathPrefixRewrite to modify the host and path prefix before forwarding to the backend.
Specifies the new host header value to rewrite the incoming request's host header to before forwarding the request to the backend service.
The value to replace the path prefix of the request with before forwarding to the backend service. Must start with '/'. If empty, the original path is preserved.

The rewrite path template, which must have the same format as the path template in the path matcher's `path_template_match`. For example, with `path_template_match = "/v1/*/products/*"`, setting `path_template_rewrite = "/v2/*/products/*"` rewrites `/v1/books/products/123` to `/v2/books/products/123`.
The regex_rewrite block defines a regular expression pattern to match the request path and a substitution string to replace it, enabling regex-based URL path rewrites.
The regex pattern (RE2 syntax) that matches the path component of the request URL. The rewrite applies when the path matches this pattern.
The substitution string to replace the portion of the URL path matched by the regex. Backreferences like `\1` can be used to reference captured groups from the regex.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.path_rules.route_action.we: A list of weighted backend services to which traffic will be distributed. Each element specifies a backend service and a weight (0-1000) controlling the proportion of traffic routed to it.
The name or self_link of the backend service that this weighted backend service routes traffic to.
Configures the header action for this weighted backend service, specifying request and response headers to add or remove.
A list of headers to add to the request before it is forwarded to the backend service. Each header is defined by a `header_name` and `header_value`.
The name of the request header to add to requests sent to the weighted backend service.
The value of the header to be added to the request.
Whether to replace an existing header value with the specified value. If true, the header is replaced; if false, the header is added.
A list of HTTP request header names to remove from the request before it is forwarded to the backend service.
A list of response headers to add to the response before it is sent back to the client. Each object in the list defines a header name and value.
The name of the response header to add to the outbound response for the matched request. For example, 'X-Custom-Header'.
Specifies the value of the response header to add to the response for the associated weighted backend service. This value is used as the header value when the header is added.
If set to true, replaces the existing header with the same name; if false, appends this header value to any existing values.
List of header names to remove from the response before it is sent back to the client.
The weight of the backend service, determining the fraction of traffic it receives relative to other weighted backend services. Must be an integer between 0 and 1000.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.path_rules.service: A reference (URL) to the backend service that will receive requests matching this path rule. If routeAction is configured, advanced routing actions are applied before forwarding the request to this service.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.path_rules.url_redirect: Specifies a URL redirect for requests matching this path rule. When set, requests are redirected to the configured target instead of being sent to a backend service.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.path_rules.url_redirect.ho: The host that will be used in the redirect response instead of the one that was supplied in the request.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.path_rules.url_redirect.ht: If true, the redirect uses HTTPS protocol; otherwise, it uses HTTP protocol.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.path_rules.url_redirect.pa: The path to redirect requests to. When set, the request path is replaced with this value in the redirect response.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.path_rules.url_redirect.pr: The prefix that replaces the matched prefix in the original request path for this redirect.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.path_rules.url_redirect.re: Specifies the HTTP status code to use for the redirect. Allowed values are FOUND (302), MOVED_PERMANENTLY_DEFAULT (301), PERMANENT_REDIRECT (308), SEE_OTHER (303), and TEMPORARY_REDIRECT (307).
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.path_rules.url_redirect.st: Indicates whether the query string of the original URL is removed before redirecting. Set to true to strip the query, or false to preserve it.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules: A list of route rules that define how requests are matched and routed for this path matcher. Each rule includes match conditions and the corresponding action.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.custom_error_r: Specifies the custom error response policy for the route rule. When configured, this policy defines custom error responses that replace the default error responses for the rule.
A list of rules that define custom error responses for specific HTTP error codes. Each rule includes a set of response codes to match and a path to the custom error page.
A list of HTTP response codes that trigger this custom error response rule. May include specific codes (e.g., '404') or wildcard ranges (e.g., '4xx', '5xx').
The HTTP status code to use as the override for the original error response status code when this error response rule matches. This allows returning a custom status code for the error response.
The path to the custom error page on the backend service or bucket that handles the error response, used when a response code in matchResponseCodes is returned.
The full or partial URL of the backend service that will serve custom error responses for this route rule.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.description: An optional, human-readable description of this route rule.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.header_action: Configures the request and response headers to add or remove for the matched route.
A list of header name/value pairs to add to the request before it is forwarded to the backend. Each object contains `header_name` and `header_value` fields.
The name of the request header to add.
The value of the request header to add.
Indicates whether to replace the header if it already exists in the request. If true, the header value is replaced; if false, the header is added without overwriting existing values.
List of request header names to remove from the request before forwarding to the backend service.
A list of response headers to add for this route rule. Each object specifies a header name and value, which are added to the response to the client.
The name of the header to add to the response.
The value to assign to the response header being added. This, together with the corresponding header name, defines a header that will be added to the response for matching requests.

If true, replaces the value of the existing response header with the specified header value. If false, the header value is appended to the existing header value, potentially resulting in multiple headers with the same name.
A list of response header names to remove from the response before it is returned to the client.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.match_rules: Specifies a list of match rules that determine whether a request applies to this route rule. Each match rule can define path-based matching (e.g., prefix, exact, regex) and additional header or query parameter conditions.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.match_rules.fu: Specifies a full path that must exactly match the request path for the match rule to apply.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.match_rules.he: A list of header match criteria. Each element specifies a header name and a value (exact match or regular expression) to match against the request headers.
The exact value that the request header must match for this header match rule to apply.
The name of the HTTP header to match. For example, to match the `User-Agent` header, set this field to `User-Agent`.
When set to true, the header match condition is inverted. A request matches this rule if the header does NOT satisfy the specified header match criteria.
The prefix of the header value to match. Only one of exact_match, prefix_match, suffix_match, regex_match, or present_match can be set.
If set to true, the match is satisfied when the request header is present, regardless of its value.

Defines a range of integer values that a numeric header value must fall within for the header match to apply. The object contains rangeStart and rangeEnd fields specifying the inclusive lower and upper bounds.
The end of the range for the header value to match. Used together with range_start.
The start of the range (inclusive) to match against the header value. The header value must be a number within the specified range.
The regular expression (RE2 syntax) to match against the header value. Only one of exactMatch, regexMatch, prefixMatch, suffixMatch, or rangeMatch can be set.
Specifies a suffix match for the value of a request header. The header value must end with the given string for the match to succeed.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.match_rules.ig: Whether to ignore case when matching the URL path. When set to true, case differences are ignored; when false, matching is case-sensitive. Defaults to false.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.match_rules.me: A list of metadata filters that the request metadata (headers) must satisfy for the route rule match to apply. Each filter defines a matching criterion and a set of label name/value pairs to match against.
A list of label filters used to match request metadata. Each label filter defines a key-value pair that must match the request's metadata for the metadata_filters condition to be true.
The name (key) of the metadata filter label, used as the key in a key-value pair for request filtering.
The value part of a metadata filter label key-value pair. This is used to specify the value of the label that metadata must match for the filter to apply.
Specifies the match criteria for applying the metadata filters. MATCH_ALL requires all filter criteria to match, MATCH_ANY requires at least one to match, and NOT_SET indicates no criteria is set.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.match_rules.pa: The path template to match against the request path, using a template syntax with variables (e.g., '/foo/{bar}') for dynamic segment matching.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.match_rules.pr: Matches requests whose URL path begins with this string. For example, a prefix_match of '/foo' matches '/foo' and '/foo/bar'.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.match_rules.qu: Defines the query parameters that must be present and match in the request URL for the match rule to apply. Each object in the list specifies a query parameter name and a value or regular expression to match against.
The name of the query parameter to match.
Indicates whether the query parameter must be present for the match to succeed. Set to true to match when the parameter is present, and false to match when it is absent.

The regular expression to match the query parameter value against. If set, the query parameter value must satisfy this regex for the match rule to apply. Cannot be set together with value_match; exactly one of the two must be specified.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.match_rules.re: A regular expression (RE2) to match against the request path. When set, this match rule applies if the path matches the regex. It is mutually exclusive with full_path_match and prefix_match.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.priority: The priority of this route rule, used to determine the order in which rules are evaluated. Lower values have higher precedence; rules are matched in increasing priority order. This value must be unique within the path matcher.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.route_action.c: The list of request header names to consider for cache bypass. When a request contains any of these headers, the cache is bypassed and the request is sent to the origin server.

Configuration for the cache key used by the cache policy. It defines which request attributes (such as host, protocol, query string, headers, and cookies) are included in the cache key for this route rule.
A list of query parameters to exclude from the cache key. Requests that differ only in these parameters will share the same cached response.
If true, the HTTP host (host header) is included in the cache key. If false, the host is excluded. This affects cache key differentiation based on the requested host.
If true, HTTP and HTTPS requests are treated as distinct cache keys, meaning the protocol is included in the cache key.
If true, the query string is included in the cache key. If false, the query string is excluded, meaning all requests with different query strings share the same cache entry.
Specifies a list of cookie names to include in the cache key. If empty, no cookies are included in the cache key.
A list of HTTP header names to include in the cache key. If specified, each listed header is added as a component of the cache key; if empty, no custom headers are included.
The list of query parameters to include in the cache key. If specified, only these query parameters are considered when generating the cache key; other query parameters are ignored.

The cache mode for the cache policy. Valid values are: CACHE_ALL_STATIC (cache static content automatically), FORCE_CACHE_ALL (cache all content, ignoring origin cache headers), and USE_ORIGIN_HEADERS (respect the origin's cache-control headers).

Specifies the time-to-live (TTL) for the client-side cache. This is a Duration object with 'seconds' and 'nanos' fields that limits how long the client can cache a response before revalidating with the origin.
The nanosecond portion of the duration. For a client_ttl, this specifies the fractional seconds component, and must be an integer between 0 and 999,999,999 inclusive.
The number of seconds for the client TTL, represented as a string. This value specifies how long to keep requests cached.
Specifies the default time-to-live (TTL) for cached responses, used when the origin server does not provide an explicit TTL. Represented as a duration object.
The nanosecond component of the default TTL duration. Valid values are 0 to 999,999,999.
The maximum time-to-live for cached responses, specified as a duration object. This sets an upper bound on how long a response can be stored in the cache.
The nanoseconds component of the maximum TTL duration. Must be an integer from 0 to 999,999,999 inclusive.
The seconds component of the maximum time-to-live (TTL) duration. This is a string representation of an integer number of seconds.
Enables or disables negative caching, which allows the CDN to cache responses for error status codes (such as 404) according to the negative caching policy.
A list of negative caching policies for HTTP error status codes. Each entry specifies an HTTP status code (e.g., 404) and the TTL (in seconds) for caching that error response.
The HTTP status code (e.g., 404, 500) that triggers negative caching for responses with that status.
The time-to-live (TTL) for this negative caching entry, defining how long the cache should retain the negative response for the associated status code.
The nanoseconds component of the TTL duration. Must be a non-negative integer between 0 and 999,999,999.
The number of seconds in the TTL duration for the negative caching policy, specified as a string (e.g., '60' for 60 seconds).

Enables request coalescing, which combines concurrent requests for the same cached object into a single origin request. This reduces origin load when multiple clients request the same content simultaneously.
The nanosecond component of the duration, ranging from 0 to 999,999,999 inclusive.
The duration, in seconds, for which stale cached content may be served while the cache attempts to revalidate the origin resource.
The Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) policy for this route. This specifies how the backend responds to cross-origin requests, including allowed origins, methods, headers, and other CORS settings.
Specifies whether the response to the request can be exposed when the credentials flag is true.
The set of HTTP request headers that are allowed in a CORS request. This corresponds to the Access-Control-Allow-Headers header in a CORS response.
Specifies the list of HTTP methods that are allowed for cross-origin requests in the CORS policy. For example, GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, etc.

Specifies a list of regular expressions that match request origins allowed to make cross-origin requests. If an origin matches one of these expressions, it is included in the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header.
List of origins that are allowed to make cross-origin requests. Each origin is a string such as `http://example.com`. This is part of the CORS policy for route actions in a URL map path matcher.
When true, this CORS policy is disabled for the route, and other CORS settings are ignored.
Specifies the response headers that are exposed to the client as part of the CORS policy.
The maximum time in seconds that the client can cache the CORS preflight response. This value is sent in the Access-Control-Max-Age header.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.route_action.f: The fault injection policy for this route. It allows configuring how requests are aborted or delayed to test the behavior of the backend.

The abort fault injection action, which aborts a percentage of requests routed to the backend service by returning a configured HTTP status code. It contains the HTTP status code and the percentage of requests to abort.
The HTTP status code used to abort the request. Must be between 200 and 599 (inclusive). Defaults to 500.
The percentage of requests that will be aborted, between 0.0 and 100.0.
The delay fault injection configuration for the route action. It sets a fixed delay and percentage of requests to which the delay is applied.
A fixed delay duration to inject before forwarding the request. This object specifies the exact delay period, used to simulate latency in fault injection testing.
The fractional seconds component of the fixed delay duration, in nanoseconds. A value from 0 to 999,999,999 inclusive, used together with the seconds field to specify the total delay.
Specifies the number of seconds for the fixed delay applied in the fault injection policy.
The percentage of requests that will be subjected to the delay specified in the fixed_delay field. Must be a number between 0.0 and 100.0.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.route_action.m: Specifies the maximum duration for a stream. When the stream duration exceeds this limit, the connection is terminated. The duration is represented as a Duration object with `seconds` and `nanos` fields.

The fractional seconds component of the maximum stream duration, expressed in nanoseconds. Valid values are from 0 to 999,999,999, and are used in conjunction with the `seconds` field to define the total duration.
Span of time at a resolution of seconds. Must be from 0 to 315,576,000,000 inclusive.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.route_action.r: Defines the request mirroring policy for the route action. It configures a backend service to receive a copy of the requests for traffic analysis.
The backend service resource that will receive mirrored traffic. This is the target to which a copy of the original request is sent.
The percentage of requests that will be mirrored to the backend configured in the request mirroring policy. Must be a number between 0 and 100.
The retry policy for requests routed by this route rule. It specifies the conditions under which a request should be retried, the maximum number of retry attempts, and the timeout for each attempt.
The number of retry attempts to perform for a request before returning an error.
Specifies a timeout for each retry attempt. The value is a duration string, such as '30s'. If not set, the default per-try timeout is used.
The fractional part of the per-try timeout duration in nanoseconds. Valid values are from 0 to 999,999,999 inclusive.
A list of conditions that trigger a retry attempt. Each string represents a failure type (such as a connection error or a server error) that causes the request to be retried.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.route_action.t: Specifies the timeout for this route rule, expressed as a duration string ending in 's' (e.g., '30s'). If not set, the largest timeout among the associated backend services is used.
The nanosecond component of the timeout duration. Must be a non-negative integer less than 1,000,000,000.
The number of seconds in the timeout duration, as a string. For example, '30' represents a 30-second timeout.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.route_action.u: Configures the URL rewriting for this route rule. This block allows setting a new host header and/or a new path prefix before the request is forwarded.
Specifies the new host name to use in the request. If set, the Host header is rewritten to this value.
Before forwarding the request to the selected service, the matched portion of the request's path is replaced by this value.

Specifies a path template to which the URL path will be rewritten, allowing the use of variables extracted from the matching path template. For example, a match template like '/users/{id}' can be rewritten to '/profiles/{id}'.
The regex_rewrite block configures a regular expression pattern and a replacement string to rewrite the request path within the URL rewrite action.
The regular expression pattern that matches a portion of the URL path. This pattern is used together with the replacement string to perform the URL rewrite.
The string to substitute for the matched path pattern. It can include capture group references such as \1, \2, etc., referencing groups from the regex pattern in the parent regex_rewrite.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.route_action.w: This block defines a list of backend services with assigned weights to control the proportion of traffic each receives, enabling traffic splitting in the route action.
The name of the backend service that the traffic is routed to for the given weight. This should reference a backend service resource, either by name or URL.
Specifies modifications to request and response headers for this weighted backend service.
A list of request headers to be added to the request before forwarding to the backend service. Each object in the list contains a 'header_name' and a 'header_value'.
The name of the HTTP header to add to the request.
The value of the request header to add. This is the actual string that will be sent as the header value.
Determines whether to replace the value of the specified header (true) or append the value to an existing header (false).
Specifies a list of header names to remove from the request before forwarding to the backend service.
The name of the HTTP response header to add.
The value of the response header to add.
Indicates whether to replace an existing response header with the same name. If true, the header value is replaced; if false or unset, the header is added as an additional header.
The names of response headers to remove from the outgoing response before sending it to the client.
The weight of this backend service. Must be between 0 and 1000. Higher values receive more traffic.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.service: The name or URL of a BackendService or BackendBucket that defines where traffic matching this route rule should be sent. In a URL map, this service is used as the destination for requests that match the rule's match conditions.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.url_redirect: The url_redirect block configures the redirect behavior for this route rule. It defines where and how requests are redirected, including settings for host, path, prefix, response code, and query string handling.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.url_redirect.h: The host that will be used in the redirect response instead of the one that was supplied in the request. If empty, the host from the request is used.
If set to true, the request is redirected to the HTTPS version of the same URL.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.url_redirect.p: The path portion of the redirect URL. If empty, the path of the incoming request is used.
The prefix that replaces the matched prefix in the request path when a redirect is triggered.
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.url_redirect.r: Specifies the HTTP status code to return for the redirect. Allowed values are FOUND (302), MOVED_PERMANENTLY_DEFAULT (301), PERMANENT_REDIRECT (308), SEE_OTHER (303), and TEMPORARY_REDIRECT (307).
google_compute_url_map.path_matchers.route_rules.url_redirect.s: If set to true, any query portion of the original URL is removed before the redirect is performed. Defaults to false.
google_compute_url_map.tests.description: An optional description of this test.
google_compute_url_map.tests.expected_output_url: The expected URL that the host and path specified in the test case should resolve to, used to verify URL map routing behavior.
google_compute_url_map.tests.headers: A list of headers to include in the test request, where each header is an object with 'name' and 'value' fields.
google_compute_url_map.tests.headers.value: The value of the HTTP header to include in the test request.
google_compute_url_map.tests.host: The hostname used in the test request to match against the URL map's host rules.
google_compute_url_map.tests.path: The request path to test against the URL map's routing rules.
google_compute_url_map.tests.service: The backend service that the test expects the request to be routed to, validating the URL map's routing configuration.

google_compute_vpn_gateway.vpn_interfaces.interconnect_attachment: The Interconnect attachment to use for this VPN interface. This is applicable when using HA VPN over Cloud Interconnect.
google_compute_vpn_gateway.vpn_interfaces.ip_address: The external IP address assigned to this VPN gateway interface.

google_compute_vpn_tunnel.cipher_suite: The cryptographic suite (e.g., encryption and authentication algorithms) used for the VPN tunnel. This is a computed read-only field provided by the system.
google_compute_vpn_tunnel.cipher_suite.phase1: The phase1 object defines the IKE Phase 1 (ISAKMP SA) settings for the VPN tunnel's cipher suite, including the encryption, integrity, and DH group algorithms used during the initial key exchange.
google_compute_vpn_tunnel.cipher_suite.phase1.dh: List of Diffie-Hellman group identifiers used during IKE phase 1 negotiation for the VPN tunnel cipher suite.
google_compute_vpn_tunnel.cipher_suite.phase1.encryption: List of encryption algorithms used for IKE phase 1 negotiation. These algorithms define the encryption methods permitted during the initial IPsec/IKE key exchange.
google_compute_vpn_tunnel.cipher_suite.phase1.integrity: The list of integrity algorithms permitted for IKE phase 1 negotiation. Supported values include SHA1, SHA256, SHA384, and SHA512; if left empty, the default set of algorithms is used.
google_compute_vpn_tunnel.cipher_suite.phase1.prf: The list of allowed Pseudo-Random Function (PRF) algorithms for the IKE phase 1 proposal, used for key derivation during the IKE handshake.
google_compute_vpn_tunnel.cipher_suite.phase2: Settings for IPsec Phase 2 (IKE Quick Mode), including encryption and integrity algorithms, within the cipher suite for the VPN tunnel.
google_compute_vpn_tunnel.cipher_suite.phase2.encryption: A list of acceptable encryption algorithms for Phase 2 of the IKE negotiation.
google_compute_vpn_tunnel.cipher_suite.phase2.integrity: A list of integrity algorithms to be used for the IPsec phase 2 proposal in the VPN tunnel. The tunnel negotiates using one of the listed algorithms to ensure data integrity.
google_compute_vpn_tunnel.cipher_suite.phase2.pfs: Specifies the Diffie-Hellman groups allowed for Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS) during Phase 2 of the IKE negotiation.

google_compute_wire_group.wires.endpoints.interconnect: The URL of the Compute Engine interconnect used by this endpoint.
google_compute_wire_group.wires.wire_properties.bandwidth_allocati: Specifies the bandwidth allocation mode for the wire: either ALLOCATE_PER_WIRE (each wire gets its own bandwidth) or SHARED_WITH_WIRE_GROUP (bandwidth is shared among wires in the group).
google_compute_wire_group.wires.wire_properties.fault_response: Specifies the action taken when a fault is detected on the wire. Valid values are DISABLE_PORT (disables the port) or NONE (takes no action).

google_compute_zone_vm_extension_policie.instance_selectors.label_selector: Specifies the label-based criteria for selecting instances to apply the VM extension policy. This selector uses labels on instances to determine inclusion.
google_compute_zone_vm_extension_policie.instance_selectors.label_selector.inclus: A map of label keys to values that an instance must have for the selector to match. An instance is included if it has all specified labels with matching values.
